reallife_camera_enabled: Third-person camera (off: the game's own camera)
reallife_camera_pitch: Camera tilt in degrees (the starting tilt while mouse look is on)
reallife_camera_height: Height the camera looks at (tenths of a metre)
reallife_car_camera: Chase camera when driving (hold the look-behind key to look behind)
reallife_camera_follow: Swing behind you when mouse look is off (0 = off)
reallife_visuals_bloom: Bloom in % (costs performance, 0 = the game's own)
reallife_crash_consequences: Your own car crashes cost damages and can injure you
reallife_police: Police (patrol cars at accidents and crimes, officers on the street, traffic stops)
reallife_police_presence: Police presence: parked patrol cars, officers on the beat and at junctions (0 = none)
reallife_police_pursuit: Police chase you if you hit a car or a person and drive off
reallife_people: People at scenes and on the street (drivers, paramedics, officers on foot)
reallife_patrol_officers: Police officers walk the beat near you
reallife_patrol_frequency: Officers on the beat: how often
reallife_ragdolls: Ragdolls and pedestrian collisions (people you hit fall, and can be hurt or killed)
reallife_player_knockdown: Traffic can knock you down when you are on foot (needs ragdolls)
reallife_ped_incidents: Pedestrians struck by traffic nearby (needs ragdolls; uses the accident frequency)
reallife_phone_skin: Modern phone look (body, wallpaper, status bar)
reallife_phone_contacts: Extra phone contacts you can call (applies on next load)
reallife_event_sick: You have come down with a cold. You will get tired faster until you recover. Rest, or call the doctor.
reallife_event_ambulance: You are being taken to hospital by ambulance. Ambulance fee: {amount}.
reallife_event_car_towed: Your car was towed to a parking space near the hospital. Towing fee: {amount}.
reallife_event_car_towed_shop: There was no space near the hospital, so your car was towed to the repair shop at {address}. Towing fee: {amount}.
reallife_event_car_not_towed: Your car could not be towed. It is still where you crashed.
reallife_event_ambulance_failed: The ambulance could not reach you. Try again in a moment.
reallife_crash_liability: You hit another car. You paid {amount} in damages.
reallife_crash_stop_prompt: You hit another car. Stop here to exchange details, or it is a hit-and-run.
reallife_crash_stopped: You stopped and exchanged details. You paid {amount} in damages.
reallife_pursuit_start: You left the scene of a crash. Police are after you: pull over, or try to lose them.
reallife_pursuit_caught: Pulled over for hit-and-run. Damages and a fine cost you {amount}.
reallife_pursuit_escaped: You lost the police. For now.
reallife_pursuit_fine_later: A traffic camera caught your plate at that hit-and-run. Damages and fine: {amount}.
reallife_crash_injured: You are hurt in the crash: bruised and shaken, but you can carry on.
reallife_crash_severe: You are severely injured in the crash. An ambulance has been called.
reallife_test_ragdoll: Test: knock down the nearest pedestrian
reallife_accident_minor: Fender bender nearby. Two drivers are out of their cars over a dented bumper.
reallife_accident_single_minor: A car has come to grief nearby: it clipped the kerb and is stopped in the road with its hazards on.
reallife_accident_single_moderate: A car has crashed nearby with nobody else involved. It is badly damaged and an ambulance has been called.
reallife_accident_single_severe: Serious single-car crash nearby. The driver is hurt and emergency services are on their way.
reallife_accident_moderate: Traffic accident nearby. A car is badly damaged and an ambulance has been called.
reallife_accident_severe: Serious crash nearby. Emergency services are on their way.
reallife_accident_paramedics: Paramedics have arrived and are treating the people involved.
reallife_accident_police: Police are at the scene, taking statements and directing traffic.
reallife_accident_closed: Police have taped off the accident and closed that stretch of road. Keep out of the tape; traffic is being turned away or let past a few cars at a time.
reallife_chase_start: Hit-and-run: one driver took off when the police arrived. A patrol car is in pursuit.
reallife_chase_caught: Police have stopped the hit-and-run driver a few blocks away.
reallife_chase_escaped: The hit-and-run driver got away. Police have called off the chase.
reallife_accident_cleared_hitrun: The driver who was hit gave a statement and the road has been cleared.
reallife_accident_cleared_minor_1: The drivers swapped insurance details and went on their way.
reallife_accident_cleared_minor_2: After some shouting, both drivers drove off. Traffic is moving again.
reallife_accident_cleared_moderate_1: One driver was taken to hospital with minor injuries. The wreck has been towed.
reallife_accident_cleared_moderate_2: Paramedics treated a driver at the scene. The damaged car has been towed away.
reallife_accident_cleared_moderate_3: Nobody was seriously hurt. A tow truck has cleared the road.
reallife_accident_cleared_severe_1: The injured were rushed to hospital. The wrecks have been cleared and the road has reopened.
reallife_accident_cleared_severe_2: Emergency crews freed a trapped driver. All vehicles have been towed.
reallife_accident_cleared_severe_3: Everyone survived the crash, some with serious injuries. The road is open again.
reallife_accident_helped: You stopped to check on the drivers. Everyone is okay.
reallife_accident_helped_single: You stopped to check on the driver. Shaken, but okay.
reallife_accident_helped_severe: You stopped at the crash. Someone is hurt; help is on its way.
reallife_accident_cleared_single_minor_1: The driver changed a wheel, looked the car over and drove off.
reallife_accident_cleared_single_minor_2: The stranded car got going again and the road is clear.
reallife_accident_cleared_single_moderat: The driver was checked over by paramedics. The damaged car has been towed away.
Nobody else was involved. A tow truck has cleared the wreck.
reallife_accident_cleared_single_severe_: The driver was taken to hospital. The wreck has been cleared and the road has reopened.
Emergency crews got the driver out and away. The car has been towed.
reallife_crime_chase_start_1: Someone just bolted down the pavement nearby, with a police officer sprinting after them.
reallife_crime_chase_start_2: Shouts from down the street: an officer is chasing somebody on foot.
reallife_crime_chase_start_3: A foot chase nearby. Somebody is running hard, and a cop is right behind.
reallife_crime_chase_caught_1: The runner gave up, hands in the air. The officer led them away.
reallife_crime_chase_caught_2: Caught. The suspect was out of breath long before the officer was.
reallife_crime_chase_caught_3: The chase is over. One suspect in custody, and one very winded officer.
reallife_crime_chase_escaped_1: The runner got away. The officer is on the phone, describing a jacket.
reallife_crime_chase_escaped_2: Lost them. The officer stopped, hands on knees, and called it in.
reallife_crime_chase_escaped_3: Whoever that was, they were faster than the police. The officer has given up.
reallife_crime_chase_near: You flatten yourself against a wall as the chase goes past. Nobody even looks at you.
reallife_crime_question_start_1: A police officer has stopped someone on the pavement nearby and is asking questions.
reallife_crime_question_start_2: Nearby, an officer is having a long word with someone who would clearly rather be elsewhere.
reallife_crime_question_start_3: Police stop nearby. One officer, one pedestrian, and a great deal of hand-waving.
reallife_crime_question_released_1: The officer let them go with a warning. They left quickly.
reallife_crime_question_released_2: Whatever the story was, the officer bought it. They went their separate ways.
reallife_crime_question_released_3: Nothing to see: a few questions, a nod, and the pedestrian walked on.
reallife_crime_question_led_1: The answers weren't good enough. The officer walked them off down the street.
reallife_crime_question_led_2: The officer has heard enough and is taking them in for a longer conversation.
reallife_crime_question_near: You slow down to listen. The officer gives you a look, and you remember somewhere you need to be.
reallife_crime_disturbance_start_1: Two people are having a blazing row on the pavement nearby. Somebody has called the police.
reallife_crime_disturbance_start_2: Raised voices down the street: an argument is getting out of hand, and an officer is on the way.
reallife_crime_disturbance_start_3: A disturbance nearby. Two people, one parking space or one ex, and a lot of pointing.
reallife_crime_disturbance_end_1: An officer stepped in and sent the two of them off in opposite directions.
reallife_crime_disturbance_end_2: The row is over. Both parties have left, each certain that they won.
reallife_crime_disturbance_end_3: Calm again. After a word from the police, both of them walked away.
reallife_crime_disturbance_near: You step in and ask if everything is all right. It takes some of the heat out of it.
reallife_pedhit_knocked: You knocked a pedestrian off their feet. They are getting up, and they are furious.
reallife_pedhit_stop_prompt: You hit a pedestrian and they are not getting up. Stop here and wait, or it is a hit-and-run.
reallife_pedhit_scene: Someone has called it in. An ambulance and the police are on their way to the pedestrian you hit.
reallife_pedhit_stopped_injured: You stopped and stayed. The pedestrian is badly hurt but alive. It is being treated as an accident: a {amount} fine, and a rough day.
reallife_pedhit_stopped_dead: You stopped and stayed. The pedestrian did not survive. It is being treated as an accident: a {amount} fine. That will stay with you.
reallife_pedhit_fled_injured: You injured a pedestrian and left the scene. Your plate was reported: {amount} in fines.
reallife_pedhit_fled_dead: You killed a pedestrian and left the scene. Your plate was reported: {amount} in fines. That will stay with you.
reallife_pedhit_pursuit_start: You hit a pedestrian and drove off. That is a hit-and-run: police are after you. Pull over, or try to lose them.
reallife_pedhit_caught_injured: Pulled over for a hit-and-run that left a pedestrian injured. It cost you {amount}.
reallife_pedhit_caught_dead: Pulled over for a fatal hit-and-run. It cost you {amount}, and it will stay with you.
reallife_pedhit_cleared_injured: Paramedics have taken the injured pedestrian to hospital. The road is clear again.
reallife_pedhit_cleared_dead: The pedestrian did not survive. The ambulance has left and the road has reopened.
reallife_pedhit_helped: You went over to the pedestrian who was hit and stayed with them.
reallife_pedstruck_start_1: A car has hit a pedestrian nearby. Someone is lying in the road and an ambulance has been called.
reallife_pedstruck_start_2: Screeching brakes down the street: someone stepped out in front of a car. Emergency services are on their way.
reallife_pedstruck_start_3: Pedestrian struck by a car nearby. The driver has stopped and is calling for help.
reallife_player_hit_knocked: A car knocked you off your feet. Nothing broken, but you are shaken.
reallife_player_hit_injured: You were hit by a car. You are hurt, but you can carry on.
reallife_player_hit_severe: You were hit hard by a car and are badly injured. An ambulance has been called.
reallife_contact_911_desc: Report an accident, a crime or a fire, or call an ambulance
reallife_text_911_welcome: Emergency Services. Call to report an accident, a crime or a fire, or to ask for an ambulance.
reallife_911_dispatched: Thank you. A unit is on its way to the scene now.
reallife_911_nothing: We have no reports of anything in your area. Please keep this line free for emergencies.
reallife_911_ambulance_offer: We can send an ambulance to take you to hospital. The ambulance fee is {amount}, and the hospital will bill you separately. Shall I send it?
reallife_911_ambulance_sent: An ambulance is on its way. Put your phone away and stay where you are.
reallife_text_doctor_welcome: Dr. Patel's practice. If you're feeling unwell, call for a phone consultation.
reallife_doctor_healthy: You sound perfectly healthy to me. Call again if you start feeling unwell.
reallife_doctor_offer: That does not sound good. A phone consultation with a prescription is {amount}. Would you like that?
reallife_doctor_treated: I've sent the prescription to your pharmacy. You should feel better right away. Take care!
reallife_text_friend_welcome: Hey, it's Alex. Got a new number. Call me sometime!
reallife_friend_greeting: Hey, finally! I was starting to think you'd forgotten about me. Got a few minutes?
reallife_friend_bye: Ha, that was great. Don't be a stranger, okay? Talk soon!
reallife_friend_again: We literally just talked today! Call me tomorrow, I'll have new gossip by then.
reallife_text_mom_welcome: Hi sweetie, it's Mom. Call me when you can. Are you eating properly?
reallife_mom_greeting: Sweetheart! It's so good to hear your voice. Tell me everything. How is the big city treating you?
reallife_mom_bye: I'm so proud of you. Don't work too hard, and call your mother more often!
reallife_mom_bye_sick: You sound terrible! Go see a doctor and get some rest. I mean it. Love you.
reallife_mom_again: We already spoke today, sweetie! I love hearing from you, but go enjoy your evening.
reallife_ev_st01: A folded bill is stuck in a subway grate. You fish out {amount} with a pen and some patience.
reallife_ev_st02_b: Someone on the street says they lost their wallet and asks for $25 to get home.
reallife_ev_st02_y1: They thank you warmly. That felt good.
reallife_ev_st02_y2: They thank you, then you watch them tell the next person the same story. Oh well.
reallife_ev_st03: Someone bumped into you in the dark. Your wallet is {amount} lighter.
reallife_ev_st04: You twisted your ankle on the kerb. Ouch.
reallife_ev_st05_b: A street musician is playing something slow and lovely. The open case holds a few coins.
reallife_ev_st05_y1: He nods without missing a note. The tune follows you for three blocks.
reallife_ev_st06_b: There's a wallet lying by a fire hydrant. Cash inside, and an ID with an address a few blocks away.
reallife_ev_st06_y1: The owner is so relieved they press {amount} into your hand as a reward.
reallife_ev_st06_y2: The owner barely says thanks, and it was a long walk. You still know you did right.
reallife_ev_st06_n1: You pocket {amount}. It spends fine, but it doesn't feel great.
reallife_ev_st07: A stranger compliments your jacket out of nowhere. You stand a little taller.
reallife_ev_st08_h: Shell game on a cardboard box
reallife_ev_st08_b: A fast-talking man slides three cups around a box. 'Find the ball, double your money. Twenty bucks!'
reallife_ev_st08_y1: The ball was never under any cup. Of course it wasn't.
reallife_ev_st08_y2: You actually found it. He pays out {amount} through gritted teeth and packs up fast.
reallife_ev_st09: A pigeon scored a direct hit on your shoulder. Some say that's lucky. It doesn't feel lucky.
reallife_ev_st10_b: A family in matching ponchos, holding a paper map upside down, asks you the way to the ferry. It's a long explanation.
reallife_ev_st10_y1: You walk them two blocks. The kids wave until they're out of sight.
reallife_ev_st10_n1: You point 'that way'. They head off, confidently, in a third direction.
reallife_ev_st11: A film crew has the whole block closed. You take the long way around.
reallife_ev_st12: A new bakery is handing out free samples. You take a warm roll, and then another.
reallife_ev_st13_h: Got a minute for the garden?
reallife_ev_st13_b: A cheerful volunteer with a clipboard is raising money to replant the neighbourhood garden.
reallife_ev_st13_y1: They hand you a sticker of a tomato. You wear it all day.
reallife_ev_st14: You stepped in wet cement on the pavement. Rescuing the shoes cost {amount}.
reallife_ev_st15: The sunset lines up perfectly with the cross street. Half the block stops to look, and so do you.
reallife_ev_st16_b: A man is selling second-hand paperbacks off a blanket. One is a business memoir with a coffee ring on the cover.
reallife_ev_st16_y1: It's surprisingly good. You dog-ear three pages before lunch.
reallife_ev_st16_y2: It turns out to be a signed first printing. A collector pays you {amount} for it.
reallife_ev_st17: A cop writes you a {amount} ticket for jaywalking. Everyone else kept walking, naturally.
reallife_ev_st18: A man in a full chicken costume hands you a flyer for a wing place. You both pretend this is normal.
reallife_ev_st19_b: An older woman's shopping bag just split open. Oranges are rolling towards the gutter.
reallife_ev_st19_y1: She insists you take two oranges for your trouble. They're excellent.
reallife_ev_st19_n1: You sidestep an orange. It feels like the orange is judging you.
reallife_ev_st20: Someone followed you for a block and a half. You ducked into a lit doorway until they passed.
reallife_ev_st21: A parking meter spits out someone else's change as you walk by. {amount}, all in quarters.
reallife_ev_st22_b: A man at a stone chess table waves you over. 'Five-minute game, ten dollars. Winner takes twenty.'
reallife_ev_st22_y1: Checkmate in fourteen moves. He was being polite about it.
reallife_ev_st22_y2: He blunders his queen and laughs. You take {amount} and a handshake.
reallife_ev_st23: Scaffolding, a moving truck and a tour group. It takes five minutes to walk one block.
reallife_ev_st24: You find an empty bench in a patch of sun and sit for a minute. It helps.
reallife_ev_st25_b: A market researcher offers $15 if you'll taste two colas and say which one is better.
reallife_ev_st25_y1: They taste identical. You pick the left one with great confidence and collect {amount}.
reallife_ev_st26: Your shoelace snapped and a heel came loose on the same block. The cobbler charged {amount}.
reallife_ev_st27: A kid's lemonade stand is doing better numbers than some businesses you know. You admire the hustle.
reallife_ev_st28_b: A man opens his coat to reveal a row of watches. 'Genuine. Thirty bucks. Fell off a truck.'
reallife_ev_st28_y1: It stopped ticking before you reached the corner.
reallife_ev_st28_y2: It turns out to be real. A pawn shop gives you {amount} for it, no questions asked.
reallife_ev_st29: A delivery cyclist misses you by an inch and yells something. Your heart is still going.
reallife_ev_st30: Rush hour. The pavement moves like one large, annoyed animal, and you're part of it.
reallife_ev_st31: A stranger holds a door, you say thanks, they say 'you got it'. Tiny, but the city feels friendlier.
reallife_ev_st32_b: A stressed-looking guy says his battery died and he needs to call his sister for a ride.
reallife_ev_st32_y1: He makes a thirty-second call and thanks you like you saved his life.
reallife_ev_st32_y2: He fumbles it. The screen cracks on the pavement. He's very sorry. The repair is {amount}.
reallife_ev_st33_b: A street magician points straight at you. The crowd turns. There is no graceful way out.
reallife_ev_st33_y1: He pulls your own watch out of a lemon. The crowd goes wild. So do you, a bit.
reallife_ev_st33_y2: You were the punchline of every trick. The crowd loved it. You'll recover.
reallife_ev_st34_b: A pavement artist offers to draw your caricature for $20.
reallife_ev_st34_y1: It's oddly flattering. You look like a cartoon tycoon.
reallife_ev_st34_y2: He has given you an enormous chin. You do not have an enormous chin. Do you?
reallife_ev_wx01: You got soaked to the skin, and now your throat feels scratchy.
reallife_ev_wx02_b: A vendor with a bucket of umbrellas has appeared out of nowhere, as they do the second it rains.
reallife_ev_wx02_y1: Dry at last. Worth every cent.
reallife_ev_wx02_y2: It turns inside out at the first corner. You carry the wreck to a bin.
reallife_ev_wx02_n1: You arrive everywhere damp for the next hour.
reallife_ev_wx03: A bus hits a puddle at full speed. You were standing in exactly the wrong place.
reallife_ev_wx04: Rain is drumming on the windows and you're inside, dry. A small, smug pleasure.
reallife_ev_wx05: The wipers can barely keep up. You grip the wheel and squint at the tail lights ahead.
reallife_ev_wx06: You share an awning with a stranger while the worst of it passes. You both agree the forecast lied.
reallife_ev_wx07: The afternoon heat is bouncing off the pavement. You're wilting.
reallife_ev_wx08: Cool, clear morning air. The city almost smells clean. You feel sharp.
reallife_ev_wx09: You left a window open at home before the rain started. Drying out the rug cost {amount}.
reallife_ev_wx10: Your shoes are soaked through. Dry socks from a corner shop: {amount}.
reallife_ev_wx11: Warm night, open windows, music from three different flats. The street feels alive.
reallife_ev_wx12_b: A woman with a huge golf umbrella sees you getting drenched and offers to walk you to the corner.
reallife_ev_wx12_y1: You make small talk about the weather, because of course you do. It's nice.
reallife_ev_wx12_n1: You insist you're fine. You are not fine. You are wet.
reallife_ev_wx13: Rain on the roof and nowhere to be. You haven't felt this relaxed in days.
reallife_ev_wx14: A gust of wind takes your receipt, a stranger's hat and a whole newspaper down the avenue.
reallife_ev_wx15: The low sun is right in your eyes. You drive three blocks using one hand as a visor.
reallife_ev_wx16: The sunrise turns the tall buildings pink for about four minutes. You happened to look up.
reallife_ev_wx17_b: It's coming down hard out there. You could give it ten minutes, or just get on with your day.
reallife_ev_wx17_y1: It eases to a drizzle. Patience, rewarded.
reallife_ev_wx17_y2: It gets heavier. The sky is doing this on purpose.
reallife_ev_tr01: You hit a pothole the size of a bathtub. Realigning the wheel cost {amount}.
reallife_ev_tr02: Green lights all the way down the avenue. Every single one. You feel chosen.
reallife_ev_tr03: A double-parked truck, a cab cutting in, and somebody leaning on the horn. Deep breaths.
reallife_ev_tr04: A traffic camera flashed as you went through. That'll be {amount} in the post.
reallife_ev_tr05: You found {amount} in coins and crumpled bills wedged down the side of the seat.
reallife_ev_tr06: The streets are empty and the lights are timed. For once, driving in this city is a pleasure.
reallife_ev_tr07: A cab cuts you off, and the driver gestures like it was your fault.
reallife_ev_tr08: A warning light came on. It was only washer fluid, but the garage still charged {amount} to look.
reallife_ev_tr09: The radio plays a song you loved at seventeen. You know every word. Windows up, thankfully.
reallife_ev_tr10: A parking ticket was tucked under your wiper: {amount}, for being four inches too close to a hydrant.
reallife_ev_tr11: Someone dinged your car door and left without a note. Touch-up paint: {amount}.
reallife_ev_tr12: Somebody left a note on your windscreen. It just says 'nice car'. That's the whole note.
reallife_ev_tr13_b: A shoeshine man with a folding chair calls out: 'Sit down, rest your feet. Ten bucks and you'll see your face in them.'
reallife_ev_tr13_y1: Two minutes off your feet and shoes like mirrors. You walk away feeling expensive.
reallife_ev_tr14: The train sat between stations for twenty minutes this morning. 'We are being held momentarily,' the speaker lied.
reallife_ev_tr15: A transit card on the ground still has credit on it. The booth clerk refunds you {amount} for it.
reallife_ev_tr16_b: A hatchback has died at the junction. The driver is steering through the window and looking around for help.
reallife_ev_tr16_y1: Three strangers and you roll it to the kerb. High fives all round.
reallife_ev_tr16_y2: You roll it to the kerb, and the driver insists you take {amount} for the help.
reallife_ev_tr17: A flat tyre, and the spare was flat too. Roadside help and a new tyre: {amount}.
reallife_ev_tr18: A street fair has closed four blocks. The detour takes you past places you've never seen.
reallife_ev_tr19: The bus pulled away just as you reached the stop. The driver definitely saw you.
reallife_ev_tr20_b: A teenager with a bucket and a squeegee offers to wash your car where it's parked. Fifteen dollars.
reallife_ev_tr20_y1: It hasn't been this shiny since you got it.
reallife_ev_tr20_y2: He washed the wrong car. A very confused stranger now owns a spotless saloon.
reallife_ev_tr21: Bridge traffic. You moved eleven car lengths in a quarter of an hour.
reallife_ev_tr22: You let a delivery van merge. The driver gives you the full grateful wave. Karma, banked.
reallife_ev_tr23: Your registration sticker was about to expire. Renewing at the last minute cost {amount}.
reallife_ev_tr24_b: A driver with a dead battery flags you down near your parked car and asks for a jump start.
reallife_ev_tr24_y1: Their engine coughs to life. They honk a thank-you all the way down the block.
reallife_ev_tr24_y2: It starts first try. They push {amount} into your hand and won't take it back.
reallife_ev_hm01: The upstairs neighbour took up tap dancing last night. You're running on four hours of sleep.
reallife_ev_hm02: The kitchen tap at home started spraying sideways. The plumber charged {amount} for ten minutes' work.
reallife_ev_hm03_b: Your neighbour is away for a few days and asks if you'd water her plants. There are a lot of plants.
reallife_ev_hm03_y1: Twenty-two plants. You counted. She'll be thrilled.
reallife_ev_hm03_y2: She comes back with a thank-you card and {amount} tucked inside.
reallife_ev_hm03_n1: She finds someone else. The ferns will remember this.
reallife_ev_hm04: The neighbour across the hall made too much lasagne and saved you a plate. Still warm.
reallife_ev_hm05: You locked yourself out of your place. The locksmith took ninety seconds and {amount}.
reallife_ev_hm06: Your building's hot water is out until further notice. The notice is handwritten and unsigned.
reallife_ev_hm07_b: A parcel for someone two floors up was left at your door. It's heavy.
reallife_ev_hm07_y1: It's a new neighbour. You get a handshake and an open invitation for coffee.
reallife_ev_hm08: Your smoke detector started chirping at 03:00. New batteries and a step stool: {amount}.
reallife_ev_hm09: You found {amount} in the pocket of a coat you haven't worn since last year.
reallife_ev_hm10: The radiator at home has started clanking like there's a small blacksmith inside. It does this all night.
reallife_ev_hm11_b: Your neighbours are throwing a loud party tonight. One of them messages the whole floor: 'Come by!'
reallife_ev_hm11_n: Ask them to keep it down
reallife_ev_hm11_y1: You stay an hour, eat a lot of dip and meet a man who sells boats.
reallife_ev_hm11_n1: They turn it down. For about nine minutes.
reallife_ev_hm11_n2: They apologise and actually keep it down. Miracles happen.
