reallife_ev_lk11: You confidently waved back at someone who was waving at the person behind you.
reallife_ev_lk12: You dropped your coffee, and your sandwich landed in it. Lunch, take two: {amount}.
reallife_ev_lk13_b: A carnival-style barker on the corner: 'I guess your age within two years, or you get ten dollars!'
reallife_ev_lk13_y1: He's off by six years, in the flattering direction. You take {amount} and the compliment.
reallife_ev_lk13_y2: He nails it. Exactly. It's a little unsettling.
reallife_ev_lk14: The vending machine dropped two snacks instead of one. You look around. Nobody saw.
reallife_ev_lk15: It's the middle of the night and the city is still humming. Somewhere, someone is making bagels.
reallife_ev_lk16: A penny on the pavement, heads up. You pick it up, because rules are rules.
reallife_ev_lk17: Your shopping bag split at the worst possible moment. Eggs were involved. Replacing it all: {amount}.
reallife_ev_lk18: You overhear a child explain, very seriously, that pigeons are 'government ducks'.
reallife_ev_lk19_b: A shop is selling unclaimed suitcases, sealed, $25 each. 'No peeking, no refunds.'
reallife_ev_lk19_y1: Eleven identical grey t-shirts and a single flipper.
reallife_ev_lk19_y2: A decent camera, wrapped in a towel. You sell it on for {amount}.
reallife_ev_lk19_y3: A beautiful wool coat that fits you perfectly. Somebody's loss.
reallife_ev_tc01: Your phone screen cracked. The repair cost {amount}.
reallife_ev_tc02: Your phone updated itself overnight and moved every single button.
reallife_ev_tc03: Your phone battery hit 1% at the exact moment you needed the map.
reallife_ev_tc04_b: Your phone refuses to take another photo until you delete things or pay $10 for more storage.
reallife_ev_tc04_y1: Problem solved, for now. The four hundred photos of receipts live on.
reallife_ev_tc04_n1: You scroll through two years of photos to delete twelve. Worth it for the memories.
reallife_ev_tc05: You got added to a group chat of forty strangers planning a surprise party. You stay for the drama.
reallife_ev_tc06: Your charger cable frayed down to the wire. A replacement at kiosk prices: {amount}.
reallife_ev_tc07: Autocorrect changed 'regards' to 'regrets' in an email to your landlord. It's already sent.
reallife_ev_tc08_b: An email says you've won a $100 gift card. All you have to do is click the link and 'confirm your details'.
reallife_ev_tc08_y1: It was phishing. You cancel the card, but not before {amount} goes missing.
reallife_ev_tc08_y2: Unbelievably, it's real. A shop you once did a survey for sends you {amount}.
reallife_ev_tc08_n1: Deleted. You feel wise and slightly smug.
reallife_ev_tc09: The wifi is fast, the phone is charged and nothing needs updating. Savour it.
reallife_ev_tc10: Coffee met laptop. The laptop lost. Keyboard replacement: {amount}.
reallife_ev_tc11: You spent ten minutes looking for your phone, using its torch to look.
reallife_ev_tc12: The password you've used for years is suddenly 'incorrect'. Three resets later, you're back in.
reallife_ev_tc13_b: A pair of expensive wireless earbuds is sitting on a bench. The case has a name sticker and a cafe loyalty card tucked in it.
reallife_ev_tc13_y: Hand them in at the cafe
reallife_ev_tc13_y1: The barista knows the owner. You get a free coffee for your honesty.
reallife_ev_tc13_y2: The owner happens to walk in, frantic. You're handed {amount} and a very sincere thank-you.
reallife_ev_tc14: You replied-all. To your whole building's mailing list. About the lobby smell.
reallife_ev_tc15: Every screen in the place froze for a second. Someone, somewhere, tripped over a cable.
reallife_ev_tc16: Your headphones died mid-song, on one side only. A new pair: {amount}.
reallife_ev_tc17_b: Your phone wants to install an update right now. 'This may take a few minutes.'
reallife_ev_tc17_y1: Forty minutes of a progress bar. Everything looks exactly the same afterwards.
reallife_ev_tc17_y2: Done in two minutes, and the battery seems better. A rare win.
reallife_ev_tc17_n1: It will ask again in an hour. And again. Forever.
reallife_ev_pt01_b: A small, scruffy dog trailing a lead trots up to you and sits down like you had an appointment.
reallife_ev_pt01_y1: The owner sprints over in tears and insists on a {amount} reward.
reallife_ev_pt01_y2: The owner lives a block away. The dog acts like it barely knows you now.
reallife_ev_pt01_n1: It gives you a long look and trots off. You think about that look for a while.
reallife_ev_pt02: A very fluffy dog decides you're its favourite person on the block. The owner says he never does that.
reallife_ev_pt03: A cat is asleep in the window, in the one patch of light. It opens one eye at you and closes it again.
reallife_ev_pt04: A squirrel stole a whole bagel off a bench and stared you down while doing it.
reallife_ev_pt05_b: A neighbour is desperate: can you feed her cat tonight? She'll pay $25. The cat is 'spirited'.
reallife_ev_pt05_y1: The cat ignores you completely. Easiest {amount} you ever made.
reallife_ev_pt05_y2: You earned that {amount}. The scratches on your hand should heal in a week or so.
reallife_ev_pt06: A dog on a long lead wrapped itself twice around your legs. You very nearly went down.
reallife_ev_pt07: A dog walker goes by with nine dogs in perfect formation. Best-run operation you've seen all week.
reallife_ev_pt08: A pigeon has been walking beside you for half a block, like it's got somewhere to be too.
reallife_ev_pt09_b: An animal shelter has set up on the pavement with a pen full of puppies and a donation jar.
reallife_ev_pt09_y1: You get ten minutes of puppy time and a volunteer's eternal gratitude.
reallife_ev_pt09_n1: You pet a puppy for free. It was still an excellent decision.
reallife_ev_pt10: Birds started singing outside the window at 04:00 and did not stop.
reallife_ev_pt11: A dog in a tiny yellow raincoat splashes past. Briefly, the rain doesn't seem so bad.
reallife_ev_pt12: A goose is standing in the middle of the road. Traffic waits. The goose is in no hurry.
reallife_ev_pt13_b: A green parrot sits on a railing, saying 'hello' to everyone. There's a 'LOST PARROT' poster on the lamp post behind it.
reallife_ev_pt13_y1: The owner arrives in slippers, weeping. You get {amount}, and the parrot calls you 'Kevin'.
reallife_ev_pt13_y2: By the time the owner arrives, the parrot has moved one tree over. They're grateful anyway.
reallife_ev_pt13_n1: 'Hello,' you say. 'Hello,' says the parrot. A good chat.
reallife_ev_wk01: Monday morning. The whole city seems to be on its second coffee and first complaint.
reallife_ev_wk02: Friday evening. You can feel the entire city exhale.
reallife_ev_wk03: Sunday morning. The streets are quiet, the light is soft and nobody is honking yet.
reallife_ev_wk04_b: The avenue is closed for a street fair: grilled corn, tube socks, a band playing covers. $12 gets you fed.
reallife_ev_wk04_y1: Corn, a lemonade and a tube-sock three-pack you didn't know you needed.
reallife_ev_wk04_n1: You detour around six blocks of funnel cake smell. It follows you.
reallife_ev_wk05: The bars are letting out. You weave past a hen party and a man singing to a postbox.
reallife_ev_wk06: Lunch hour. Every bench, step and ledge in the neighbourhood has someone eating a salad on it.
reallife_ev_wk07: The Sunday evening feeling arrives right on schedule. Tomorrow has a lot of week in it.
reallife_ev_wk08_b: A small museum you keep walking past has free entry this afternoon.
reallife_ev_wk08_y1: An hour among old maps of the city. You find your own street, back when it was a farm.
reallife_ev_wk08_y2: The whole exhibit is chairs. Just chairs. You're not allowed to sit on any of them.
reallife_ev_wk09: Everyone's heading home at once. The crossings look like the start of a marathon.
reallife_ev_wk10: Saturday errands. Half the neighbourhood is carrying laundry or a plant.
reallife_ev_wk11: The clock outside the bank has been stuck at 3:40 for as long as you've lived here. Today it's right. Unsettling.
reallife_ev_wk12_b: A family is selling off half their flat on the front steps. There's a decent desk lamp for $15.
reallife_ev_wk12_y1: It works, it's handsome, and it came with a free story about their grandfather.
reallife_ev_wk12_y2: A vintage dealer spots it under your arm and offers {amount} on the spot. Sold.
reallife_ev_wk13: The city before seven belongs to bakers, joggers and delivery trucks. And today, you.
reallife_ev_wk14: You gave your order at the deli too slowly and got sighed at. A New York rite of passage.
reallife_ev_wk15: You told a cab driver about a shortcut and he said 'huh, good call'. You've lived here a while now.
reallife_ev_wk16: You stepped around a cellar hatch in the pavement without even looking. Your feet know this city now.
reallife_ev_wk17_b: A street has been closed off for a block party. Someone's uncle is running the grill, and he's waving you over.
reallife_ev_wk17_y1: A burger, a folding chair and three neighbours you'd never spoken to. A good night.
reallife_character_high_detail: High-detail player character (uses the game's own detailed model in the city)
reallife_character_hair: Fuller hair and beards on detailed characters
reallife_character_lighting: Softer lighting in character creation and shop previews
reallife_looks_header: Real Life Overhaul: Your character's hair and wardrobe
reallife_character_new_looks: New looks: the mod's clothes and shoes, and a hair-coloured scalp under your hair so that it does not look thin from a distance
reallife_crime_enabled: Crime near you (street crime, thieves in shops, other drivers pulled over)
reallife_crime_against_player: Crimes against you (pickpockets, muggers, break-ins, scam calls; all capped)
reallife_player_offences: Police stop you for red lights, speeding and reckless driving, and warn or fine you for jaywalking
reallife_test_crime_traffic: Test: a traffic offence by another driver
reallife_test_crime_shop: Test: a crime in a shop (stand inside a shop)
reallife_test_crime_player: Test: a crime against you (on foot, outdoors, carrying at least $60)
reallife_test_crime_offscreen: Test: break-in, car broken into, scam call (one per press, in turn)
reallife_crime_none_shop: Test not started: stand inside an open shop with shelves (your own, or one with customers in it).
reallife_crime_none_breakin: Test not started: a break-in needs a shop of your own that sells from shelves, and you must not be standing in it.
reallife_crime_none_car: Test not started: a car break-in needs a car of your own parked on the street, more than 60 m from you.
reallife_crime_none_scam: Test not started: a scam call needs every prompt closed and at least $100 on you.
reallife_crime_report_thanks: The police made an arrest thanks to your call.
reallife_911_report_theft_store: Report a theft in my shop
reallife_911_dispatched_crime: Understood. Officers are on their way. Stay where you are and don't put yourself in danger.
reallife_911_wasted_fine: We have nothing at your location, and you have already been warned twice today. Wasting police time: a {amount} fine has been issued.
reallife_crime_wasted_fine: Fined {amount} for wasting police time with 911 calls about nothing.
reallife_crime_chase_tripped_1: The runner caught a kerb and went sprawling. The officer was on them before they could get up.
reallife_crime_chase_tripped_2: It ended the undignified way: a stumble, a faceplant, and handcuffs.
reallife_crime_question_bolted_1: Mid-sentence, they bolted. The officer gave chase for half a block and gave up.
reallife_crime_question_bolted_2: The questions got awkward, so they ran. The officer is on the radio with a description.
reallife_crime_disturbance_fizzled_1: The shouting burned itself out. Both of them stalked off without a backward glance.
reallife_crime_disturbance_fizzled_2: Nobody came, nobody won, and eventually they both just left.
reallife_crime_disturbance_arrest_1: One of them shoved the officer. That one is now leaving in handcuffs.
reallife_crime_disturbance_arrest_2: The officer had heard enough from one of them in particular, and took them in.
reallife_crime_snatch_start_1: Someone is hovering a little too close behind a pedestrian who is busy with their phone.
reallife_crime_snatch_start_2: Nearby, a pedestrian is texting and hasn't noticed who has just fallen into step behind them.
reallife_crime_snatch_start_3: You notice somebody drifting through the crowd nearby, watching bags and pockets instead of where they're going.
reallife_crime_snatch_x_1: "Hey, HEY, that's my bag!" A thief is sprinting away down the pavement.
reallife_crime_snatch_x_2: A shout nearby: somebody just had their phone snatched right out of their hand.
reallife_crime_snatch_x_3: "Stop, thief!" Somebody is running hard with a wallet that isn't theirs.
reallife_crime_snatch_escaped_1: The thief vanished round a corner. The victim is on the phone, cancelling cards.
reallife_crime_snatch_escaped_2: Gone. Whoever took it knew these streets better than anyone chasing them.
reallife_crime_snatch_escaped_3: The thief got clean away. One more police report that nobody will ever read.
reallife_crime_snatch_victim_1: The victim ran the thief down themselves and got their things back after a short, undignified tug of war.
reallife_crime_snatch_victim_2: Never rob a runner. The victim caught up, took it back, and the thief slunk away.
reallife_crime_snatch_bystander_1: A passer-by stuck out an arm and the thief went down hard. The police took it from there.
reallife_crime_snatch_bystander_2: The thief ran straight into the wrong bystander. They were still on the ground when the officer arrived.
reallife_crime_snatch_officer_1: An officer round the corner heard the shouting. The thief made it about forty metres.
reallife_crime_snatch_officer_2: Bad luck for the thief: a cop was close by. Caught, cuffed, and the bag returned.
reallife_crime_snatch_false_1: False alarm. They were only tapping a stranger on the shoulder to hand back a dropped wallet.
reallife_crime_snatch_false_2: Not a thief after all: the pedestrian had dropped their keys, and somebody was returning them.
reallife_crime_mugging_start_1: Down the street, one person has their hands up and another is standing far too close to them.
reallife_crime_mugging_start_2: Something is wrong nearby: a pedestrian is backed against a wall, emptying their pockets.
reallife_crime_mugging_start_3: A mugging, right there on the pavement nearby. Nobody else seems to have noticed.
reallife_crime_mugging_near_1: The mugger saw you coming and ran. The victim is shaking, but still has their wallet.
reallife_crime_mugging_near_2: One look at a witness walking straight at them, and the mugger bolted empty-handed.
reallife_crime_mugging_robbed_1: The mugger got what they wanted and ran. The victim is on the phone to the police.
reallife_crime_mugging_robbed_2: It was over in seconds. A wallet gone, a thief gone, and one very shaken pedestrian.
reallife_crime_mugging_robbed_3: The mugger disappeared into the side streets with a phone and a watch.
reallife_crime_mugging_fought_1: The victim swung first. The mugger hit the pavement, scrambled up and ran.
reallife_crime_mugging_fought_2: Wrong victim. One punch later the mugger was on the ground reconsidering their career.
reallife_crime_mugging_interrupted_1: An officer came round the corner at exactly the right moment. The mugger is in custody.
reallife_crime_mugging_interrupted_2: The mugger ran straight from the victim into a foot chase, and lost it.
reallife_crime_mugging_lost_1: An officer arrived and gave chase, but the mugger was gone into the alleys.
reallife_crime_mugging_lost_2: The police came quickly. The mugger left quicker.
reallife_crime_assault_start_1: Two people nearby are squaring up to each other, and it has gone well past words.
reallife_crime_assault_start_2: An argument down the street is getting physical: chests out, fingers jabbing.
reallife_crime_assault_start_3: Raised voices nearby, and the kind of shoving that only ends one way.
reallife_crime_assault_x_1: A punch was thrown. Somebody is on the ground.
reallife_crime_assault_x_2: That was a fist. One of them just went down.
reallife_crime_assault_arrested_1: An officer arrived to find one on the floor and one standing over them. Easy arrest.
reallife_crime_assault_arrested_2: The one who threw the punch is leaving with the police. The other is going to have a black eye.
reallife_crime_assault_fled_1: The one who threw the punch ran before anyone could stop them. The other is calling it in.
reallife_crime_assault_fled_2: One punch, then a sprint. The victim picked themselves up and got their phone out.
reallife_crime_assault_apart_1: A passer-by got between them and talked the pair of them down. Braver than most.
reallife_crime_assault_apart_2: Somebody stepped in and pulled them apart. Both walked off muttering.
reallife_crime_assault_walked_1: They glared at each other for a while and left it at that. No police, no winner.
reallife_crime_assault_walked_2: The fight ended as suddenly as it began. Both of them walked away, one a bit unsteadily.
reallife_crime_graffiti_start_1: Somebody nearby is busy with a spray can and a wall that doesn't belong to them.
reallife_crime_graffiti_start_2: You can hear the rattle of a spray can from down the street.
reallife_crime_graffiti_start_3: A tagger is at work on a wall nearby, in broad view of everyone.
reallife_crime_graffiti_near: You get a look at the artwork. It's a name, mostly. The artist gives you a wary glance.
reallife_crime_graffiti_ran_1: The tagger spotted the officer first and was gone, leaving half a signature behind.
reallife_crime_graffiti_ran_2: One shout from a cop and the tagger was over a fence. The wall keeps its new decoration.
reallife_crime_graffiti_caught_1: Caught red-handed. And blue-handed, and silver-handed. The officer walked the tagger off.
reallife_crime_graffiti_caught_2: The tagger ran, but spray cans rattle. The officer caught up within a block.
reallife_crime_graffiti_told_1: A neighbour came out and gave the tagger a dressing-down that could be heard a block away. They left.
reallife_crime_graffiti_told_2: The building's super turned up shouting. The tagger packed up and slunk off.
reallife_crime_graffiti_cleared_1: An officer came to look. It turns out the landlord commissioned the mural. Everybody relaxed.
reallife_crime_graffiti_cleared_2: False alarm: the artist had a permit, and showed it to the officer with some satisfaction.
reallife_crime_graffiti_alone_1: The tagger finished, stepped back to admire the work, and strolled away. Nobody stopped them.
reallife_crime_graffiti_alone_2: Signature complete. The tagger pocketed the can and vanished.
reallife_crime_breakin_start_1: Someone nearby is working on the door of a parked car, and they don't look like they own it.
reallife_crime_breakin_start_2: A figure is crouched at a parked car's window down the street, glancing over their shoulder.
reallife_crime_breakin_start_3: You notice somebody trying car door handles along the kerb nearby, one after another.
reallife_crime_breakin_near: They hear your footsteps and freeze, one hand still on the door.
reallife_crime_breakin_ran_1: The thief saw the officer coming and ran, leaving the car door scratched but shut.
reallife_crime_breakin_ran_2: A cop turned the corner and the would-be car thief was gone in a heartbeat.
reallife_crime_breakin_caught_1: The officer caught them with a screwdriver in one hand and a car stereo in the other.
reallife_crime_breakin_caught_2: Run down within a block. The officer walked them back past the car they'd been breaking into.
reallife_crime_breakin_owner_1: The car's owner came out shouting. The thief dropped everything and ran.
reallife_crime_breakin_owner_2: "That's MY car!" The thief didn't stay to discuss it.
reallife_crime_breakin_cleared_1: An officer checked. It's their own car: keys locked inside, and a very long day.
reallife_crime_breakin_cleared_2: Not a thief: just someone who locked their keys in the car. The officer helped.
reallife_crime_breakin_alone_1: The thief got the door open, took what they wanted and walked off. Somebody is in for a bad surprise.
reallife_crime_breakin_alone_2: Nobody stopped them. A glovebox emptied, a door left ajar, and they were gone.
reallife_crime_drunk_start_1: Somebody nearby is very drunk, very loud, and arguing with a lamp post.
reallife_crime_drunk_start_2: A drunk is weaving along the pavement nearby, singing to nobody in particular.
reallife_crime_drunk_start_3: There's shouting down the street: one person, no audience, a great deal to say.
reallife_crime_drunk_near: The drunk tells you that you're their best friend, and then that you owe them twenty dollars.
reallife_crime_drunk_home_1: An officer had a quiet word and pointed the drunk towards home. They went, mostly in a straight line.
reallife_crime_drunk_home_2: The police sent them home to sleep it off. No harm done.
reallife_crime_drunk_arrested_1: The drunk took a swing at the officer. They'll be sleeping it off in a cell.
reallife_crime_drunk_arrested_2: Drunk and disorderly: the officer ran out of patience and took them in.
reallife_crime_drunk_friend_1: A friend turned up, apologised to everyone within earshot, and steered them home.
reallife_crime_drunk_friend_2: Somebody who knows them arrived and led them away by the elbow, still singing.
reallife_crime_drunk_fell_1: The drunk went over like a felled tree, lay there a moment, got up and wandered off.
reallife_crime_drunk_fell_2: Gravity won. They picked themselves up, dusted off nothing in particular and staggered on.
reallife_crime_drunk_alone_1: They ran out of things to shout and wandered off into the city.
reallife_crime_drunk_alone_2: The performance ended without applause. The drunk drifted away.
reallife_crime_vendor_start_1: Someone has set up an unlicensed stall on the pavement nearby: handbags, watches, no questions.
reallife_crime_vendor_start_2: A street vendor nearby is selling designer sunglasses at prices that explain themselves.
reallife_crime_vendor_near: "Rolex, my friend? Very real." You keep walking.
reallife_crime_vendor_moved_1: An officer told the vendor to pack up. Everything was folded into a blanket in four seconds flat.
reallife_crime_vendor_moved_2: Moved on by the police. The stall will be back by tomorrow, two blocks over.
reallife_crime_vendor_ticket_1: The officer wrote the vendor a ticket for trading without a licence. The vendor argued the whole time.
reallife_crime_vendor_ticket_2: No permit, so a fine. The vendor took it with the weariness of long practice.
reallife_crime_vendor_ran_1: The vendor saw the uniform, grabbed the corners of the blanket and ran with the whole shop.
reallife_crime_vendor_ran_2: One glimpse of a cop and the entire stall was gone down the street at a sprint.
reallife_crime_vendor_alone_1: The vendor sold a few watches, checked both ways, and moved on by themselves.
reallife_crime_panhandler_start_1: A panhandler nearby isn't taking no for an answer, and people are crossing the street to avoid them.
reallife_crime_panhandler_start_2: Somebody down the street is following pedestrians and demanding change, loudly.
reallife_crime_panhandler_near: They block your way with a hand out. You step around them.
reallife_crime_panhandler_moved_1: An officer moved the panhandler along, firmly but without fuss.
reallife_crime_panhandler_moved_2: The police had a word. The panhandler shrugged and shuffled off.
reallife_crime_panhandler_arrested_1: The panhandler grabbed the officer's arm. That was a mistake; they've been taken in.
reallife_crime_panhandler_told_1: A passer-by lost their temper and told the panhandler exactly what they thought. It worked.
reallife_crime_panhandler_told_2: Somebody finally snapped at them. The panhandler backed off and moved on.
reallife_crime_panhandler_alone_1: Business was slow. The panhandler gave up on this block and went to try another.
reallife_crime_panhandler_alone_2: After a while they simply wandered off.
reallife_crime_fare_start_1: A transit officer has stopped someone nearby who jumped a turnstile and didn't run fast enough.
reallife_crime_fare_start_2: Nearby, an officer has a fare dodger by the elbow. There is a lot of pocket-patting going on.
reallife_crime_fare_near: "I swear I had a ticket." The officer has heard it before. So have you.
reallife_crime_fare_ticket_1: A fine for fare evasion, many times the price of the ride. They took the ticket and left.
reallife_crime_fare_ticket_2: The fare dodger got a ticket and a short lecture, and went on their way.
reallife_crime_fare_cleared_1: The ticket turned up in the last pocket they tried. The officer waved them on.
reallife_crime_fare_cleared_2: They had a valid pass all along. Apologies were not exchanged.
reallife_crime_fare_arrested_1: There was already a warrant out for them. A turnstile jump has turned into a ride downtown.
reallife_crime_fare_arrested_2: Giving the officer a false name did not help. They're being taken in.
reallife_crime_deal_start_1: Two people nearby are standing very close and saying very little. Something small changes hands.
reallife_crime_deal_start_2: A quick handshake down the street that lasted a second too long. A deal, by the look of it.
reallife_crime_deal_start_3: You notice two people nearby doing business the quiet way, eyes on everything but each other.
reallife_crime_deal_near: They both go silent and look at you until you've walked past.
reallife_crime_deal_scattered_1: A cop came round the corner and they scattered, one each way. Neither was caught.
reallife_crime_deal_scattered_2: The deal broke up in a hurry when the police appeared. Both of them got away.
reallife_crime_deal_caught_1: They split up and ran. The officer picked one and caught them; the other is long gone.
reallife_crime_deal_caught_2: One got away. The other is face down on the pavement with an officer's knee in their back.
reallife_crime_deal_nothing_1: An officer questioned them both. One was selling the other a phone charger. Probably.
reallife_crime_deal_nothing_2: The police found nothing on either of them and let them go, unconvinced.
reallife_crime_deal_done_1: Business concluded. They walked off in opposite directions without a word.
reallife_crime_deal_done_2: Whatever it was, it's done. Both of them are gone.
reallife_crime_cartheft_start_1: Somebody on the pavement nearby is watching the cars stopped at the light a little too carefully.
reallife_crime_cartheft_start_2: A figure just stepped off the kerb nearby, straight towards a car waiting in traffic.
reallife_crime_cartheft_x_1: A carjacking: the driver was dragged out and their car is speeding away.
reallife_crime_cartheft_x_2: A car was just taken at the lights. Its owner is standing in the road, shouting after it.
reallife_crime_cartheft_caught_1: The police ran the stolen car down and boxed it in. The thief came out with their hands up.
reallife_crime_cartheft_caught_2: The stolen car didn't get far. One arrest, and one car going back to its owner.
reallife_crime_cartheft_escaped_1: The stolen car lost the patrol car in traffic. It'll turn up stripped in a day or two.
reallife_crime_cartheft_escaped_2: The car thief got away. Somebody is having a long conversation with their insurer tonight.
reallife_crime_stop_start_1: A car nearby just went straight through a red light, and there was a patrol car behind it.
reallife_crime_stop_start_2: Blue lights nearby: the police are pulling a driver over for speeding.
reallife_crime_stop_start_3: A patrol car has lit up behind a driver who was on their phone at the wheel.
reallife_crime_stop_start_4: Somebody nearby ran a stop line with a police car right behind them. Lights on.
reallife_crime_stop_ticket_1: The officer wrote the driver a ticket and sent them on their way.
reallife_crime_stop_ticket_2: A ticket, a lecture, and the driver pulled away again very carefully indeed.
reallife_crime_stop_ticket_3: Licence, registration, and a fine. The traffic stop is over.
reallife_crime_stop_warning_1: The driver got away with a warning. Lucky day.
reallife_crime_stop_warning_2: Just a warning this time. The patrol car has moved on.
reallife_crime_stop_arrested_1: The traffic stop turned into an arrest: the driver had been drinking. Their car is being towed.
reallife_crime_stop_arrested_2: No licence, no insurance, and an attitude. The driver left in the back of the patrol car.
reallife_crime_reckless_start_1: A car just tore past nearby at twice the limit, weaving through traffic. Sirens are following.
reallife_crime_reckless_start_2: A reckless driver is carving through traffic nearby, and the police are after them.
reallife_crime_reckless_start_3: Tyres screaming down the street: somebody is driving like the city is a racetrack.
reallife_crime_reckless_caught_1: The police stopped the reckless driver and took them out of the car in handcuffs.
reallife_crime_reckless_caught_2: Chase over. The driver was drunk; the car is being taken away.
reallife_crime_reckless_escaped_1: The reckless driver lost the patrol car. Somewhere out there they're still at it.
reallife_crime_reckless_escaped_2: The police called off the chase. The driver got away.
reallife_crime_parking_start_1: A traffic officer nearby is writing a ticket for a car parked where it shouldn't be.
reallife_crime_parking_start_2: An officer down the street has a ticket book out and a badly parked car in front of them.
reallife_crime_parking_near: You check, out of habit, that it isn't your car.
reallife_crime_parking_ticketed_1: Ticket under the wiper. The officer has moved on to the next one.
reallife_crime_parking_ticketed_2: The ticket is written. The car's owner has a nasty surprise waiting.
reallife_crime_parking_argued_1: The owner came running and argued for five minutes. They got the ticket anyway.
reallife_crime_parking_argued_2: "I was only gone two minutes!" The officer handed over the ticket without looking up.
reallife_crime_parking_letoff_1: The owner got back just in time and talked their way out of it. The officer tore the ticket up.
reallife_crime_parking_letoff_2: A lucky escape: the officer let them move the car instead of writing them up.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_camera: Security camera: someone at the {shelf} is slipping stock into their coat.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_spotted: You catch it out of the corner of your eye: a customer just pocketed something off the shelf.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_guard: Your security guard has spotted a shoplifter and is going after them.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_prompt: The shoplifter is right there. Press {key} to confront them, or call 911.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_bolted_1: The shoplifter shoved past you and is running for the door.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_bolted_2: "I didn't take anything!" And then they ran for it.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_escaped_1: The shoplifter made it out of the door with {amount} of your stock.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_escaped_2: Gone, and {amount} of stock gone with them. It'll show as theft in the day's books.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_guard_1: Your security guard stopped the shoplifter at the door. {amount} of stock recovered.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_guard_2: Caught by your guard before they reached the street. {amount} goes back on the shelf.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_dropped_1: Confronted, the shoplifter dumped everything on the floor and ran. {amount} of stock recovered.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_dropped_2: They emptied their pockets and fled. You got back {amount} of stock.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_paid_1: Red-faced, the shoplifter paid for what they'd taken: {amount} that would have walked out of the door.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_paid_2: "I was going to pay." They did, in the end. {amount} no longer counts as stolen.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_arrested_1: The officer you called met the shoplifter at the door. {amount} of stock recovered, one arrest.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_start_1: A customer near the shelves keeps glancing at the staff. Their jacket is getting fuller.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_start_2: You notice another customer slipping something into a bag when they think nobody is looking.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_start_3: Someone in here is shopping without a basket, and without any intention of visiting the till.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_x_1: "Hey, you haven't paid for that!" A shoplifter is running for the door.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_x_2: The staff are shouting: somebody is making a run for it with a coat full of goods.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_x_3: "Stop them!" A shoplifter bolts past the tills.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_escaped_1: The shoplifter was out of the door and gone before anyone could react.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_escaped_2: They got away. The cashier sighs and reaches for the incident book.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_caught_1: A police officer was waiting at the door. The shoplifter left the shop in handcuffs.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_caught_2: Stopped at the exit by an officer the staff had called. Pockets emptied, cuffs on.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_false_1: False alarm: they'd simply forgotten to pay. They went back to the till, bright red.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_false_2: An honest mistake, apparently. They stopped at the door, apologised and paid.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_tripped_1: The shoplifter ran straight into you and went down. The staff are very grateful.
reallife_crime_shoplifter_tripped_2: You were in exactly the right place: the thief bounced off you and hit the floor. The manager thanks you.
reallife_crime_holdup_start_1: Someone with a hood up and a hand in their pocket just pushed through the door.
reallife_crime_holdup_start_2: The door bangs open. Whoever just came in is not here to shop.
reallife_crime_holdup_x_1: "Nobody move, and empty the till!" It's a hold-up.
reallife_crime_holdup_x_2: "Everybody stay where you are!" The shop is being robbed.
reallife_crime_holdup_fled_1: The robber grabbed the cash and ran. The police arrived a few minutes too late.
reallife_crime_holdup_fled_2: Over in thirty seconds. The robber is gone, and everyone in the shop starts breathing again.
reallife_crime_holdup_caught_1: The robber ran out of the door and straight into the police. Arrested on the pavement.
reallife_crime_holdup_caught_2: Patrol cars were already outside. The robber didn't get ten steps.
reallife_crime_holdup_bungled_1: The robber lost their nerve, looked around at everyone staring, and fled with nothing.
reallife_crime_holdup_bungled_2: Something spooked them. The would-be robber backed out of the door empty-handed and ran.
reallife_crime_holdup_till_1: The robber emptied your till and ran: {amount} gone.
reallife_crime_pickpocket_noticed_1: You felt a hand in your pocket. {amount} is gone and the thief is making off: catch them.
reallife_crime_pickpocket_noticed_2: Someone just bumped you and your wallet feels lighter by {amount}. They're getting away: go after them.
reallife_crime_pickpocket_unnoticed_1: You reach for your wallet and find it lighter. Somebody lifted {amount} from you back there.
reallife_crime_pickpocket_unnoticed_2: Pickpocketed. You never felt a thing, and {amount} is gone.
reallife_crime_pickpocket_recovered_1: You caught up with the pickpocket and got your {amount} back.
reallife_crime_pickpocket_recovered_2: Cornered, the thief handed back your {amount} and ran.
reallife_crime_pickpocket_lost_1: The pickpocket got away with your {amount}.
reallife_crime_pickpocket_lost_2: Too slow. The thief is gone, and so is {amount}.
reallife_crime_pickpocket_gone: The pickpocket got away with {amount} of your cash.
reallife_crime_mugged_body: Someone has stepped out of the dark and is blocking your way, one hand in their jacket. They want your cash. Handing it over costs part of what you're carrying. Refusing might scare them off, or might get you hurt.
reallife_crime_mugged_complied_1: You handed over {amount}. The mugger counted it while running.
reallife_crime_mugged_complied_2: {amount} gone, but you're in one piece. The mugger vanished into the dark.
reallife_crime_mugged_scared_1: You stood your ground and shouted. The mugger thought better of it and ran.
reallife_crime_mugged_scared_2: "No." It turns out they weren't expecting that. The mugger backed off and bolted.
reallife_crime_mugged_hurt_1: The mugger hit you and you went down hard. You'll be feeling that for a while.
reallife_crime_mugged_hurt_2: Refusing earned you a fist in the ribs. You're hurt.
reallife_crime_mugged_taken: While you were down, the mugger took {amount} from your jacket.
reallife_crime_mugged_avoided_1: Whoever was following you has given up and melted away.
reallife_crime_mugged_avoided_2: You had the feeling someone was coming up behind you. Not any more.
reallife_crime_breakin_alarm: Alarm call: {business} has been broken into. The locksmith and glazier cost you {amount}; the police will report on missing stock in the morning.
reallife_crime_breakin_alarm_free: Alarm call: {business} has been broken into. The police will report on missing stock in the morning.
reallife_crime_breakin_report: Police report on the break-in at {business}: {amount} of stock was taken from the shelves. Better security makes burglars pick another shop.
reallife_crime_breakin_report_nothing: Police report on the break-in at {business}: nothing was taken. The burglars were disturbed, or found nothing worth carrying.
reallife_crime_carbreak_1: Your {vehicle} has been broken into where it was parked: a smashed window, about {amount} to repair.
reallife_crime_carbreak_2: Someone forced the door of your parked {vehicle}. Nothing taken, but the damage will cost about {amount} to fix.
reallife_crime_scam_body_1: "This is the security department of your bank. We've detected suspicious activity on your account and need to verify your card number and PIN immediately."
reallife_crime_scam_body_2: "A parcel in your name is being held at customs. To release it, a small handling fee must be paid by card over the phone today."
reallife_crime_scam_body_3: "Congratulations! You've been selected for a government tax refund. We just need your bank details to process the payment."
reallife_crime_scam_hungup_1: You hung up. Your real bank would never ask for that.
reallife_crime_scam_hungup_2: Click. One more scammer wasting their afternoon.
reallife_crime_scam_lost: It was a scam. By the time you called your real bank, {amount} had been taken.
reallife_crime_scam_lucky: You mistyped a digit, the call dropped, and it slowly dawned on you what that was. A lucky escape.
reallife_crime_jaywalk_warn_1: "Hey, use the crossing!" The officer's shout follows you across the road.
reallife_crime_jaywalk_warn_2: A police officer whistles and points you back to the pavement. Just a warning.
reallife_crime_jaywalk_warn_red_1: "The light's red, pal!" An officer waves you back. No ticket this time.
reallife_crime_jaywalk_warn_red_2: An officer watches you cross against the light and shakes their head. Consider yourself warned.
reallife_crime_jaywalk_fine: An officer saw you wandering across the road and wrote you up: {amount} for jaywalking.
reallife_crime_jaywalk_fine_red: You crossed on red right in front of a police officer. A {amount} ticket.
reallife_crime_pullover_redlight: Police lights behind you: you ran a red light. Pull over and stop.
reallife_crime_pullover_speeding: Police lights behind you: you were clocked well over the speed limit. Pull over and stop.
reallife_crime_pullover_reckless: Police lights behind you: driving on the pavement. Pull over and stop.
reallife_crime_pullover_wrongside: Police lights behind you: you were driving against the traffic. Pull over and stop.
reallife_crime_ticket_redlight: Ticket for running a red light: {amount}.
reallife_crime_ticket_reckless: Ticket for reckless driving (on the pavement): {amount}.
reallife_crime_ticket_wrongside: Ticket for reckless driving (against the traffic): {amount}.
reallife_crime_stop_fleeing: You didn't stop. Now you're fleeing the police, and the bill grows the longer this goes on. Stop to give yourself up, or get out of their sight to lose them.
reallife_crime_stop_escaped: You lost the police. No ticket, but they know your car: for the rest of today they'll be looking out for it.
reallife_crime_stop_dodged: The patrol car lost sight of you. They have your plate, though: for the rest of today they'll be looking out for it.
reallife_crime_bust: Caught after fleeing a traffic stop. Fines for the offences and for running: {amount}. You're being taken in.
reallife_crime_custody_fade: You're taken to the police station...
reallife_crime_custody_released: Released from the holding cell. Hours held: {hours}. You're back where they picked you up.
reallife_911_noted: We already know about that incident. Thank you; stay clear and let the officers work.
reallife_crime_ticket_crash: Ticket for your driving, plus the damages for what you hit on the way: {amount} in all.
reallife_crime_bust_crash: Caught after fleeing a traffic stop and crashing on the way. Fines, damages and the charge for running: {amount} in all. You're being taken in.
reallife_crime_shoptheft_held: The shoplifter freezes with their hands up. Stay close: the police are on their way.
reallife_crime_citizen_hold_1: You've got them. Stay with them: the police are on their way.
reallife_crime_citizen_hold_2: Caught. They put their hands up. Hold them here until an officer arrives.
reallife_crime_citizen_hold_3: You grab them by the jacket and they give up. Don't walk off: the police are coming.
reallife_crime_citizen_break_1: They twisted free and they're running again. After them.
reallife_crime_citizen_break_2: A shove, and they're off. Catch them again.
reallife_crime_citizen_recaught: Got them again. This time the fight has gone out of them.
reallife_crime_citizen_slipped: They slipped away while your back was turned. You did what you could.
reallife_crime_citizen_letgo_1: You walked away and they took their chance. Not your problem.
reallife_crime_citizen_letgo_2: You let them go. They didn't wait to be told twice.
reallife_crime_citizen_nobody: No officer came. You gave them a piece of your mind and let them go; what they took has been handed back.
reallife_crime_citizen_thanks_1: Cuffed and on their way to a cell, thanks to you. The officer shakes your hand, and the victim has their things back.
reallife_crime_citizen_thanks_2: The police have them in handcuffs. "Nice work," says the officer. The victim can't thank you enough.
reallife_crime_citizen_thanks_3: Arrested, because you stepped in. Everything they took has gone back to its owner.
reallife_crime_citizen_reward_1: Arrested, thanks to you. The grateful victim presses {amount} into your hand and won't take no for an answer.
reallife_crime_citizen_reward_2: The officer cuffs them and takes your name. A shopkeeper who saw it all insists you take {amount} as a reward.
reallife_crime_citizen_commend_1: Arrested, thanks to you. The officer says they'll put your name forward for a citizen's commendation. You feel ten feet tall.
reallife_crime_citizen_commend_2: The suspect is led away in handcuffs, and half the street applauds you. A good day.
reallife_city_enabled: City life: people at work and going about their day on the pavements
reallife_city_density: City life: how much is going on (1 = now and then, 10 = always something; never more than 8 people)
reallife_city_workers: City life: people at work (sweepers, road crews, window cleaners, leaflets, carts, couriers, the post, painters, gardeners)
reallife_city_everyday: City life: everyday people (friends talking, smokers, phone calls, tourists, joggers, chess, pushchairs, queues, umbrellas in the rain)
reallife_city_interactions: City life: you can buy a coffee at the coffee cart (the interact key, at the counter)
reallife_city_test_workers: Test: put the next kind of street worker just ahead of you
reallife_city_test_everyday: Test: put the next kind of everyday scene just ahead of you
reallife_city_test_stalls: Test: put the next kind of cart (coffee, hot dogs) just ahead of you; its customers walk up
reallife_city_test_clear: Test: clear the city life people off the street
reallife_city_test_started: City life test: {what}, just ahead of you. Press the button again for the next one.
reallife_city_test_outdoors: Test not started: go out on to the street, on foot, first.
reallife_city_test_loading: Test not started: the mod's animations and models are still loading; try again in a few seconds.
reallife_city_test_failed: City life is switched off for this session after an error. See Player.log.
reallife_city_test_cleared: City life: the street has been cleared.
reallife_city_name_window_cleaner: a window cleaner at a shopfront
reallife_city_name_repairs: a maintenance worker kneeling at a wall
reallife_city_name_fundraiser: a charity fundraiser with a clipboard
reallife_city_name_phone_call: somebody on the phone by the wall
reallife_city_name_busker_audience: an audience for the nearest street performer
reallife_city_name_coffee_cart: a coffee cart with its vendor and customers
reallife_city_coffee_bought: A hot coffee from the cart. That's better.
reallife_city_coffee_broke: You can't afford a coffee right now.
reallife_perf_armed: Close the menu: the measurement starts two seconds later.
reallife_perf_probe_started: Measuring performance for 10 seconds. Play normally.
reallife_perf_probe_done: Performance report written: RealLifeOverhaul_perf_(time).txt, next to Player.log.
reallife_perf_bench_done: Performance test finished and everything is back as it was. The table is RealLifeOverhaul_bench_(time).txt, next to Player.log.
reallife_perf_bench_aborted: Performance test stopped. Everything is back as it was.
reallife_perf_bench_refused: The performance test needs you on foot in the street, with no menu open and the game running.
reallife_jobs_enabled: Jobs you can take yourself (call the Gig Line on your phone)
reallife_test_job_taxi: Test: start a ride-hail shift (your car if it is near, else a hired van)
reallife_contact_jobs_desc: Day work, paid on the spot
reallife_text_jobs_welcome: Gig Line here. Need cash today? Call us: flyers to hand out, parcels to run, and fares to drive once somebody can vouch for you. Paid the moment the work is done.
reallife_job_flyers_pitch: Flyers. A print shop wants a bundle of 24 handed out, wherever you are standing right now. Walk up to people and offer one; some take it, some don't. {pay} for every flyer taken, more on a busy street. No car, no experience needed. You are level {level}; {left} flyers left for today. {status}
reallife_job_courier_pitch: Parcels. Five small parcels from a pick-up address near you to doors around the district, in any order, against the clock. Park, carry each one to the door, hand it over. {pay} a parcel plus {km} per kilometre, a bonus for beating the clock, less for every crash and every time the police pull you over. With no car of your own near you, a van is hired for the day and the fee comes out of your pocket. You are level {level}; {left} parcels left for today. {status}
reallife_job_taxi_pitch: Fares. You drive, in your own car or a van hired for the day: pick people up where they wave, take them where they are going. {pay} a pick-up plus {km} per kilometre, and they tip for a smooth, quick ride. You need a taxi endorsement on your driving licence, a reference from other work and a clean record with the police. You are level {level}; {left} fares left for today. {status}
reallife_jobline_ready: It's yours if you want it.
reallife_jobline_go: You're on. Watch the top of your screen, and call me if you need to drop out.
reallife_jobline_failed: Can't set that one up where you are right now. Try from another street.
reallife_jobline_on_job: You're still on the books as {job}, with {amount} earned this shift. Finish up, or tell me you're done and I'll take you off.
reallife_jobline_quit_done: Off the books. What you'd already earned is yours. Call when you want more.
reallife_job_no_now: Not right now. Call back when you're free.
reallife_job_no_mission: You're already on a delivery. Finish that first.
reallife_job_no_indoors: Call me from the street, not from indoors.
reallife_job_no_sacked: They won't have you back yet after last time. Give it a few days.
reallife_job_no_daily: That's all there is of that for today. Try tomorrow.
reallife_job_no_energy: You sound dead on your feet. Sleep first.
reallife_job_no_reference: For that they want a reference. Reach level 2 in another job and you'll have one.
reallife_job_no_record: Not so soon after the police pulled you over on the job. Keep it clean for two days.
reallife_job_no_car: You need a car near you for that, and there is no room at the roadside here to bring you a hired one. Try from another street.
reallife_job_no_here: Nothing I can set up around where you are. Try from another street.
reallife_job_end_hospital: Your job is over: you are in no state to work. You keep the {amount} you earned.
reallife_job_end_time: Your job ended while you were away. You keep the {amount} you earned.
reallife_job_end_mission: Your job was dropped for the delivery you took on. You keep the {amount} you earned.
reallife_job_end_indoors: You went indoors and your job was called off. You keep the {amount} you earned.
reallife_job_end_exhausted: You are too exhausted to carry on. You keep the {amount} you earned.
reallife_job_end_off: Jobs were switched off. You keep the {amount} you earned.
reallife_job_done_tired: You are too tired for more today. The Gig Line takes you off the books.
reallife_job_week_summary: Gig Line, your week: shifts worked {shifts}, earned {amount}.
reallife_job_level_up: You reached level {level} in this job. It pays more from now on.
reallife_job_level_reference: You reached level {level}. The Gig Line will now give you a reference: better jobs are open to you.
reallife_job_sacked: The Gig Line: "That's three bad shifts. They don't want you back." You are off that job for {days} days.
reallife_job_strike: That shift goes down as a bad one. {left} more and they stop giving you this work.
reallife_job_taxi_obj_stop: Your fare is waving. Stop right beside them.
reallife_job_taxi_obj_car: Get back in your car: you have a fare waiting.
reallife_job_taxi_obj_room: They can't reach a door. Pull up where there is room beside the car.
reallife_job_taxi_obj_boarding: Hold still while your passenger gets in.
reallife_job_taxi_obj_back: Your passenger is sitting in the car. Get back in.
reallife_job_taxi_obj_room_out: No room to open the door. Pull up where your passenger can get out.
reallife_job_taxi_greet_1: Passenger: "{place}, please. No rush, just get me there in one piece."
reallife_job_taxi_greet_2: Passenger: "Hi. {place}. I've had a day, so go easy on the brakes."
reallife_job_taxi_greet_3: Passenger: "{place}. Quick as you can without scaring me."
reallife_job_taxi_greet_4: Passenger: "Thanks for stopping. {place}, if you know it."
reallife_job_taxi_good_2: Passenger: "Smoothest trip I've had all week. Here, a little extra."
reallife_job_taxi_good_3: Passenger: "That's how it's done. Five stars."
reallife_job_taxi_good_4: Passenger: "Perfect, thank you. Have a good one."
reallife_job_taxi_fair_2: Passenger: "Bit of a bumpy one, but fine."
reallife_job_taxi_fair_3: Passenger: "Here's your fare. Maybe ease off a little next time."
reallife_job_taxi_bad_1: Passenger: "Never again. You're lucky I'm paying at all."
reallife_job_taxi_bad_2: Passenger: "Where did you learn to drive? I'm reporting this."
reallife_job_taxi_bad_3: Passenger: "I think I left my stomach three streets back. No tip."
reallife_job_taxi_brake_3: Passenger: "A little warning next time, please."
reallife_job_taxi_crash_1: Passenger: "You hit something! Are you kidding me?"
reallife_job_taxi_crash_2: Passenger: "That was my neck. Watch the road!"
reallife_job_taxi_crash_3: Passenger: "Great. Just great. That's coming off the fare."
reallife_job_taxi_police_1: Passenger: "Is that for us? Oh, come on. I'm going to be late."
reallife_job_taxi_police_2: Passenger: "Police? Seriously? This is the last time I book with you."
reallife_job_taxi_fast_1: Passenger: "Could you slow down? I'd like to arrive alive."
reallife_job_taxi_fast_2: Passenger: "This isn't a race. Slow down!"
reallife_job_taxi_gaveup_1: The Gig Line: "Your fare got tired of waiting and walked. Be quicker."
reallife_job_taxi_gaveup_2: The Gig Line: "Too slow. They took another car."
reallife_job_taxi_hold_1: Passenger: "Hey, hold still, I'm trying to get in!"
reallife_job_taxi_hold_2: Passenger: "Where are you going? Stop the car!"
reallife_job_taxi_abandoned: You left your passenger sitting in the car. They got out and found another ride. No fare.
reallife_job_taxi_done_day: The Gig Line: "That's your fares for today. Good work. Same again tomorrow?"
reallife_job_taxi_done_quiet: The Gig Line: "It's gone quiet around you. Call in again from a busier part of town."
reallife_test_job_flyers: Test: start handing out flyers (on foot, on a street with people)
reallife_test_job_courier: Test: start a parcel round (your car if it is near, else a hired van)
reallife_job_flyers_on_foot: You hand flyers out on foot. Get out of the car and call again.
reallife_job_flyers_obj: Offer flyers to passers-by: {taken} of {bundle} taken
reallife_job_flyers_obj_back: You have wandered off your pitch. Go back to hand out the rest.
reallife_job_flyers_time: The Gig Line: "Time's up on the flyers. You're paid for the ones that were taken."
reallife_job_flyers_took_4: "Go on, then. My sister loves that place."
reallife_job_courier_prompt_load: {key}: load the parcels into the car
reallife_job_courier_prompt_take: {key}: take a parcel from the car
reallife_job_courier_prompt_leave: {key}: leave the parcel at the door
reallife_job_courier_obj_depot: Parcels to collect at {place}: {count}. Park nearby and walk up.
reallife_job_courier_obj_hands: Your hands are full. Put that away before you collect the parcels.
reallife_job_courier_obj_car: Carry the parcels to your car and load them.
reallife_job_courier_obj_fetch: The parcel is still in your car. Take it out at the car first.
reallife_job_courier_loaded: All loaded. The clock is running: any order you like.
reallife_job_courier_time: The Gig Line: "You're out of time. The rest go back to the sender; you're paid for the doors you made."
reallife_job_courier_left: Nobody came to the door. You leave the parcel on the step.
reallife_job_courier_no_box: The parcels weren't ready after all. The round is called off.
reallife_job_courier_thanks_1: "Finally! I've been waiting on this all day. Thank you."
reallife_job_courier_thanks_3: "Oh, lovely. Mind the step on your way."
reallife_job_courier_bump_1: Something slid across the back seat. That will come off your pay.
reallife_job_courier_bump_2: You hear a parcel hit the floor. The shop will hear about that dent.
reallife_test_refused_not_loaded: Test not started: the save is still loading. Try again in a few seconds.
reallife_test_refused_indoors: Test not started: you are indoors. Go out on to the street first.
reallife_test_refused_traffic_off: Test not started: the street is paused while a menu is open or time is being skipped.
reallife_test_refused_scene_active: Test not started: something of this kind is already going on. Wait for it to end, or end it first.
reallife_test_refused_police_busy: Test not started: the police already have business with you. Settle that first.
reallife_test_refused_pool_busy: Test not started: all the people it needs are busy elsewhere. Try again in a few seconds.
reallife_test_refused_feature_off: Test not started: its option is switched off. Switch it on above and try again.
reallife_test_refused_no_moving_car: Test not started: no traffic car on the move within {metres} m. Stand near a street with traffic and try again.
reallife_test_refused_nobody_near: Test not started: no pedestrian within {metres} m.
reallife_test_refused_not_driving: Test not started: you need to be driving a car.
reallife_test_refused_nothing_fits: Test not started: nothing of this kind can be set up at this place and hour. Try another street, or another button.
reallife_job_flyers_nobody: No one close enough. Walk up to someone and press {key}.
reallife_job_hint_door: You are on a job: going indoors would end the shift. Click the building if you mean to.
reallife_perf_stale_lights: Street lamps the game has switched off no longer keep their lights enabled (no visible change)
reallife_perf_step_timing: Measurements time every step of the frame (switch off only if a measurement ever misbehaves)
reallife_perf_sky_updates: The sky's reflection and its light on things are refreshed every 2 seconds instead of every frame (no visible change)
reallife_perf_refraction: Outdoors, the refraction effect is switched off, as nothing outdoors uses it (no visible change)
reallife_perf_far_districts2: Scenery more than 1.3 km away is not drawn, and is back before you can see it (no visible change)
reallife_perf_view_radius: People, cars and small things are drawn only within 300 m in every direction, as they already are straight ahead (buildings and roads unchanged)
reallife_perf_far_props2: Street furniture and parked cars are not drawn beyond 200 m (visible: they appear at 200 m instead of 300 m)
reallife_perf_bench_started4: Performance test: about 3 minutes. Stand still and leave the mouse alone. Parts of the picture and of the interface will go and come back for a second at a time, many times over; that is the test.
reallife_car_tuning: Realistic car performance: every car accelerates and tops out like its kind (off: the game's own cars)
reallife_car_top_speed: Car top speed (% of each car's own)
reallife_car_acceleration: Car acceleration (% of each car's own)
reallife_car_smooth_throttle: Smooth throttle: the key eases the pedal down, a tap pulls away gently
reallife_car_measure: Measure this car (then stop, and hold full throttle for 20 seconds)
reallife_car_measure_armed: Measuring: stand still, then hold full throttle for 20 seconds on a straight, empty road.
reallife_car_measure_result: {car}: 0-50 km/h in {to50} s, 0-100 in {to100} s, {after20} km/h after 20 s. Its target: 0-100 in {target} s, top speed {top} km/h.
reallife_car_measure_stopped: Measurement stopped: it needs one run from a standstill at full throttle for 20 seconds. Press the button again to retry.
reallife_camera_mouselook_keys: Mouse look, GTA style (the 'Free the cursor' key under Controls gives the mouse back)
reallife_enter_with_keys: Get into buildings and your vehicles with the interact keys (see Controls)
reallife_keys_header: Controls (click a line, then press the new key; Shift, Ctrl or Alt may be held with it)
reallife_keys_reset: Reset the mod's keys to their defaults
reallife_keys_interact: Interact: enter a building or car, job and street prompts
reallife_keys_interact_alt: Interact, second key (only while the game offers nothing itself)
reallife_keys_free_cursor: Free the cursor while mouse look is on
reallife_keys_gentle_throttle: Gentle throttle: half the pedal (hold; needs Smooth throttle)
reallife_keys_phone_dump: Write the phone's interface to a file (developer diagnostics)
reallife_test_job_cleaner: Test: start a cleaning job at a business nearby (on foot)
reallife_test_job_stocker: Test: start stocking shelves at a shop nearby (on foot)
reallife_test_job_vendor: Test: start a drinks cart shift (on foot, on a pavement with room)
reallife_test_job_busker: Test: start busking (on foot, on a pavement)
reallife_job_on_foot: That one is done on foot. Get out of the car and ask again.
reallife_job_no_client: Nobody near you is open and asking for help right now. Try from another street, or in opening hours.
reallife_job_obj_hands: Your hands are full. Put that away first.
reallife_job_rental_no_money: You have no car near you, and hiring a van for the day is more than you have on you.
reallife_job_rental_returning: Your hired van is still out. Get out of it and let it be collected before you take driving work again.
reallife_job_rental_hired: You have no car nearby, so the Gig Line has hired you a van for the day: {amount}. It is waiting at the roadside near you. It goes back when the shift ends.
reallife_job_rental_again: Your hire is paid up for today: a van is waiting at the roadside near you.
reallife_job_rental_return: Shift over. Park up and get out: the hired van is collected as soon as you leave it.
reallife_job_cleaner_pitch: Cleaning. A business near you has spills on its floor and nobody to see to them. Go in, mop each patch, done. {pay} a patch and a little extra for the whole floor. The mop is theirs; you bring the elbow. You are level {level}; {left} patches left for today. {status}
reallife_job_stocker_pitch: Shelves. A shop near you has a delivery sitting on the pavement and no one to bring it in. Carry the boxes in one at a time and stock the shelf each is for. {pay} a box, a little extra for clearing the pile in time. You are level {level}; {left} boxes left for today. {status}
reallife_job_vendor_pitch: A drinks cart. We set it up on the pavement where you are standing and you work it: people ask for one of three drinks, you serve the right one before they lose patience. {pay} for every customer served, and they tip when you are quick. Keep three waiting too long and the shift is over. You are level {level}; {left} customers left for today. {status}
reallife_job_busker_pitch: Not really ours, but I'll tell you: a guitar and a patch of pavement. You play, people drop what they like in the case. A busy street in the evening pays; an empty one at dawn does not. About {pay} a song on an ordinary street, played well. The police move you on now and then. You are level {level}; {left} songs left in you today. {status}
reallife_job_cleaner_obj_go: Cleaning wanted at {place}. Walk there and go in.
reallife_job_cleaner_obj_back: There is more floor to do at {place}. Go back in.
reallife_job_cleaner_obj_floor: Mop the spills: {done} of {count} done. Stand on the next one.
reallife_job_cleaner_time: The Gig Line: "Time's up on the cleaning. You're paid for the patches you did."
reallife_job_cleaner_small: There is no more clear floor to work on in here. That is the job done.
reallife_job_cleaner_no_mop: There was no mop to be had after all. The job is called off; you are paid for what you did.
reallife_job_cleaner_done: "Spotless. Thank you." The floor is done.
reallife_job_stocker_obj_pile: Boxes for {place} on the pavement by its door: {left}. Pick one up.
reallife_job_stocker_obj_shelf: Take the box to its shelf: {done} of {count} stocked.
reallife_job_stocker_obj_out: Boxes still outside: {left}. Go back out for the next one.
reallife_job_stocker_time: The Gig Line: "The shop needed that delivery in by now. You're paid for the boxes you shelved."
reallife_job_stocker_no_shelf: There is no shelf you can get to in here. The job is called off; you are paid for what you did.
reallife_job_stocker_no_box: The boxes were not ready after all. The job is called off.
reallife_job_stocker_done: "That's the lot. Good work." The delivery is in.
reallife_job_vendor_no_room: There is no room for a cart on this pavement. Try a wider one.
reallife_job_vendor_obj_post: Your cart is set up. Take your place behind it.
reallife_job_vendor_obj_back: Customers are waiting. Get back behind your cart.
reallife_job_vendor_obj_order: "{item}, please." Serve it with the matching key.
reallife_job_vendor_open: You are open. Here they come.
reallife_job_vendor_thanks_1: "Just what I needed. Keep the change."
reallife_job_vendor_left_1: "Forget it. I haven't got all day." They walk off.
reallife_job_vendor_left_2: "I'll go somewhere that wants my money." They walk off.
reallife_job_vendor_abandoned: You left the cart standing with nobody at it. The owner has taken it back; you are paid for the customers you served.
reallife_job_vendor_sacked: The cart's owner: "Three walked off. Pack it in." You are paid for the customers you served.
reallife_job_vendor_done: That was the last of them. The owner takes the cart back.
reallife_job_busker_no_room: There is no room to set up on this pavement. Try another spot.
reallife_job_busker_obj_pitch: Stand on your pitch and set up.
reallife_job_busker_obj_next: Pick the next song, or pack up.
reallife_job_busker_obj_song: Playing: {song}. Strum when it is called for, and only then.
reallife_job_busker_wrong: A wrong note. Strum only when it is called for.
reallife_job_busker_good_1: That one went down well: {amount} in the case.
reallife_job_busker_good_2: A few people slowed to listen. {amount} in the case.
reallife_job_busker_poor_1: A ragged one. {amount} in the case.
reallife_job_busker_poor_2: People walked a little faster. {amount} in the case.
reallife_job_busker_no_play: You cannot play here after all. You pack up.
reallife_job_busker_packed: You pack up. What is in the case is yours.
reallife_job_busker_done: Your fingers have had enough for one day. You pack up.
reallife_job_busker_moved_on: An officer: "You can't play here all day. Move along." You pack up; what is in the case is yours.
reallife_job_rental_lost: The hired van is a write-off and has been towed away. The shift is over; you keep what you earned.

reallife_home_header: Real Life Overhaul: Home and health
reallife_home_needs: Needs: hygiene, stress and a tidy home
reallife_home_strip: Show the needs strip (at home, or when a need runs low)
reallife_home_easy: Easy needs: needs wear down half as fast, illness is half as likely
reallife_home_routines: Home routines: cook, make coffee, tidy up, floor exercises
reallife_home_morning_option: Morning summary after a night's sleep
reallife_home_illness: Illness (cold, flu, food poisoning, back pain, burnout) and the doctor at the hospital
reallife_home_body: Body changes slowly with exercise and food (on waking)
reallife_test_home_page: Test: open the "How am I doing" page
reallife_test_home_cook: Test: cook the first dish the fridges allow (needs food in a fridge at home)
reallife_test_home_coffee: Test: make a coffee (needs a coffee machine at home)
reallife_home_people_notice: People are keeping their distance. You need a wash.
reallife_home_cook_slider: {recipe}: {minutes} min, uses {portions} of the {have} portions in your fridge. Leftovers put by: {leftovers}.
reallife_home_cook_info: Cooked food fills more than the same food eaten cold and counts as a proper meal. The food leaves the fridge when you start: stopping early wastes it.
reallife_home_cook_done: {meal}: cooked and eaten. That was good.
reallife_home_cook_done_leftovers: {meal}: cooked and eaten, and there is some left for another day.
reallife_home_cook_burnt: {meal}: burnt. You ate what could be saved.
reallife_home_cook_wasted: {meal}: you took it off the heat half raw. The food is wasted.
reallife_home_coffee_info: Ten minutes, a little energy and a little calm. Cups today: {cups} (after {most} it only makes you jittery).
reallife_home_coffee_no_kick: A fresh coffee, but you have had all the lift food and drink can give you today.
reallife_home_coffee_too_many: One coffee too many: your hands are shaking.
reallife_home_tidy_slider: {minutes} min: the flat goes from {now} to about {then} out of 100.
reallife_home_tidy_done: Tidied up. The flat is at {tidy} out of 100.
reallife_home_exercise_slider: {minutes} min. Builds fitness and takes stress off; costs energy and a clean shirt.
reallife_home_run_line: Run to the next checkpoint ({done} of {all} reached)
reallife_home_run_started: A loop of six checkpoints, back to where you stand. Run it: walking does not count.
reallife_home_run_started_park: A loop of six checkpoints round the park. Running here is worth a quarter more.
reallife_home_run_started_rain: A loop of six checkpoints. It is raining: the run is worth a fifth less, and you will get soaked.
reallife_home_run_done: Run finished: {minutes} minutes, fitness +{fitness}. You could use a shower.
reallife_home_run_ended_left: Run over after {legs} checkpoints: {minutes} minutes, fitness +{fitness}.
reallife_home_run_ended_tired: You are out of puff. Run over after {legs} checkpoints: fitness +{fitness}.
reallife_home_run_ended_time: You took too long over it. Run over after {legs} checkpoints: fitness +{fitness}.
reallife_home_run_ended_stopped: Run stopped after {legs} checkpoints: {minutes} minutes, fitness +{fitness}.
reallife_home_morning: Good morning. You slept {slept} hours and feel {quality}. {tip}
reallife_home_refused_busy: Not now: finish what you are doing first (a menu, a conversation or an activity is open, or the game is paused).
reallife_home_refused_on_job: Not while you are on a job shift.
reallife_home_refused_vehicle: Get out of the vehicle first.
reallife_home_refused_running: You are out on a run: finish it or stop it first.
reallife_home_refused_not_home: This is done at home: go into a home you rent or own.
reallife_home_refused_not_here: Not in somebody else's premises: do it at home, in a place of your own, or out of doors.
reallife_home_refused_no_cooker: There is no cooker in this home: buy a stove or a grill and place it.
reallife_home_refused_no_coffee_machine: There is no coffee machine in this home.
reallife_home_refused_no_food: There is not enough food in the fridge for that, and no leftovers: put groceries in a fridge at home.
reallife_home_refused_no_room: There is no clear piece of floor within a few steps: try somewhere with more room.
reallife_home_refused_ill: You are in no state for that: rest, or stretch gently.
reallife_home_refused_tired: You are too tired for that.
reallife_home_refused_no_pavement: There is no pavement within 12 m to start a run from.
reallife_home_refused_no_route: No loop of pavement could be found from here: try from a more open street.
reallife_home_refused_not_hospital: The doctor is seen at a hospital or a clinic: go inside one.
reallife_text_health_welcome: Your wellbeing page. Call for a summary of how you are doing (hygiene, stress, home, health, fitness, food and sleep), and to tidy up, exercise or go for a run.
reallife_health_page_off: Home life and health is switched off on the options page.
reallife_health_page_ill: {illness}. {symptom} About {days} to go. A doctor at the hospital can halve that.
reallife_health_page_note: Sick note valid for {days}: a lost job shift is no strike.
reallife_health_tip_doctor: Tip: see a doctor at the hospital, and sleep it off.
reallife_health_tip_sleep: Tip: you owe yourself sleep. A full night in a good bed, before one in the morning.
reallife_health_tip_eat: Tip: eat something. Cooking at home is the best meal there is.
reallife_health_tip_relax: Tip: wind down. Television, a book, a bath or a run all take stress off.
reallife_health_tip_tidy: Tip: tidy up the flat (from this page, or with a mop).
reallife_health_tip_cook: Tip: cook at home for a few days. Bought food and skipped meals are dragging you down.
reallife_health_tip_exercise: Tip: it has been days since you exercised. A run, the gym or push-ups at home.
reallife_health_menu_routines_text: What do you want to do?
reallife_health_menu_exercise_text: Which exercise? It is done right where you stand, if there is room.
reallife_health_menu_ok: Put the phone away and it starts.
reallife_health_caught: You have come down with {illness} ({cause}). It should last about {days}.
reallife_health_over: You are over it: {illness} is gone.
reallife_health_symptom_cold: You feel rotten and tire faster.
reallife_health_symptom_flu: You feel rotten, tire much faster and cannot exercise.
reallife_health_symptom_food: You cannot keep food down, tire much faster and cannot exercise.
reallife_health_symptom_back: Everything aches and exercise is out, except gentle stretching, which helps.
reallife_health_symptom_burnout: You are worn out and tire faster. It will not lift until the stress comes down.
reallife_health_cause_rain: an hour out in the rain without an umbrella
reallife_health_cause_no_sleep: too little sleep for too long
reallife_health_cause_diet: a poor diet has left you run down
reallife_health_cause_strain: more exercise than you are fit for
reallife_health_cause_overwork: weeks of stress with no let-up
reallife_health_test_cured: Test: cured, and the three days of immunity are cleared.
reallife_health_test_nothing_to_cure: Test: there was nothing to cure.
reallife_health_test_fitness: Test: fitness is now {fitness} out of 100. The body shows it the next time you wake.
reallife_health_test_needs_low: Test: hygiene, stress, the flat and sleep debt are all set to a bad state.
reallife_health_test_needs_full: Test: hygiene, stress, the flat and sleep debt are all set to a good state.
reallife_doctor_wait_info: About {minutes} minutes' wait, then the doctor. The consultation is {amount}, paid when you are seen.
reallife_doctor_no_money: The consultation has to be paid first. Come back when you can.
reallife_doctor_checkup: A full check-up, and nothing wrong with you. Fitness {fitness} out of 100, diet {diet}, {debt} hours of sleep owed. {tip}
reallife_doctor_diagnosis: It is {illness}. {symptom} Left alone it will take about {days}. A prescription ({fee}) halves that and eases it; a sick note ({note} more) covers you at work for two days.
reallife_doctor_diagnosis_hurt: That injury needs dressing properly. A prescription ({fee}) will have you right again; a sick note ({note} more) covers you at work for two days.
reallife_doctor_already: You are already on medicine for {illness}: about {days} to go. Keep taking it and rest. I can write you a sick note.
reallife_doctor_done_medicine: Take these with food. You should be right in about {days}. Rest: a full night's sleep helps as much as the pills.
reallife_doctor_done_both: Take these with food: about {days} and you are right. And here is your note: two days, no questions asked at work.
reallife_doctor_done_note: Here is your note: two days, no questions asked at work.
reallife_doctor_note_used: Your sick note covered that shift: no strike.
reallife_home_refused_no_animation: Your character has no animation for that exercise in this version of the game, so it is not offered.
reallife_law_precincts: Police stations: one in each district, with its sign, patrol cars and officers at the door
reallife_law_custody: Custody: an arrest ends in a holding cell at the nearest police station (off: a time skip where you were caught)
reallife_law_arrests: Arrests for serious offences: a death on the road even if you stop, a fifth 911 call about nothing in one day, and being wanted after you get away
reallife_law_reputation: Record and reputation have effects: more police scrutiny with a long record, thanks from passers-by with a good name
reallife_law_test_arrest_minor: Test: arrest me (minor: fled a traffic stop)
reallife_law_test_arrest_serious: Test: arrest me (serious: hit-and-run with an injury)
reallife_law_test_nearest: Test: show the nearest police station
reallife_law_test_clear: Test: clear my record and reset my reputation
reallife_test_refused_no_precinct: Test not started: the police stations are not set up yet, so step out on to a street and try again in a few seconds.
reallife_test_refused_screen_busy: Test not started: wait until the conversation or time skip is over.
reallife_law_test_fine: Test arrest started: close this menu and it begins. The test charges no fines.
reallife_law_charge_hit_and_run: Reckless driving causing a crash, and leaving the scene
reallife_law_charge_injury_fled: Injuring a pedestrian and leaving the scene
reallife_law_charge_death_stayed: Causing the death of a pedestrian
reallife_law_charge_death_fled: Causing the death of a pedestrian and leaving the scene
reallife_law_charge_wanted: Wanted: left the scene after hurting a pedestrian
reallife_law_arrest_notice: You are under arrest. Charge: {charges}. Sentence: {hours} hours in a holding cell at the {precinct}.
reallife_law_arrest_dropped: The officers could not take you in. You are let go with the fines already charged; it stays on your record.
reallife_law_cell_paid: Fines and damages charged at your arrest: {amount}
reallife_law_cell_sentence: Sentence: {hours} hours. The clock runs in game time.
reallife_law_cell_sentence_repeat: Sentence: {hours} hours, longer because you have been held here recently. The clock runs in game time.
reallife_law_cell_waiting: You sit back down on the bench.
reallife_law_cell_lawyer_short: You cannot afford the lawyer's fee.
reallife_law_cell_lawyer_done: Your lawyer had a third of the remaining time struck off.
reallife_law_released: Released from the {precinct}. Hours held: {hours}. Fines and damages paid: {amount}. It is on your record.
