reallife_leisure_chess_no_table: Street chess: there is no chess player at a table here.
reallife_leisure_chess_too_far: Street chess: walk up to the free stool at the chess table first.
reallife_leisure_chess_set_up: A chess player has set up a table just ahead. Walk up to the free stool.
reallife_leisure_chess_sit_down: Your stake is on the table. Walk to the free stool.
reallife_leisure_chess_flag: Your clock runs down while you stare at the board. Your opponent plays on, a move to the good.
reallife_leisure_chess_result: You scored {points} of 10 over five positions.
reallife_leisure_chess_won: Your opponent tips their king over. You win {amount}.
reallife_leisure_chess_drawn: A draw by agreement. You take your stake back.
reallife_leisure_chess_lost: Your opponent wins, and pockets your {amount}. "Come back any time."
reallife_leisure_chess_p1: The opening. Your opponent has pushed their king's pawn two squares; your pieces are all still at home.
reallife_leisure_chess_p1_m2: Push a pawn on the edge
reallife_leisure_chess_p1_r1: Sound. A piece out and an eye on the centre. Your opponent nods and does the same.
reallife_leisure_chess_p1_r2: Harmless, but slow. Your opponent takes the centre.
reallife_leisure_chess_p1_r3: Too soon. Your opponent chases her round the board, bringing a piece out with every move.
reallife_leisure_chess_p2: Their bishop pins your knight: if the knight moves, the bishop takes your queen behind it.
reallife_leisure_chess_p2_m2: Push a pawn at the bishop
reallife_leisure_chess_p2_r1: Your opponent takes your queen with a small smile.
reallife_leisure_chess_p2_r2: The bishop must take or retreat. Either way the pin is over.
reallife_leisure_chess_p2_r3: Nothing is lost, but you are the one doing the dodging.
reallife_leisure_chess_p3: Your knight can jump to a square where it attacks their king and their rook at the same time.
reallife_leisure_chess_p3_m2: Take a pawn with the bishop
reallife_leisure_chess_p3_r1: Safe enough, but your opponent sees the fork now and tucks the rook away.
reallife_leisure_chess_p3_r2: That bishop was guarding your king. Their queen walks in.
reallife_leisure_chess_p3_r3: Check! The king must step aside, and you lift the rook off the board.
reallife_leisure_chess_p4: Your opponent has left their queen on the same file as their king, and your rook can reach that file.
reallife_leisure_chess_p4_m1: Put the rook on the file
reallife_leisure_chess_p4_r1: The queen is pinned to the king and cannot run. She falls next move.
reallife_leisure_chess_p4_r2: Your opponent steps out of the line, and the piece that took the pawn is trapped.
reallife_leisure_chess_p4_r3: Your opponent blocks the check, tidies their king away, and the chance is gone.
reallife_leisure_chess_p5: You are a pawn ahead and the position is quiet. Your opponent offers to swap queens.
reallife_leisure_chess_p5_r1: The attack comes to nothing, but you are still a pawn up.
reallife_leisure_chess_p5_r2: With less on the board your extra pawn counts for more. Your opponent frowns at it.
reallife_leisure_chess_p5_r3: There was no mate at the end of it. Now your opponent is the one ahead.
reallife_leisure_chess_p6: Your king is still in the middle of the board, and their rooks are lining up on the open file in front of it.
reallife_leisure_chess_p6_r1: Their rook lands on the open file with check. It goes downhill from there.
reallife_leisure_chess_p6_r2: It holds for now, though that bishop will never move again.
reallife_leisure_chess_p6_r3: The king is safe in the corner and your own rook comes into the game.
reallife_leisure_chess_p7: The endgame. A king each, and you have one pawn left, three squares from becoming a queen.
reallife_leisure_chess_p7_m1: King in front of the pawn
reallife_leisure_chess_p7_r1: By the book. Their king is shouldered aside and the pawn walks home.
reallife_leisure_chess_p7_r2: It gets there by a single move, with your heart in your mouth.
reallife_leisure_chess_p7_r3: Their king slips round yours and eats the pawn.
reallife_leisure_chess_p8: Your king sits behind three pawns that have never moved, and their rook is eyeing your back row.
reallife_leisure_chess_p8_m1: Guard the row with a rook
reallife_leisure_chess_p8_r1: Solid, though your rook has become a night watchman.
reallife_leisure_chess_p8_r2: Now a check on the back row is only a check. A good habit.
reallife_leisure_chess_p8_r3: Rook to the back row: mate. Your opponent lets you take it back, shaking their head.

reallife_social_topic_fine_1: It's a lovely day out. It seems a waste to be inside.
reallife_social_topic_fine_2: Have you looked outside? The city almost looks pretty today.
reallife_social_topic_fine_a: We should get out in it
reallife_social_topic_fine_ra: We should! Say the word and I'll put my shoes on.
reallife_social_topic_fine_rb: Such a cynic. I'm going to enjoy it anyway.
reallife_social_topic_memory_1: I was thinking about the other day. You know: {outing}. That was good.
reallife_social_topic_memory_2: Remember: {outing}. I keep smiling about that.
reallife_social_topic_memory_ra: Yes! Soon. You pick the day.
reallife_social_topic_memory_rb: All right? I thought it was more than all right. Never mind.
reallife_social_topic_birthday_1: It's my birthday soon, you know. Days to go: {days}. I'm only mentioning it.
reallife_social_topic_birthday_2: Days until I'm a year older: {days}. Not that I'm counting.
reallife_social_topic_birthday_ra: Good. A call on the day would be plenty. But a call.
reallife_social_topic_birthday_rb: Yes, already. Write it down this time.
reallife_social_topic_rich_1: You're doing well for yourself these days, aren't you? People have noticed.
reallife_social_topic_rich_2: Look at you, moving up in the world. What's it like?
reallife_social_topic_rich_b: It's every bit as good as it looks
reallife_social_topic_rich_ra: I know you are. That's the only reason I can stand it.
reallife_social_topic_rich_rb: Hm. Don't forget who knew you before, that's all.
reallife_social_topic_sick_1: You sound dreadful. Are you ill?
reallife_social_topic_sick_2: Is that a cough? You're not looking after yourself.
reallife_social_topic_sick_ra: Good. Do it today, not when it's worse. And drink something hot.
reallife_social_topic_sick_rb: That's what everybody says. Rest, at least. Promise me.
reallife_social_topic_breakin_1: I heard about the break-in at {shop}. That's awful. Did they take much?
reallife_social_topic_breakin_2: Somebody broke into {shop}? I'm so sorry. You must be furious.
reallife_social_topic_breakin_ra: That's the spirit. If you need a hand clearing up, I'm there.
reallife_social_topic_breakin_rb: Get two. And a camera. And a very large dog.
reallife_social_topic_knocked_1: Somebody said you were knocked down in the road! Are you hurt?
reallife_social_topic_knocked_2: Is it true a car hit you? You can't keep doing this to me.
reallife_social_topic_knocked_ra: Thank goodness. Look both ways. I'm being serious.
reallife_social_topic_knocked_rb: You're impossible. Take it easy for a day or two, at least.
reallife_social_topic_district_1: It's been noisy round {district} this week. They're digging the road up again.
reallife_social_topic_district_2: You should come over to {district} some time. It's changed since you last saw it.
reallife_social_topic_district_ra: Then come! I'll show you the good bits and hide the rest.
reallife_social_topic_district_rb: Big words. We'll compare notes one day.
reallife_social_topic_quiet_1: Nothing much to report, to be honest. Quiet week. You?
reallife_social_topic_quiet_2: Same old, same old. Tell me something interesting.
reallife_social_topic_quiet_3: I've got no news at all. I just like hearing from you.
reallife_social_topic_quiet_ra: It is, isn't it? I'll take a boring week over an eventful one.
reallife_social_topic_quiet_rb: Two dull people on the phone. We should do something about that.
reallife_social_greet_acq_1: Hi! You found it. I wasn't sure you'd come.
reallife_social_greet_acq_2: Hello again. It's good to see you outside of... well, wherever we met.
reallife_social_greet_acq_3: Hey! Right on time. I only just got here myself.
reallife_social_greet_friend_1: There you are! I've been looking forward to this all day.
reallife_social_greet_friend_2: Hey, you. You look well. Come on, let's do this.
reallife_social_greet_friend_3: You made it! I saved us a spot. Well, I stood on one.
reallife_social_greet_close_1: Come here, you. It's been too long.
reallife_social_greet_close_2: Finally! I've got so much to tell you.
reallife_social_greet_close_3: Look who it is. My favourite bad influence.
reallife_social_greet_love_2: There you are. I've been counting the minutes.
reallife_social_greet_love_3: Hey, you. I missed you today.
reallife_social_greet_late_1: You're late. I was about to give up and go home.
reallife_social_greet_late_2: Oh, there you are. I've been standing here long enough to know this pavement personally.
reallife_social_greet_late_3: I've been waiting ages. A text would have been nice.
reallife_social_greet_late_easy_1: You're late! Good. That makes two of us, I only just got here.
reallife_social_greet_late_easy_2: Don't apologise, I'm never on time either. Come on.
reallife_social_they_late_1: Sorry, sorry! The subway sat in a tunnel for ten minutes. Have you been waiting long?
reallife_social_they_late_2: I know, I'm late. I couldn't find my keys. Forgive me?
reallife_social_they_late_3: Sorry! I left on time, I swear. The city had other ideas.
reallife_social_part_1: This was good. Let's not leave it so long next time.
reallife_social_part_2: Right, I'd better head off. Thanks for today.
reallife_social_part_3: I needed that. Get home safe!
reallife_social_part_4: Same again soon? Good. See you!
reallife_social_part_love_1: I'll call you tonight. Go on, before I change my mind and keep you.
reallife_social_part_love_2: Today was perfect. See you soon, love.
reallife_social_after_bad_1: Well. That could have gone better. Another time, maybe.
reallife_social_after_bad_2: I think I'll call it a day. No hard feelings.
reallife_social_after_bad_3: Not our best outing, was it? Never mind.
reallife_social_after_coffee_1: That hit the spot. They do know how to make a coffee at {place}.
reallife_social_after_coffee_2: Nothing beats a coffee out in the fresh air. Thanks for this.
reallife_social_after_coffee_3: I feel human again. Good coffee, good company.
reallife_social_after_meal_1: I'm stuffed. That was exactly what I wanted.
reallife_social_after_meal_2: Good food, and you didn't steal my fries. A perfect meal.
reallife_social_after_meal_3: I won't need to eat until Thursday. That was great.
reallife_social_after_drinks_1: What a night! My ears are still ringing.
reallife_social_after_drinks_2: I haven't danced like that in years. Don't tell anyone.
reallife_social_after_drinks_3: That was a proper night out. I'll regret it in the morning and I don't care.
reallife_social_after_cinema_1: I did not see that ending coming. Did you?
reallife_social_after_cinema_2: Great film. You jumped at the loud bit, I saw you.
reallife_social_after_cinema_3: I could watch that again tomorrow. Thanks for coming with me.
reallife_social_after_walk_1: I needed that. A walk fixes most things.
reallife_social_after_walk_2: My feet say stop but my head feels clear. Thank you.
reallife_social_after_walk_3: We should do this more often. It costs nothing and I feel better.
reallife_social_after_drive_1: That was lovely. You see the city differently through a windscreen.
reallife_social_after_drive_2: Smooth driving! I nearly fell asleep, and I mean that as a compliment.
reallife_social_after_drive_3: Thanks for the ride. Next time I'm choosing the music.
reallife_social_after_workout_1: Good session! You kept up better than I expected.
reallife_social_after_workout_2: I'll feel that tomorrow. Worth it.
reallife_social_after_workout_3: That's the best I've trained in weeks. You're a good gym partner.
reallife_social_after_business_1: So this is what you've built. I'm impressed. Really.
reallife_social_after_business_2: You did all this? It's a proper business. Look at you.
reallife_social_after_business_3: I like it. It feels like you. Thank you for showing me.
reallife_social_after_lift_1: You're a star. I'd never have made it without you. Here, for the petrol.
reallife_social_after_lift_2: Door to door! Thank you. I owe you one, and here's something towards the fuel.
reallife_social_after_lift_3: That saved my day. Thanks. Take this for your trouble.
reallife_social_after_moving_1: That's the lot! I couldn't have done it alone. Pizza's on me.
reallife_social_after_moving_2: All done. You're a true friend. Take this and get yourself something to eat.
reallife_social_after_moving_3: Last box! Thank you, thank you. I'll remember this.
reallife_social_closed_1: Oh no, {place} is shut. Never mind. Let's just walk instead.
reallife_social_closed_2: Closed! Typical. Come on, a walk will do us just as much good.
reallife_social_pay_ask: Shall we? It'll come to about {cost} for the two of us, {half} each.
reallife_social_pay_ask_offer: Shall we go in? About {cost} for both. Let me get this one.
reallife_social_pay_covered: You've not got it on you? Don't worry, I'll cover it. You get the next one.
reallife_social_walk_talk_1: {first}: "I never notice this street when I'm rushing. It's nice."
reallife_social_walk_talk_2: {first}: "Can I tell you something? I've been thinking about changing jobs."
reallife_social_walk_talk_3: {first}: "You walk fast. Are we late for something?"
reallife_social_walk_talk_4: {first}: "I love this time of day. Everybody's going somewhere."
reallife_social_walk_talk_5: {first}: "This is better than sitting indoors. Good idea."
reallife_social_walk_behind_2: {first}: "Where are you going? I thought we were walking together."
reallife_social_left_1: {first} has given up and gone home. "I suppose you had somewhere better to be."
reallife_social_left_2: {first} waited, then left. "Call me when you've got time for me."
reallife_social_ride_talk_1: {first}: "I never get driven anywhere. This is the life."
reallife_social_ride_talk_2: {first}: "Turn here! No, go on, you choose."
reallife_social_ride_talk_3: {first}: "The city looks smaller from a car, doesn't it?"
reallife_social_ride_talk_4: {first}: "You drive better than I thought you would."
reallife_social_ride_jolt_2: {first}: "I'd like to arrive in one piece, please."
reallife_social_ride_jolt_3: {first}: "That was my coffee. It's on your seat now."
reallife_social_ride_crash_1: {first}: "What was that? Are you trying to kill us both?"
reallife_social_ride_crash_2: {first}: "That's it. I'm never getting in a car with you again."
reallife_social_moving_talk_1: {first}: "Mind your back! That one's all books."
reallife_social_moving_talk_2: {first}: "Just there is fine. You're a machine."
reallife_social_moving_talk_3: {first}: "One more like that and I'll buy you two pizzas."
reallife_social_moving_nothing: {first}: "There's no room to put anything down out here. Forget the boxes, I'll get a van. Thanks for coming, though."
reallife_social_meet_coming: Somebody is walking up to you
reallife_social_dropby_coming: {first} has spotted you and is coming over
reallife_social_intro_coming: {first} is coming over, and has brought somebody
reallife_social_meet_gym_1: Hey! You were in the gym just now, weren't you? You've got good form. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_gym_2: Sorry to chase you down the street. I see you training in there all the time. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_work_1: Hey, you were on shift today too, right? I'm {first}. I thought I'd say hello while we're both standing still.
reallife_social_meet_work_2: You work round here as well, don't you? I've seen you at it. {first}. Good to finally meet you.
reallife_social_meet_cart_1: You again! We keep ending up at that coffee cart at the same time. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_cart_2: I know that face. The cart, most mornings. I thought I should introduce myself: {first}.
reallife_social_meet_neighbour_1: Hello! I think we're neighbours. I've seen you coming and going. I'm {first}, from along the hall.
reallife_social_meet_neighbour_2: Excuse me, you live in my building, don't you? I'm {first}. I thought it was time I said hello.
reallife_social_meet_helped_1: Wait! You're the one who stepped in back there. I wanted to say thank you properly. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_helped_2: Hey! I've been looking for you. What you did earlier, most people would have walked past. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_customer_1: It is you! You own the shop, don't you? I'm in there all the time. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_customer_2: Sorry to bother you. I shop at your place most weeks and I never see the owner. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_warm_1: Likewise! I'm {job}, I live over in {district}. We should grab a coffee some time.
reallife_social_meet_warm_2: You're friendlier than most people in this city. I'm {job}, by the way. {district} born and bred.
reallife_social_meet_warm_3: I had a feeling you'd be nice. I'm {job}, for my sins. I'm usually around {district}.
reallife_social_meet_cool_1: Not a talker. That's fine. I'm {job}, if you ever wonder. Anyway.
reallife_social_meet_cool_2: Right. Well. I'm {job}, I live in {district}. I just thought I'd say hello.
reallife_social_meet_numbers_1: Great, I've got you. I'll text so you have mine. See you around!
reallife_social_meet_numbers_2: Done. Now you can't say you don't know anyone. Take care!
reallife_social_meet_brushed_1: They shrug and walk away. "Suit yourself."
reallife_social_meet_brushed_2: "All right, all right. Only being friendly." They leave you to it.
reallife_social_meet_gaveup_1: Whoever it was gave up and walked on.
reallife_social_meet_gaveup_2: They waited a moment, thought better of it and left.
reallife_social_meet_no_numbers: You said goodbye without swapping numbers. Maybe you will run into them again.
reallife_social_intro_1: There you are! This is {name}, the friend I told you about. {first}, this is the one I keep going on about.
reallife_social_intro_2: Perfect timing. I want you to meet {name}. You two will get on, I can tell.
reallife_social_intro_3: Hey! Come and meet {name}. I've been meaning to put you two in the same place for weeks.
reallife_social_intro_hello: Hi! I'm {first}. I've heard a lot about you. Mostly good.
reallife_social_dropby_good_1: I was passing and thought I'd see how {shop} is doing. It looks busy in there!
reallife_social_dropby_good_2: So this is {shop}. People were queueing when I walked past. You must be raking it in.
reallife_social_dropby_quiet_1: I thought I'd come and see {shop} for myself. Quiet today, is it? It'll pick up.
reallife_social_dropby_quiet_2: I was in the area, so here I am. So this is {shop}. I like it.
reallife_social_dropby_street_1: I saw you from across the road. What are you up to out here?
reallife_social_dropby_street_2: Of all the streets in this city! I was just on my way home.
reallife_social_obj_early: You are early: {first} will be here about {time}
reallife_social_obj_park: Park up and walk over to {first}
reallife_social_obj_bring_car: Bring your car round: {first} is waiting
reallife_social_obj_no_room: No room for {first} to reach a door: move the car a little
reallife_social_obj_no_room_out: No room for {first} to get out here: move up a little
reallife_social_cut_short: Your time with {name} was cut short. No harm done.
reallife_social_cut_short_left: You left {name} standing there. They will remember that.
reallife_transaction_social_moving: A thank-you for helping with a move
reallife_social_invite_coffee: Coffee some time soon? I'm buying if you say yes quickly. Call me!
reallife_social_invite_meal: I'm hungry and I hate eating alone. Dinner? Ring me and we'll pick a time.
reallife_social_invite_drinks: It's been a week. I need a night out. Are you in? Call me.
reallife_social_invite_cinema: There's a film on I want to see and nobody to see it with. Call me?
reallife_social_invite_walk: Fancy a walk one of these days? Nothing fancy. Give me a ring.
reallife_social_invite_drive: Take me out for a drive some time? I never get out of this neighbourhood. Call me.
reallife_social_invite_workout: Gym this week? I need somebody to stop me skipping it. Call me and we'll fix a time.
reallife_social_invite_business: When do I get the tour of your business? I keep hearing about it. Ring me.
reallife_social_invite_lift: Any chance of a lift? Call me if you can.
reallife_social_invite_moving: I've got some boxes to shift. Call me if you've got an hour.
reallife_social_text_news_1: Just saw a dog on the subway wearing a raincoat. Thought you should know.
reallife_social_text_news_2: Long day. The coffee machine at work broke and nobody survived.
reallife_social_text_news_3: My landlord finally fixed the heating! Only took him a month.
reallife_social_text_news_4: I walked past a place that smelled like fresh bread and nearly cried. How's your day?
reallife_social_text_news_5: Guess who got a parking ticket this morning. Don't laugh.
reallife_social_text_news_6: I've decided to learn to cook. Wish my smoke alarm luck.
reallife_social_text_news_7: Work let us go early today. I don't know what to do with myself.
reallife_social_text_news_8: The lift in my building is stuck again. Seven floors. I'm counting it as exercise.
reallife_social_text_news_9: Somebody on my street is learning the trumpet. Pray for me.
reallife_social_text_news_10: Found twenty dollars in an old coat. Today is a good day.
reallife_social_text_news_11: It's {first}. Nothing to report, I just hadn't said hello in a while. Hello!
reallife_social_text_news_12: My boss said "good job" today. I'm having it framed.
reallife_social_text_badday_1: Rough day. Don't mind me. I just needed to tell somebody.
reallife_social_text_badday_2: Everything went wrong today. Tell me yours was better.
reallife_social_text_badday_3: Not my day. I'm going to bed early and starting again tomorrow.
reallife_social_text_cancel_1: I'm so sorry, I have to cancel. Work has kept me late. Can we do it another day? Call me.
reallife_social_text_cancel_2: Bad news: I can't make it. Something's come up at home. I'll make it up to you, call me.
reallife_social_text_cancel_3: I feel awful about this but I'm not going to make it today. Rain check? Ring me.
reallife_social_text_cancel_4: Don't hate me. I have to bail, my day has fallen apart. Call me and we'll rearrange.
reallife_social_text_cancel_rain_1: Have you seen the weather? I'm not walking in that. Another day? Call me.
reallife_social_text_cancel_rain_2: It's pouring. Let's not. Ring me when it's dry and we'll try again.
reallife_social_text_stoodup_1: I waited over an hour. You could at least have sent a message.
reallife_social_text_stoodup_2: So you're not coming. Good to know where I stand.
reallife_social_text_stoodup_3: I've gone home. I felt like an idiot standing there on my own.
reallife_social_text_stoodup_4: Is everything all right? You never showed up. I hope it was something serious, because I'm quite upset.
reallife_social_text_thanks_1: Home now. Thanks for today, I had a really good time.
reallife_social_text_thanks_2: That was fun. Let's do it again soon.
reallife_social_text_thanks_3: Still smiling. Thank you for today.
reallife_social_text_birthday_own_1: It's my birthday today! No pressure. (A little pressure.)
reallife_social_text_birthday_own_2: Guess what day it is. I'll give you a clue: there's cake. A call would be nice!
reallife_social_text_birthday_mom_1: Sweetheart, don't forget it's {name}'s birthday tomorrow. A call costs nothing.
reallife_social_text_birthday_mom_2: A little bird tells me {name} has a birthday tomorrow. I raised you to remember these things.
reallife_social_text_birthday_missed_1: It was my birthday yesterday. I suppose you were busy.
reallife_social_text_birthday_missed_2: Everyone called yesterday but you. It's fine. It's a bit not fine.
reallife_social_text_rich_kind_1: I hear business is booming. I'm so pleased for you. You've worked for it.
reallife_social_text_rich_kind_2: Look at you go! Don't forget us little people. Seriously though, well done.
reallife_social_text_rich_sour_1: Must be nice, having money to burn. Some of us are still counting coins.
reallife_social_text_rich_sour_2: I see you're doing very well for yourself. Don't go changing your number.
reallife_social_text_arrest_kind_1: I heard what happened. Are you okay? If you need anything, anything at all, call me.
reallife_social_text_arrest_kind_2: Whatever they say you did, I'm on your side. Ring me when you can.
reallife_social_text_arrest_stern_1: Arrested? Really? I don't know what to say to that.
reallife_social_text_arrest_stern_2: I heard about the police. I thought you were smarter than that.
reallife_social_text_arrest_mom_1: The police? I nearly dropped the phone. Call your mother this minute.
reallife_social_text_arrest_mom_2: I didn't raise you to see the inside of a cell. Are you eating? Call me.
reallife_social_text_crash_1: Somebody said you crashed on {street}. Tell me you're all right!
reallife_social_text_crash_2: I just heard about the accident on {street}. Are you hurt? Call me.
reallife_social_text_breakin_1: I just heard {shop} was broken into. I'm so sorry. Is there anything I can do?
reallife_social_text_breakin_2: A break-in at {shop}? That's horrible. Let me know you're okay.
reallife_social_text_missed_1: Tried to call you. Nothing urgent. Ring me back when you get a minute.
reallife_social_text_missed_2: You didn't pick up! Call me back, I've got something to ask you.
reallife_social_text_drift_1: Are you alive? It's been ages. Call me.
reallife_social_text_drift_2: I feel like I haven't heard from you in forever. Everything okay?
reallife_social_text_drift_3: Remember me? Your friend {first}? Pick up the phone some time.
reallife_social_text_loan_back_1: I've sent you the {amount} I owed. Thanks again for bailing me out.
reallife_social_text_loan_back_2: {amount}, back where it belongs. You're a good friend.
reallife_social_text_loan_excuse_1: About the {amount}. I haven't got it yet. A few more days, I promise.
reallife_social_text_loan_excuse_2: I know I owe you {amount}. Things are tight. Bear with me a bit longer?
reallife_social_text_debt_1: Hi. About the {amount} you borrowed. It's been a while now.
reallife_social_text_debt_2: I don't like to nag, but I do need that {amount} back.
reallife_social_text_home_1: I'll be home before you. Shall I put something on for dinner?
reallife_social_text_home_2: The flat feels empty without you in it. Come home soon.
reallife_social_text_home_3: We're out of milk. Also I love you. Mostly the milk, though.
reallife_social_text_love_1: Thinking about you. That's all. Carry on.
reallife_social_text_love_2: I saw something today that reminded me of you and now I can't stop smiling.
reallife_social_text_love_3: Hello, you. I hope today is being kind to you. Call me later?
reallife_social_text_breakup_1: I can't do this any more. We want different things, and I'm tired of waiting for you. I'm sorry.
reallife_social_text_breakup_2: This isn't working. You know it and I know it. Take care of yourself.
reallife_social_text_intro_1: You have to meet my friend {other}. Next time I catch you out on the street I'm bringing them over.
reallife_social_text_intro_2: I've told {other} all about you. You two should meet. I'll find you when you're out and about.
reallife_social_text_lift_1: I'm stranded. Any chance of a lift across town? Call me if you can come.
reallife_social_text_lift_2: My ride fell through. Could you drive me somewhere? Ring me, I'm outside now.
reallife_social_text_loan_1: Can I ask you something awkward? Call me when you've got a second.
reallife_social_text_loan_2: I need a small favour. A money one. Ring me?
reallife_social_text_moving_1: I'm moving a few boxes to my new place and I could use another pair of arms. Call me?
reallife_social_text_moving_2: Moving day is coming and I've nobody to help carry. I'll pay you in pizza. Ring me.
reallife_news_none: No paper has come yet. The City Ledger arrives every morning after 06:00.
reallife_news_end: That is all the news for today.
reallife_news_accident_minor_1: BUMP ON {street}. A light collision on {street} at about {time}. Nobody was hurt and the road was clear within minutes.
reallife_news_accident_minor_2: A minor collision held up traffic on {street} around {time}. Nobody was hurt, though a few words were exchanged.
reallife_news_accident_minor_3: Low-speed bump on {street}: police attended a minor collision at {time}. No injuries were reported.
reallife_news_accident_moderate_1: CRASH CLOSES {street}. An ambulance was called to a collision on {street} at about {time}. One person was treated at the scene.
reallife_news_accident_moderate_2: Traffic on {street} stood still for some time after a crash around {time}. Paramedics saw to the injured before the road reopened.
reallife_news_accident_moderate_3: Police taped off part of {street} at {time} after a collision. One driver was taken away for a check-up.

reallife_news_ped_killed_2: A person on foot was killed on {street} around {time}. Police have appealed for anyone who saw the collision.

reallife_news_crime_2: Residents of {street} reported {what} around {time}. Officers attended.
reallife_news_crime_3: {street}, {time}: {what}. "You don't expect it on your own street," said one passer-by.

reallife_news_quiet_1: A QUIET DAY. Police report no incidents of note since yesterday's edition. Enjoy it while it lasts.
reallife_news_quiet_2: Nothing to report from the streets: no crashes, no arrests, no sirens. The desk sergeant is said to have finished a crossword.
reallife_news_quiet_3: For once, the news is that there is no news. The city behaved itself yesterday.
reallife_news_quiet_4: A calm day and night across the city. Our crime reporter went home early.
reallife_news_rain_now_1: WEATHER: Rain this morning. Take an umbrella, and take the corners gently.
reallife_news_rain_now_2: WEATHER: Wet streets and grey skies to start the day. It should pass.
reallife_news_rained_1: WEATHER: Dry this morning after yesterday's rain. Mind the puddles.
reallife_news_rained_2: WEATHER: The rain has moved on. A brighter day is expected.
reallife_news_dry_1: WEATHER: Dry and settled. A good day to be out.
reallife_news_dry_2: WEATHER: No rain in sight. Clear skies over the city this morning.
reallife_news_dry_3: WEATHER: Fine and dry again. The umbrella sellers are not pleased.
reallife_news_shop_good_1: BUSINESS: {shop} on {street} took {amount} yesterday, a good day by any measure.
reallife_news_shop_good_2: BUSINESS: Trade was brisk at {shop}, {street}, where the tills rang up {amount} in a day.
reallife_news_shop_good_3: BUSINESS: One to watch: {shop} on {street} reports takings of {amount} for the day.
reallife_news_shop_loss_1: BUSINESS: A hard day for {shop} on {street}, which ended {amount} out of pocket.
reallife_news_shop_loss_2: BUSINESS: {shop}, {street}, lost {amount} on the day. Its owner will hope for better.
reallife_news_shop_none_1: BUSINESS: Shop rents held steady this week. Agents say good corners are still hard to find.
reallife_news_shop_none_2: BUSINESS: Wholesalers report steady demand. Small shopkeepers say the margins are as thin as ever.
reallife_news_shop_none_3: BUSINESS: Empty units are filling up downtown. "Somebody always thinks they can make it work," says one landlord.
reallife_news_breakin_1: BREAK-IN AT {shop}. Thieves forced their way into {shop} overnight. The damage is put at {amount}.
reallife_news_breakin_2: {shop} was broken into during the night. The repairs alone will cost {amount}, its owner says.
reallife_news_carbreakin_1: A parked car was broken into on {street} overnight. Police advise leaving nothing on the seats.
reallife_news_carbreakin_2: Car crime: a vehicle left on {street} was found with a window smashed in the morning.
reallife_news_playercrash_1: A motorist came to grief on {street} at about {time}. The vehicle looked the worse for it.
reallife_news_playercrash_2: One driver's day ended early on {street} around {time}, after an argument with something solid.
reallife_news_playerarrest_1: A local resident was taken into custody on {street} at about {time}. Police would not say more.
reallife_news_playerarrest_2: Police detained a member of the public on {street} around {time}, who then spent some hours as their guest.
reallife_news_playerknocked_1: A pedestrian was struck by a passing vehicle on {street} at about {time} and, by all accounts, got up again.
reallife_news_playerknocked_2: Traffic on {street} knocked a person off their feet around {time}. They are said to be recovering.
reallife_news_person_birthday_1: PEOPLE: Many happy returns to {name}, {job} from {district}, who has a birthday today.
reallife_news_person_birthday_2: PEOPLE: {name} of {district} is a year older today. Cards may be sent to the usual address.
reallife_news_person_job_1: PEOPLE: Our "faces of the city" column this week: {name}, {job}, who says {district} is the only place to live.
reallife_news_person_job_2: PEOPLE: Asked what the city needs, {name}, {job} from {district}, said: "Fewer car horns. More benches."
reallife_news_person_job_3: PEOPLE: {name}, {job}, tells us business is "the same as ever, which is to say busy".
reallife_news_person_seen_1: PEOPLE: Spotted about town yesterday: {name} of {district}, in good company.
reallife_news_person_seen_2: PEOPLE: {name}, {job} from {district}, was seen enjoying a day out. We approve.
reallife_news_noun_parking_ticket: a dispute over a parking ticket
reallife_news_filler_1: The pigeons of the financial district have learned to recognise lunch hour, a study of nobody in particular has found.
reallife_news_filler_2: A reader writes to ask why the hot-dog cart on his corner is never there when he is hungry. We have no answer.
reallife_news_filler_3: ON THIS DAY: nothing in particular happened, as far as our archive can tell.
reallife_news_filler_4: The city's oldest lift attendant retires this week after forty-one years. "It had its ups and downs," he said.
reallife_news_filler_5: LETTERS: "Sir, the benches in the park face the wrong way. I have said so before."
reallife_news_filler_6: A lost umbrella was handed in at our front desk. The owner may claim it by describing the handle.
reallife_news_filler_7: The subway authority promises the trains will run on time this week. We will let you know.
reallife_news_filler_8: RECIPE OF THE DAY: toast. Bread, heat, butter. Do not overthink it.
reallife_news_filler_9: A street musician on the avenue was asked to move on, then asked to come back. The crowd had followed him.
reallife_news_filler_10: HOROSCOPE: Today favours those who look both ways. Tomorrow also.
reallife_news_filler_11: The mayor's office denies that the new traffic lights are slower than the old ones. Drivers remain unconvinced.
reallife_news_filler_12: CLASSIFIED: For sale, one exercise bike, hardly used. Buyer collects. Seller will hold the door.
reallife_news_filler_13: A coffee cart on the east side claims the strongest cup in the city. Our reporter has not slept since.
reallife_news_filler_14: The annual count of city squirrels has been abandoned again. They would not stand still.
reallife_news_filler_15: LETTERS: "Madam, when I was young a sandwich cost a quarter. I do not know what else to tell you."
reallife_news_filler_16: A window cleaner on the thirtieth floor says the view is wasted on the people inside.
reallife_news_filler_17: CROSSWORD CLUE, 7 across: "What everybody is, in this city" (4). Answer tomorrow.
reallife_news_filler_18: The corner kiosk reports that sales of maps are down and sales of umbrellas depend entirely on the sky.
reallife_news_filler_19: A man who has fed the same pigeon for nine years admits he cannot be sure it is the same pigeon.
reallife_news_filler_20: THE LEDGER ASKS: what is the best street in the city? Answers on a postcard. Our own will not be considered.
reallife_news_filler_21: Road crews say the hole on the avenue will be filled by the weekend. They did not say which weekend.
reallife_news_filler_22: A doorman of thirty years' standing shares his secret: "Remember names. Forget everything else."
reallife_news_filler_23: CLASSIFIED: Wanted, a quiet flat. Present neighbour learning the trumpet.
reallife_news_filler_24: The chess players in the square have been at the same game since Tuesday. Neither will say who is winning.
reallife_news_filler_25: HOROSCOPE: A stranger may speak to you today. Consider speaking back.
reallife_news_filler_26: The parks department reminds citizens that the flowers are for looking at.
reallife_news_filler_27: LETTERS: "Sir, I was nearly run down on a crossing by a man eating a sandwich. Both hands."
reallife_news_filler_28: A cab driver claims to know every street in the city. Asked for the shortest route, he said: "There isn't one."
reallife_news_filler_29: The bakery on the corner sold out by nine again. The owner refuses to bake more, on principle.
reallife_news_filler_30: ON THIS DAY, some years ago, a reader found a parking space on the first attempt. A plaque is planned.
reallife_news_filler_31: A sweeper on the west side says the street is cleanest at six in the morning and it is all downhill from there.
reallife_news_filler_32: CLASSIFIED: Lost, one glove, left hand, sentimental value. Right hand lonely.
reallife_news_filler_33: The library reports that the most borrowed book this month is the one about getting rich. It is overdue.
reallife_news_filler_34: A florist says business rises sharply the day after a row. "I ask no questions," she adds.
reallife_news_filler_35: HOROSCOPE: Money comes and goes today. Mostly goes.
reallife_news_filler_36: The gym on the avenue reports its busiest week of the year. It expects to be quiet again by the next.
reallife_news_filler_37: LETTERS: "Madam, your weather forecast was wrong again. I enclose my wet hat."
reallife_news_filler_38: A courier claims a record: eleven floors, no lift, one parcel, under two minutes. The parcel was a pillow.
reallife_news_filler_39: The city's taxi drivers have voted, by a narrow margin, that the best time to drive is when nobody else is.
reallife_news_filler_40: THOUGHT FOR THE DAY: call somebody you have not spoken to in a while. They may be wondering.
