reallife_travel_depart_has_room: You have a hotel room in the city. Check out of it before you set off for the cottages.
reallife_travel_depart_hamptons: A bag on the back seat, the city in the mirror. The cottages are two hours out along the shore.
reallife_travel_depart_cruise: A cab drops you at the terminal. The ship stands over the pier like a white building; a steward takes your ticket and waves you up the gangway.
reallife_travel_depart_ski: An early cab to the airport, a short flight, a coach up a road with more bends than it has any right to. The air at the top is thin and sharp.
reallife_travel_depart_miami: A cab to the airport, three hours in the air, and the doors open on warm air that smells of salt and sunscreen.
reallife_travel_depart_europe: A cab to the airport and a night flight east. You watch the map on the seat-back until the ocean runs out.
reallife_travel_depart_tradefair: A cab to the airport with the first flight of the day, a lanyard waiting at the registration desk, and coffee that tastes of cardboard.
reallife_travel_trip_packed: Your suitcase is packed properly, for once.
reallife_travel_trip_unpacked: Everything you own for the trip is in two carrier bags.
reallife_travel_trip_no_money: You can't afford to splurge today.
reallife_travel_cancel_1: A storm front has closed the route: nothing is leaving today or tomorrow, and the operator has cancelled the whole departure.
reallife_travel_cancel_2: The carrier went on strike at midnight. The board is a wall of red, and your trip is off.
reallife_travel_cancel_3: The tour operator has gone bust overnight. A handwritten notice on the desk says so.
reallife_travel_cancel_4: A mechanical fault, then a missing crew, then an apology: your departure is cancelled outright.
reallife_travel_cancel_insured: Your insurance pays out in full: {amount} is back in your account.
reallife_travel_cancel_uninsured: Without insurance you get {amount} back and a lesson.
reallife_travel_ticket_expired: Your ticket for {trip} was never used and has expired. {amount} was refunded.
reallife_travel_hamptons_go: Your weekend has begun: {hotel} is yours until {day}. Drive out to the Hamptons or take the subway to the Hamptons station; the marker shows the way.
reallife_travel_hamptons_coach: The coach has brought you out to the Hamptons. {hotel} is yours until {day}; the marker shows the way.
reallife_travel_hamptons_missed: Your Hamptons weekend is over and you never slept a night at the cottage. Nothing comes back.
reallife_travel_hamptons_missed_insured: Your Hamptons weekend is over and you never slept a night at the cottage. Your insurance returned {amount}.
reallife_travel_return_hamptons: Sand in your shoes and salt in your hair: a weekend by the sea has done you good.
reallife_travel_return_cruise: The ship ties up where it started. Your legs still expect the floor to move.
reallife_travel_return_ski: You come down from the mountains with a goggle tan and thighs that ache in a satisfying way.
reallife_travel_return_miami: You come home a shade browner, with sand still in the lining of your bag.
reallife_travel_return_europe: Four cities, a dozen trains and more churches than you can tell apart. You come home with a head full of other people's streets.
reallife_travel_return_tradefair: Two days of handshakes and a pocket full of business cards. Some of it might even be useful.
reallife_travel_summary_days: Days away: {days}. The trip cost {spent} all told.
reallife_travel_summary_business: Your businesses made {total} while you were gone, {daily} a day; in the week before you left it was {before} a day.
reallife_travel_summary_business_new: Your businesses made {total} while you were gone, {daily} a day.
reallife_travel_summary_balance: Your balance has moved by {amount} since you left.
reallife_travel_summary_souvenirs: Souvenirs brought back to give away: {count}.
reallife_travel_summary_rested: You feel rested, and will for days.
reallife_travel_summary_jetlag: You feel rested, but your body is on another clock: expect jet lag for a day or two.
reallife_travel_summary_jetlag_first: You feel rested, and a flat bed on the way home took the worst off the jet lag.
reallife_travel_summary_fair: It was work, not rest, but you came back with ideas.
reallife_travel_text_friend_souvenir: You brought me something back! I love it. Next time take me with you.
reallife_travel_text_mom_souvenir: It arrived, sweetheart, and it's on the mantelpiece already. You shouldn't have. Tell me everything about the trip.
reallife_travel_fair_invite: An invitation has come: your trade's fair is coming up. Getaways Travel can book it for the next five days.
reallife_travel_burnout_friend_1: When did you last take a day off? An actual one? Go somewhere. A weekend in the Hamptons, anything.
reallife_travel_burnout_friend_2: You've been at it for weeks without a break. I'm saying this as your friend: book a holiday before you fall over.
reallife_travel_burnout_friend_3: Every time I call you're working. There's a travel agency in town, you know. Use it.
reallife_travel_burnout_doctor: You are worn out: weeks without a break are catching up with you, and everything feels heavier. A holiday, or a few lazy afternoons in a hotel room, would put it right.
reallife_travel_suggest_tired: You're dead on your feet. {hotel} is {metres} m away: a {room} is {rate} tonight.
reallife_travel_suggest_tired_driving: You're too tired to drive home. {hotel} is {metres} m away: a {room} is {rate} tonight.
reallife_travel_suggest_no_home: It's late and you have nowhere to sleep. {hotel} is {metres} m away: a {room} is {rate} tonight.
reallife_travel_suggest_locked_out: You can't get in tonight. {hotel} is {metres} m away: a {room} is {rate} tonight.
reallife_travel_trips_room: Hotel: {room} at {hotel}, nights after tonight: {nights}, checkout {time} on {day}.
reallife_travel_trips_ticket: Trip: a ticket for {trip}, days left on it: {days}.
reallife_travel_trips_weekend: Trip: your Hamptons weekend is under way.
reallife_travel_trips_fair: Trip: nothing booked. A trade fair invitation is open at Getaways Travel.
reallife_travel_trips_loyalty: Loyalty card: {stamps} of {need} stamps, free nights to use: {free}, hotel nights in all: {nights}.
reallife_travel_trips_hotel: {hotel} is {metres} m away: a {room} is {rate} tonight. It is marked for you.
reallife_travel_trips_no_hotel: There is no hotel to point you to.
reallife_travel_day_hamptons_1: Saturday at the cottage. The tide is out, the gulls are loud, and nobody knows where you are.
reallife_travel_day_hamptons_2: Sunday. Fog on the dunes first thing, burning off by ten. One more day before the city.
reallife_travel_day_cruise_1: First day at sea. The coast slides by to port; the deck chairs are filling up.
reallife_travel_day_cruise_2: The ship anchors off a harbour town. Launches run to the quay every half hour.
reallife_travel_day_cruise_3: Last day aboard. The captain's dinner is tonight, and the casino deck never closed.
reallife_travel_day_ski_1: First morning. Fresh snow overnight, blue sky, the lifts already humming.
reallife_travel_day_ski_2: Your legs remember yesterday. The mountain doesn't care; the top runs are open.
reallife_travel_day_ski_3: Cloud in the valley, sun above it. From the summit the world is a white sea with islands.
reallife_travel_day_ski_4: Last day. The snow is soft by noon and the terrace bars are doing good business.
reallife_travel_day_miami_1: First morning. The beach is thirty steps from the lobby and the sea is the colour of a swimming pool.
reallife_travel_day_miami_2: Already hot at nine. Pastel hotels, palm shadows, somebody's radio playing salsa.
reallife_travel_day_miami_3: Midweek. You have stopped checking your phone before breakfast.
reallife_travel_day_miami_4: A breeze off the water today. Kites up, pelicans working the shallows.
reallife_travel_day_miami_5: Last full day. The city back home feels like something you read about.
reallife_travel_day_europe_1: London, grey and enormous. Jet-lagged, you are on the pavement by seven with a paper cup of tea.
reallife_travel_day_europe_2: London still. Rain on and off; every second building has a plaque on it.
reallife_travel_day_europe_3: The train under the sea, and Paris at the other end: wide boulevards, tiny coffees.
reallife_travel_day_europe_4: Paris. The light on the river in the morning is the kind people paint.
reallife_travel_day_europe_5: South through the mountains to Florence. Terracotta roofs, bells, scooters.
reallife_travel_day_europe_6: On to Rome. Ruins in the middle of the traffic as if that were normal.
reallife_travel_day_europe_7: Last day in Rome. You throw the coin in the fountain like everybody else.
reallife_travel_day_tradefair_1: Day one. A hall the size of an airfield, a thousand stands, and a floor plan you can't fold back up.
reallife_travel_day_tradefair_2: Day two. Your feet hurt, your bag is full of brochures, and the good conversations happen in the coffee queue.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_1: A whole afternoon in a chair with a book you'd been meaning to read for a year.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_2: You fall asleep after lunch and wake up with no idea what day it is. Perfect.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_3: A long, slow breakfast that turns into lunch.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_4: You do nothing so thoroughly that you surprise yourself.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_5: You try to relax and catch yourself doing sums about work in your head. It takes most of the day to stop.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_6: A massage from somebody who clearly knows where shoulders keep their secrets.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_7: You order one drink with a little umbrella in it, then another. The bill has umbrellas on it too.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_8: An hour watching the light change. You can't remember when you last watched anything that slow.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_9: You stay out in the sun too long and spend the evening the colour of a lobster.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_10: A stranger at the next table tells you their life story. It's a good one.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_11: You sleep nine hours and wake up before the alarm you didn't set.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_12: For one whole day, nobody needs anything from you.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_1: You walk until the tourist streets run out and find where the locals actually eat.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_2: A wrong turn takes you up a hill to a view that isn't in any of the guidebooks.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_3: A market stall, an old man who won't haggle, and something small and handmade that had to come home with you.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_4: Somewhere in a crowd a hand finds your pocket. You notice an hour later.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_5: You pay for a guided tour. The guide is funnier than the sights.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_6: You get thoroughly lost and walk twice as far as you meant to.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_7: You stumble into a street festival: music, food on sticks, children with sparklers.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_8: A little shop down three steps sells exactly the thing a friend of yours has always wanted.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_9: It pours. You shelter in a doorway for an hour and your shoes take two days to dry.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_10: You find a banknote on the pavement and nobody near to have dropped it.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_11: You rent a bicycle and remember, wobbling, that you can ride one.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_12: A taxi takes the long way round and the meter takes the liberty.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_13: You talk your way on to a rooftop for the sunset. Worth every stair.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_14: A museum with an entrance fee and, it turns out, one good room.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_15: A cat adopts you for the length of a street and then has other business.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_16: You find a bench with a view and eat lunch out of a paper bag like a local.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_1: You walk out of a shop with a bag that has rope handles and tissue paper in it. No regrets.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_2: The tasting menu: eleven courses, each the size of a thumbnail, each astonishing.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_3: Presents for everyone back home. Your bag will barely close.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_4: You tip like a film star and are treated like one for the rest of the evening. It adds up.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_5: A day at the spa: you are steamed, scrubbed and wrapped like something precious.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_6: The famous restaurant turns out to be famous mostly for being famous.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_7: You buy the absurd hat, and something nearly as absurd for a friend.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_8: A flutter at the tables after dinner, and for once the house loses.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_9: You hire the convertible for the day. Sunglasses, radio, coast road.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_10: The bar with the view charges for the view. Separately.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_11: A shop that wraps everything beautifully. You buy things for the sake of the wrapping, and one for somebody at home.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_12: Front-row seats for a show you will be telling people about for years.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_1: {name} makes you laugh so hard at dinner that the next table asks what the joke was.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_2: {name} gets you both hopelessly lost and insists it's a shortcut. It somehow is.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_3: You and {name} stay up talking until the bar closes around you.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_4: You and {name} have a stupid argument about a map. It's forgotten by lunch, mostly.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_5: {name} takes forty photographs of you looking at things. Two are good.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_6: {name} says, out of nowhere, that this is the best trip they have ever had.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_7: {name} dares you to try the local speciality. You dare them back.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_8: Walking back late, {name} takes your arm, and neither of you says anything for a while. It's a good quiet.
reallife_travel_ev_hamptons_1: A farm stand on the back road: corn, tomatoes and a pie still warm.
reallife_travel_ev_hamptons_2: The sunset over the bay goes on for an hour and you watch every minute of it.
reallife_travel_ev_hamptons_3: A village shop sells you a striped jumper at a price that suggests the stripes are gold.
reallife_travel_ev_hamptons_4: You fall asleep on the porch to the sound of the surf.
reallife_travel_ev_cruise_1: Dolphins off the bow before breakfast. Half the ship is at the rail in dressing gowns.
reallife_travel_ev_cruise_2: A night of heavy swell. You discover which of your organs can float.
reallife_travel_ev_cruise_3: You are invited to the captain's table and he turns out to be very funny.
reallife_travel_ev_cruise_4: Bingo night in the lounge. You shout at the right moment.
reallife_travel_ev_ski_1: One perfect run, top to bottom without stopping, the snow hissing under you.
reallife_travel_ev_ski_2: You catch an edge and slide thirty yards on your back, collecting snow down your collar.
reallife_travel_ev_ski_3: Hot chocolate on a sun terrace two thousand metres up.
reallife_travel_ev_ski_4: A lesson with an instructor who fixes in an hour what you'd been doing wrong for years.
reallife_travel_ev_miami_1: You swim out past the breakers at sunrise and have the whole ocean to yourself.
reallife_travel_ev_miami_2: An afternoon thunderstorm clears the beach in ninety seconds flat.
reallife_travel_ev_miami_3: A pavement cafe, a tiny strong coffee and a sandwich pressed flat. You go back for a second.
reallife_travel_ev_miami_4: You sleep on the sand with a hat over your face and nobody wakes you.
reallife_travel_ev_europe_1: You turn a corner and there is the thing from every postcard, bigger than you imagined and entirely real.
reallife_travel_ev_europe_2: You board the wrong train and pay a fine in a language you don't speak.
reallife_travel_ev_europe_3: A bookshop by the river with a cat on the till. You buy something small for a friend.
reallife_travel_ev_europe_4: You climb four hundred steps to the top of a dome and the whole city is laid out underneath.
reallife_travel_ev_tradefair_1: A supplier you've been chasing for months turns out to be standing next to you in the coffee queue.
reallife_travel_ev_tradefair_2: A keynote that runs an hour over. You learn one thing, in the last five minutes.
reallife_travel_ev_tradefair_3: The exhibitors' dinner costs extra. Everyone who matters is there.
reallife_travel_ev_tradefair_4: You see a competitor's whole product line laid out on a stand and take very careful notes.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_1: Somebody nearby snored like a chainsaw until dawn. You barely slept.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_2: A group came in at three in the morning, singing. They did not stop singing.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_3: You wake up itching. Bedbugs. You wash everything you own twice.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_4: The radiator clanked all night like a ghost with a wrench.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_5: Your bag was open when you woke. A little cash is gone.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_6: The mattress has a spring with a grudge. You found it with your back.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_7: A fire alarm at four. False, but nobody tells your heartbeat that.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_8: The couple through the wall argued until two and made up until four.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_9: The neon sign outside the window buzzed and flickered on your eyelids all night.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_10: Half the floor was up talking until late, and one of them told a story so good you didn't mind.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_1: A newspaper outside the door and a handwritten card wishing you a good morning.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_2: Fresh coffee and warm pastries are sent up without your asking.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_3: Housekeeping has left a chocolate on the pillow and turned the lamps down just so.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_4: The manager sends up a bowl of fruit and a note thanking you for staying.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_5: Your shoes, left outside the door on a whim, have come back polished like mirrors.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_6: The doorman remembers your name. It should not matter, and it does.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_1: A mile of empty sand and the sea talking to itself.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_2: You find a whole sand dollar at the tide line, and it comes home in your pocket.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_3: A seal watches you from the surf for a while, deciding about you.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_4: The wind gets up and you walk back leaning into it, sand in your teeth.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_5: A folded banknote in the dune grass, soft with salt.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_6: The sun goes down red over the water and you stay until the last of it.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_7: Somebody's dog decides you are its friend and brings you a stick the whole length of the beach.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_8: A wave you didn't see coming soaks you to the knees.
reallife_careers_enabled: Careers: employers behind the help-wanted boards (a rota, reviews, promotions)
reallife_test_career_sign_on: Test: sign on with the next employer (cycles through all six)
reallife_test_career_shift: Test: work a shift at my current rank (goes on no record)
reallife_test_career_lead: Test: start a shift in charge
reallife_test_career_gig: Test: book a set at a nearby venue
reallife_contact_career_desc: Your employer, your rota and your CV
reallife_text_career_welcome: This is where work reaches you: shift reminders, letters from your employer, your rota and your CV. Employers hire in person, at the offices where the help-wanted boards stand. Call any time.
reallife_career_promo_pitch: Hi! Tasha, Brightline Promotions. We put paper in hands and smiles on faces, and we are always, always hiring. You'd start as a {title}: the flyer round you may know from the Gig Line, but on a rota, with {wage} an hour basic on top of what each flyer pays. Do well and you run a street team for me. {status}
reallife_career_promo_welcome: Love it! Welcome to Brightline. Your rota is {rota}. Clock on from your phone or right here, and bring the energy!
reallife_career_promo_review: Review time! Don't look so worried, I do these with a smile. Let's see how the streets have been treating you.
reallife_career_promo_notice: Oh, I'm sorry to lose you! Work {shifts} more shifts for me and you leave with my blessing and a proper reference.
reallife_career_promo_walkout: Just like that? Wow. Okay. I can't write anything nice about somebody who leaves me a team short. Bye.
reallife_career_cleaning_pitch: Dolores Whitlock. I run Brightside, and my floors are the cleanest in this city because I check every one. A {title} with us mops clients' floors, as on the Gig Line, but on a rota, with {wage} an hour basic on top of the pay per patch. The careful ones I make crew leads. {status}
reallife_career_cleaning_welcome: Good. Your rota is {rota}. Be on time, dear, and do the corners. I will know if you don't.
reallife_career_cleaning_review: Sit down, dear. I've been keeping notes, as I do for everybody. Let's go through them together.
reallife_career_cleaning_notice: I'm sorry to hear it, but thank you for telling me properly. {shifts} more shifts, done as well as the first, and I'll write you a reference I can stand behind.
reallife_career_cleaning_walkout: Mid-rota, with clients waiting? I'm disappointed. I write honest references, dear, and yours will be an honest one.
reallife_career_food_pitch: Lou! Everybody calls me Uncle Lou. I got carts all over town and not enough hands. You start as a {title}: my cart, my drinks, {wage} an hour basic and a wage for every customer you serve, tips are yours. Show me you can run a queue and I'll put you up for a licence: then you rent the cart by the day and what you take, you keep. Your first little business! {status}
reallife_career_food_welcome: Ha! Welcome to the family. Rota's {rota}. Smile at them, get the order right, and never, ever run out of lids.
reallife_career_food_review: Come here, come here, sit. I been watching the takings. Let's talk about how you been doing, eh?
reallife_career_food_notice: Ah, you're leaving your Uncle Lou. It happens. Give me {shifts} more shifts and I tell everybody in this town you're good people.
reallife_career_food_walkout: You walk off with the lunch rush coming? No, no, no. That I remember. Go on, get out of here.
reallife_career_retail_pitch: Good day. Anand Rao, area manager for Fairway Markets. We have a vacancy for a {title}: deliveries carried in from the kerb and shelved, on a fixed rota, at {wage} an hour basic in addition to the rate per box. There is a path from the stockroom to shift lead and to assistant manager for those who merit it; time at a shop till elsewhere is counted as experience. {status}
reallife_career_retail_welcome: Welcome to Fairway Markets. Your rota is {rota}. Punctuality is recorded, as is everything else. I trust we will not need to discuss it.
reallife_career_retail_review: Please, take a seat. This is your scheduled performance review. I have your figures in front of me.
reallife_career_retail_notice: Noted, with regret. Company policy is {shifts} further shifts. Complete them satisfactorily and a reference will be provided.
reallife_career_retail_walkout: That is a breach of your notice period. It will be recorded as such, and reflected in any reference we are asked for. Good day.
reallife_career_courier_pitch: Kowalski. I run this depot. I need a {title}: the parcel rounds you know, on a rota, {wage} an hour basic on top of the pay per door. Bring your own wheels or hire a van. Don't crash, don't get pulled over, don't be late. Seniors get the firm's van and the big rounds. After that there's the dispatch desk, and after that my job, if you live that long. {status}
reallife_career_courier_welcome: Fine. You're on. Rota's {rota}. Parcels don't deliver themselves and I don't chase people. Be here.
reallife_career_courier_review: Shut the door. Review. I don't do speeches, I do numbers. Here are yours.
reallife_career_courier_notice: Leaving. Right. {shifts} more shifts and I'll put my name to a reference. Miss one and I won't.
reallife_career_courier_walkout: With a van loaded? Get out. And don't put my name on anything.
reallife_career_cab_pitch: Sal DeMarco, Five Borough Cabs, talk fast because the meter's running. I take drivers with references, nobody else. {title}: four fares a shift off my dispatch, {wage} an hour basic on top of the fare, tips are yours. Keep them comfy, keep it clean, and I move you to the premium list: luxury car, picky riders, tips like you wouldn't believe. Top of the tree you're an owner-operator and most of the fare stays in your pocket. {status}
reallife_career_cab_welcome: Beautiful. Rota's {rota}. Smooth on the brakes, easy on the corners, and if the cops light you up it's on your file, not mine. Go, go.
reallife_career_cab_review: Sit, sit, two minutes, I got a radio going. Review. I got your sheet right here, let's go.
reallife_career_cab_notice: You're leaving me? Okay, okay, no hard feelings. {shifts} more shifts, clean, and Sal says nice things about you to anybody who calls.
reallife_career_cab_walkout: Now? With fares on the board? Unbelievable. You know what I tell people who call about you? Nothing good. Goodbye.
reallife_career_hire_ready: The job is yours if you want it.
reallife_career_no_off: Careers are switched off on the options page.
reallife_career_no_other: You are on the books at {value}. Work your notice there first.
reallife_career_no_banned: Not after how it ended last time. Days until you may ask again: {value}.
reallife_career_no_references: I can't take you on yet. Good references needed: {value}. A reference letter from gig work counts as one, and so does leaving an employer on good terms.
reallife_career_no_employer: You have no employer. Sign on at an office: look for the help-wanted boards.
reallife_career_rota_offer: Which rota suits you? I can offer {rota}, starting at {time}. A shift is about four hours. You can clock on up to two hours early; an hour late is a mark against you, and three marks and we part company.
reallife_career_status: {employer}. You are our {title}, on {wage} an hour basic plus what the work pays. Rota: {rota}. Next shift: {next}. Marks against you: {marks} of {most}. {note}
reallife_career_note_review: Your performance review is due: come to the office for it.
reallife_career_note_review_here: Your performance review is due: we can do it now.
reallife_career_note_notice: You are working your notice. Shifts to go: {left}.
reallife_career_clocked_on: You're clocked on. Watch the top of your screen.
reallife_career_other_2: Anything else? Your CV, or something about a job?
reallife_career_sick_ok: Sorry to hear it. Stay home: today's shift is excused. No mark against you, and no pay.
reallife_career_sick_no: You sound fine to me. If a doctor has signed you off, that's different; otherwise I expect you on your shift.
reallife_career_sick_excused: {employer}: you were off sick, so the missed shift is excused. No mark, no pay.
reallife_career_no_shift_today: You have no shift left to work today.
reallife_career_too_early: Your shift is at {time}. You can clock on up to two hours before it, not sooner.
reallife_career_too_late: That shift has gone. It is down as a no-show.
reallife_career_at_depot: This work is done at the office. Come to the help-wanted board outside it and clock on there.
reallife_career_leaving_ask: Leaving? Give notice and work {shifts} more shifts, and you go with a reference if your record earns one. Walk out now and the reference is marked down, and you won't be taken back for {days} days.
reallife_career_on_notice: You are working your notice. Shifts left: {left}. After that you leave on good terms, or you can walk out now with a marked-down reference.
reallife_career_review_numbers: Since we last sat down, shifts worked: {shifts}. On time for {ontime} of {due}; late {late}, missed {missed}. Tips from customers: {tips}. Shifts that ended in a complaint: {complaints}. Crashes on the job: {crashes}. Police stops on the job: {stops}.
reallife_career_review_promoted: That comes to {score} out of 100, and that is promotion material. From your next shift you are our {title}, on {wage} an hour basic.
reallife_career_review_raise: {score} out of 100. Solid. There's a raise in it: {wage} an hour basic from now on.
reallife_career_review_steady: {score} out of 100. Steady. Nothing to add, nothing to take away. Keep turning up on time and the next one could go better.
reallife_career_review_warning: {score} out of 100, and that is not good enough. It goes down as a mark against you: {marks} of {most}. Turn it round before the next review.
reallife_career_review_dismissed: {score} out of 100, on top of what was already on your file. We are letting you go, and the reference will say why. Don't ask again for {days} days.
reallife_career_review_due: {boss} wants a word: your performance review at {employer} is due. Go to the office.
reallife_career_freelance: You are freelance: no employer, no rota. Employers take you on at their offices, where the help-wanted boards stand, or here on the phone. References to your name: {references}.
reallife_career_gig_offer: A venue wants live music out front today: a set of eight songs, {fee} from the venue on top of whatever lands in your case, and people tip better at a booked set. Want it?
reallife_career_gig_booked: Booked: {venue}. It is marked on your map. Walk up to the front of it and the set begins. {fee} from the venue if you play at least half of it.
reallife_career_gig_booked_toast: Booked set at {venue}: {fee} from the venue plus the hat. Walk up to its front to begin.
reallife_career_gig_none: Nothing I can book near where you are. Try from another part of town.
reallife_career_gig_pending: You already have a set booked at {venue} today. Go and play it.
reallife_career_gig_no_level: Venues want somebody who can hold a crowd. Get to busker level {level} on the street first.
reallife_career_gig_no_today: One booked set a day. Ask again tomorrow.
reallife_career_gig_missed: You never turned up for your booked set. The venue found somebody else.
reallife_career_cv_letter_no: not yet (level 2 in any gig earns one)
reallife_career_cv_record_stop: stopped by the police while on a job in the last two days.
reallife_career_reminder: Shift at {employer} today at {time} ({title}). Clock on from your phone (Work) or at the office.
reallife_career_text_reminder: Reminder: you are on the rota today at {time} as {title}. Clock on by calling this number, or at the office. An hour late is a mark against you.
reallife_career_late: Late for your shift: an hour's basic pay docked, and a mark against you ({marks} of {most}).
reallife_career_noshow: You missed your shift at {employer}. {boss} has put a mark against you: {marks} of {most}.
reallife_career_text_noshow: {boss} here. You were on the rota and you did not show. That is mark {marks} of {most}. At {most} we are done.
reallife_career_dismissed_noshow: {employer} has let you go: three marks for lateness and missed shifts. {boss} has marked your reference down, and they will not take you back for {days} days.
reallife_career_dismissed_late: Late once too often. {employer} has let you go: three marks. {boss} has marked your reference down, and they will not take you back for {days} days.
reallife_career_text_dismissed: {boss}, {employer}. Your employment with us has ended. Your final pay has been made. Any reference we are asked for will reflect your record. Do not apply again within {days} days.
reallife_career_signed: Signed on with {employer} as {title}. Rota: {rota}. Your first shift is the next rota day.
reallife_career_text_signed: Welcome to {employer}. You start as {title}. Your rota: {rota}. Shift reminders will come to this number. Reviews are held at the office every three shifts.
reallife_career_left_good: You have worked your notice at {employer} and left with a good reference.
reallife_career_left_plain: You have worked your notice at {employer}. Too little on your file for a reference either way.
reallife_career_text_left_good: {employer}: thank you for working your notice. A good reference is on file for whoever asks. Good luck.
reallife_career_text_left_plain: {employer}: your notice is worked and you are off our books. We did not have enough to go on to write a reference.
reallife_career_text_review_due: {boss} here. Your performance review is due. Come to the office when you can; nothing moves on your pay or rank until we have had it.
reallife_career_mate_hello_1: {name} is on with you today. 'Morning! Kettle's just boiled if you're quick.'
reallife_career_mate_hello_2: {name} nods as you clock on. 'Oh good, it's you. Thought I was on my own again.'
reallife_career_mate_hello_3: {name} is already at it. 'There you are. Busy one today, they reckon.'
reallife_career_mate_hello_4: 'Hey, it's {name}. You on this shift too? Good. Makes it go quicker.'
reallife_career_cab_shift_done: That is your four fares. Shift done.
reallife_career_no_luxury: Premium work is done in a luxury car: a Mersaidi S500, a Lytte L6, a Petrolls. Come back at the wheel of one.
reallife_career_cart_no_money: You cannot cover today's rent on the cart. Come back when you can.
reallife_career_cart_rented: Cart rented for the day: {amount}. What you take today is yours.
reallife_career_test_top: Test: you are already at the top rank with this employer.
reallife_job_dispatch_foot_done: Your plan {km} km, best possible {best} km
reallife_job_dispatch_obj: Parcel {parcel} of {count}: which van? {key}: take one back
reallife_job_dispatch_obj_done: Planned: {km} km against a best of {best} km
reallife_job_dispatch_full: That van is full: three parcels a van.
reallife_job_dispatch_left: You walked away from the desk. The vans went out as they were.
reallife_job_dispatch_timeout: Out of time: the rest went on whichever van had room.
reallife_job_dispatch_great_1: A tight plan: hardly a wasted metre. {amount} for that batch.
reallife_job_dispatch_great_2: The drivers will thank you for that one. {amount}.
reallife_job_dispatch_fair_1: It will do: a van or two will double back. {amount}.
reallife_job_dispatch_fair_2: Not bad, not the best. {amount} for that batch.
reallife_job_dispatch_poor_1: Vans crossing each other all over the map. {amount}, and the drivers are muttering.
reallife_job_dispatch_poor_2: That plan burns fuel for nothing. {amount}, and a note on the desk.
reallife_job_lead_obj_round: Go and see how {name} is getting on
reallife_job_lead_obj_wait: Back to it. Something will come up
reallife_job_lead_obj_done: Shift over: the team are heading off
reallife_job_lead_see_fine: Head down, writing up the list: getting on with it, and well.
reallife_job_lead_see_slacking: A cigarette on the firm's time, and not the first by the look of it.
reallife_job_lead_see_stuck: Arms folded, waiting. Stuck on something and not saying so.
reallife_job_lead_right_fine: {name} grins. A word of thanks goes a long way.
reallife_job_lead_right_slacking: {name} stubs it out and gets back to it. Fair, and they know it.
reallife_job_lead_right_stuck: Two minutes of your time and {name} is moving again. That is the job.
reallife_job_lead_wrong_1: {name} gives you a look. That was not what the moment called for.
reallife_job_lead_wrong_2: Wrong call. {name} shrugs and carries on exactly as before.
reallife_job_lead_wrong_3: {name} says nothing, which says plenty. You misread that one.
reallife_job_lead_call_good_1: Handled. Nobody upstairs will ever hear about it, which is the point.
reallife_job_lead_call_good_2: Good call: quick, fair, and it is over.
reallife_job_lead_call_good_3: That is how it should be dealt with. The team noticed.
reallife_job_lead_call_ok_1: It will do. Not the neatest way out, but nobody is complaining.
reallife_job_lead_call_ok_2: Dealt with, more or less. It cost a bit more than it needed to.
reallife_job_lead_call_bad_1: That made it worse. Somebody is going to write that down.
reallife_job_lead_call_bad_2: Bad call. That one goes in the book as a complaint.
reallife_job_lead_call_bad_3: The team saw that, and so did the customer. Not your best moment.
reallife_job_lead_call_none: You said nothing and did nothing, and it sorted itself out badly.
reallife_job_lead_left: You walked off and left the team to it. That is not a shift in charge.
reallife_job_lead_time: End of the shift: whatever was not dealt with is the next lead's problem.
reallife_job_lead_inc_late: A delivery is an hour late and the client is on the phone, furious. What do you do?
reallife_job_lead_inc_row: Two of the team are having a shouting match where the customers can hear every word.
reallife_job_lead_inc_short: Somebody has called in sick and the next two hours are one pair of hands short.
reallife_job_lead_inc_spill: Something has been spilt right by the door, and people are walking straight through it.
reallife_job_lead_inc_count: The cash count is twenty short, and three people have been near the box today.
reallife_job_lead_inc_refund: A customer wants their money back and you are not sure they are owed it.
reallife_business_enabled: Business pressure: rivals, inspections, staff and supplier trouble, opportunities (listed on the Business desk contact)
reallife_business_frequency: How often something comes up (1 = about one day in twelve, 10 = about one day in three; never more than two open at once)
reallife_business_easy: Easy business: only the opportunities (bulk orders, press features, praise, awards)
reallife_business_rivals: Rival moves: a competitor undercuts you, an offer to one of your staff, a smear in the paper
reallife_business_racket: Protection racket: pay, refuse, go to the police, or rely on your security
reallife_business_inspections: Inspections: health (food businesses), fire safety, licence renewal
reallife_business_staff: Staff trouble: a strike threat over low wages, theft caught on camera, an argument to settle
reallife_business_suppliers: Supplier trouble: a late delivery, a surcharge
reallife_business_customers: Customer incidents: a complaint or praise that spreads
reallife_business_opportunities: Opportunities: a bulk order, a feature in the paper, an award
reallife_test_business_rivals: Test: next rival move at the business I am in (or my first)
reallife_test_business_racket: Test: the protection racket makes its demand
reallife_test_business_inspections: Test: next inspection (health, fire safety, licence)
reallife_test_business_staff: Test: next staff trouble (strike threat, theft, argument)
reallife_test_business_suppliers: Test: next supplier trouble (late delivery, surcharge)
reallife_test_business_opportunities: Test: next opportunity (bulk order, press feature, award)
reallife_test_business_resolve: Test: resolve all (close every issue, undo every footfall change and closure, forget the racket)
reallife_text_business_welcome: Business desk. Whatever comes up at your businesses is listed here with its deadline: competitors, inspectors, staff, suppliers, the odd piece of good news. Call to see what is open and to decide what to do about it. Nothing is decided for you before its deadline.
reallife_biz_desk_off: Business pressure is switched off on the options page.
reallife_biz_desk_empty: Nothing is open at your businesses. If something comes up it will be listed here, with its deadline.
reallife_biz_desk_empty_easy: Nothing is open. 'Easy business' is on: only opportunities will come up.
reallife_biz_cannot: That cannot be done right now: not enough money, or what it needs is not in place. Nothing has changed; choose again.
reallife_biz_staff_gone: The person concerned no longer works for you. There is nothing left to decide.
reallife_biz_test_no_business: Business test: you run no business that takes money yet.
reallife_biz_test_busy: Business test: {business} already has an open issue. Deal with it on the Business desk, or use 'resolve all'.
reallife_biz_test_kind_open: Business test: '{issue}' is already open at one of your businesses.
reallife_biz_test_failed: Business test: '{issue}' could not be started (see Player.log).
reallife_biz_test_resolved: Business test: every open issue was closed, every footfall change and closure put back, and the racket forgotten.
reallife_biz_why_no_footfall: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: its customer numbers cannot be changed now (it has no promotion figure, is temporarily closed, already has a change running, or its figure is too near 0 or 100).
reallife_biz_why_game_rival: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: one of the game's own rivals is already active in this neighbourhood.
reallife_biz_why_no_rival: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: the game's rivals are switched off, or none of them owns a business.
reallife_biz_why_no_staff: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: it needs an employee assigned there (for a rival's offer, one with no offer or complaint open).
reallife_biz_why_two_staff: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: it needs two employees assigned there.
reallife_biz_why_paid_well: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: the staff are paid at or near the going rate.
reallife_biz_why_no_theft: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: this kind of business has no stock to steal.
reallife_biz_why_no_camera: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: there is no camera to catch it on (security level under 10).
reallife_biz_why_not_food: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: health inspections are for food businesses.
reallife_biz_why_no_cash: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: you have no cash to pay its fee from.
reallife_biz_why_no_delivery: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: it has no wholesale delivery due in the next two days.
reallife_biz_why_doing_well: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: its customers have nothing to complain about.
reallife_biz_why_not_good_enough: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: its satisfaction and cleanliness are not high enough to earn it.
reallife_biz_why_no_books: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: there is not a week of books to audit yet.
reallife_biz_why_small: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: it takes too little a day to be worth anybody's while.
reallife_biz_why_racket_on: Business test: the racket is already under way. See the Business desk.
reallife_biz_why_racket_over: Business test: the racket ended with an arrest and is over for good in this save ('resolve all' forgets that).
reallife_biz_why_resting: Business test: '{issue}' was not started at {business}: it happened too recently.
reallife_biz_undercut_start: {rival} has opened near {business} and is undercutting you. Expect about {percent}% fewer customers for {length} days. Your Business desk has ways to answer it.
reallife_biz_undercut_marketing: A week of leaflets and local adverts: {amount}. It cancels the dip at once and brings a few extra customers in for three days.
reallife_biz_undercut_price: Match their opening offers for the week: {amount} in margin. The dip is halved for as long as it lasts.
reallife_biz_undercut_quality: Costs nothing: regulars come back to a clean shop that serves them well, and the dip is over in two days. It needs cleanliness of 80 (yours is {clean}) and customer satisfaction of 60 (yours is {satisfaction}).
reallife_biz_undercut_ride: Do nothing. The dip runs its {length} days and ends by itself.
reallife_biz_undercut_marketing_done: The push worked: {business} is busier than before the competitor opened. A few more customers than usual for three days.
reallife_biz_undercut_price_done: You matched them. {business} keeps most of its customers: the dip is half what it was.
reallife_biz_undercut_quality_done: Your regulars tried the new place and came back. The dip at {business} will be gone in two days.
reallife_biz_undercut_rode: {business} is riding out the competition. The dip ends on its own.
reallife_biz_poach_name: A rival wants one of your staff
reallife_biz_poach_start: A rival has made {name} at {business} an offer: {amount} an hour, {percent}% more than you pay. Answer it in {name}'s messages (Contacts): match the offer, or let them go.
reallife_biz_poach_kept: {name} is staying at {business}: the rival's offer was matched.
reallife_biz_smear_start: The local paper has run a nasty piece about {business}: unnamed sources, no proof. Expect about {percent}% fewer customers for {length} days.
reallife_biz_smear_reply: Pay a PR writer {amount} to get your side printed tomorrow. The dip ends at once.
reallife_biz_smear_lawyer: {amount} for a lawyer's letter demanding a retraction. A little better than even odds: if the paper backs down the dip ends and the correction brings a few customers in; if not, the money is gone.
reallife_biz_smear_ignore: Say nothing. The story fades in {length} days.
reallife_biz_smear_reply_done: Your reply ran on page three. The story is dead and trade at {business} is back to normal.
reallife_biz_smear_lawyer_won: The paper printed a retraction. Trade at {business} is back, and a little better than usual for two days.
reallife_biz_smear_lawyer_lost: The paper's lawyers wrote back: they stand by the story. It will have to fade by itself.
reallife_biz_smear_ignored: You let the story about {business} run. It will be forgotten in a few days.
reallife_biz_racket_start: A man came to {business} to say the neighbourhood is not safe, and that for {amount} a week it could be. Days left to answer: {days}. Your Business desk has the choices.
reallife_biz_racket_pay: {amount} now and every week after. Cheap, and nothing will happen to the shop. But what he asks creeps up week by week, to half as much again.
reallife_biz_racket_refuse: Tell him no. He may do nothing. Or, in a few days, a window goes in: a repair bill and the shop shut for a few hours. Good security makes that much less likely (your security level is {security}).
reallife_biz_racket_police: Report him. The police take three days to build a case, and cameras and guards are their evidence: your security level of {security} decides the odds. If they get him he is arrested and it is over for good. If they do not, he will know that you talked.
reallife_biz_racket_security: Put him off and see to your security instead: hire a guard, fit cameras. In three days, if the shop's security level is 50 or more (it is {security}), he decides you are not worth the trouble. If it is not, he takes it as a no.
reallife_biz_racket_paying: You paid. {amount} a week, collected every seven days. From your Business desk you can stop, or go to the police.
reallife_biz_racket_refused: You said no. He left without a word.
reallife_biz_racket_reported: The police have opened a file. They will be in touch in three days.
reallife_biz_racket_securing: You have three days to get the shop's security level to 50.
reallife_biz_racket_collected: The collector has been to {business}: {amount} paid. Next week he wants {next}.
reallife_biz_racket_short: You could not pay the collector at {business}. He took it as a no.
reallife_biz_racket_vandal: Overnight somebody put a brick through the window of {business}. Repairs: {amount}.
reallife_biz_racket_vandal_closed: Overnight somebody put a brick through the window of {business}. Repairs: {amount}, and the shop is shut for {hours} hours while the glass is replaced.
reallife_biz_racket_quiet: Nothing came of the threat at {business}. He has not been back.
reallife_biz_racket_sting_set: The police have a case. They want the collector caught taking money: he will come to {business} tomorrow at {time}. Be in the shop if you want to see it; they will take him either way.
reallife_biz_racket_no_case: The police could not build a case: not enough on camera at {business}. And he has heard that you talked.
reallife_biz_racket_ended: The collector has been arrested at your shop. The racket is over, for good.
reallife_biz_racket_ended_away: The police arrested the collector at {business} this afternoon. The racket is over, for good.
reallife_biz_racket_backed_off: The collector took one look at the security at {business} (level {security}) and has not been back.
reallife_biz_racket_not_secure: The collector came back to {business}. Its security level is {security}, short of the {need} that would have put him off: he takes it as a no.
reallife_biz_racket_page_paying: Protection at {business}: you are paying {amount} a week. Next collection: day {day}. You can stop paying (he will take it as a refusal) or go to the police.
reallife_biz_racket_page_refused: Protection at {business}: you refused. Whatever he means to do about it, he will do within days. Security level: {security}.
reallife_biz_racket_page_reported: Protection at {business}: the police are building their case. They will be in touch on day {day}.
reallife_biz_racket_page_sting: Protection at {business}: the police will be waiting for the collector on day {day} at {time}. Be in the shop to see it.
reallife_biz_racket_page_securing: Protection at {business}: he comes back on day {day}. Security level {security}; at {need} he will think better of it.
reallife_biz_health_start: The health inspector will call at {business} tomorrow at {time}. They look at one thing: how clean the place is. It is at {clean} of 100 now; {pass} is a pass.
reallife_biz_health_again: The health inspector comes back to {business} on day {day} at {time}. Cleanliness is at {clean}; it must be {pass}.
reallife_biz_health_clean: A contract crew goes through the place for {amount}: most of the dirt gone before the inspector comes. (Or have your own cleaners see to it, or pick up the mop.)
reallife_biz_health_clean_done: The contract crew has been through {business}: cleanliness is now {clean}. The inspector still calls.
reallife_biz_health_pass: {business} passed its health inspection ({clean} of 100). The certificate goes in the window: a few more customers for three days.
reallife_biz_health_warning: The health inspector is not satisfied with {business}: cleanliness {clean}, and {pass} is needed. To put right: the floors. They will be back on day {day}.
reallife_biz_health_fail_closed: {business} failed its health inspection (cleanliness {clean}). Fine: {amount}, and the shop is closed for {hours} hours to be cleaned.
reallife_biz_fire_start: The fire-safety officer will call at {business} tomorrow at {time}. They check that the floor is clear (cleanliness {clean}, needs {pass}) and that the fittings are in order (facility score {facility}, needs {need}).
reallife_biz_fire_check: A fire-safety contractor walks the shop and puts right what they find: {amount}. A pass is then certain.
reallife_biz_fire_check_done: The contractor has been through {business} and signed it off. The inspection will pass.
reallife_biz_fire_pass: {business} passed its fire-safety inspection. The certificate goes on the wall: a few more customers for three days.
reallife_biz_fire_list_both: clutter on the floor (cleanliness {clean}, needs {pass}) and fittings below standard (facility score {facility}, needs {need})
reallife_biz_fire_fail: {business} failed its fire-safety inspection. To put right: {list}. Fine: {amount}.
reallife_biz_fire_fail_closed: {business} failed its fire-safety inspection. To put right: {list}. Fine: {amount}, and the shop is closed for {hours} hours.
reallife_biz_licence_start: The trading licence of {business} is up for renewal: {amount}, to be paid by day {day}, {time}. Late renewal costs half as much again.
reallife_biz_licence_paid: The trading licence of {business} is renewed.
reallife_biz_licence_late: The trading licence of {business} was renewed late: {amount} with the late fee.
reallife_biz_licence_closed: The trading licence of {business} lapsed and the late fee could not be paid. The shop is closed for {hours} hours while it is sorted out.
reallife_biz_strike_start: The staff of {business} say they are underpaid, and by the going rate they are right. The {count} of them want {raise} an hour more between them, or they walk out. Days left to answer: {days}.
reallife_biz_strike_raise: Bring every underpaid wage up to just under the going rate (never more than 15% at once): {raise} an hour more on the wage bill, for good.
reallife_biz_strike_bonus: A day's wages each as a bonus: {amount} now. It buys peace for a while; the wages stay where they are.
reallife_biz_strike_refuse: Tell them no. Even odds: they back down, sore about it; or they walk out and the shop is shut for {hours} hours.
reallife_biz_strike_raised: You agreed the raise at {business}. The staff are back at work, and happier.
reallife_biz_strike_bonus_done: The bonus went down well at {business}. The talk of a walkout has stopped, for now.
reallife_biz_strike_walkout: The staff of {business} have walked out. The shop is shut for {hours} hours.
reallife_biz_strike_backed_down: The staff of {business} have backed down. Nobody is happy about it.
reallife_biz_stafftheft_start: The camera at {business} has caught {name} taking from the till: {amount} gone, booked as theft. What do you do about it?
reallife_biz_stafftheft_dismiss: {name} goes today. You will be a pair of hands short until you hire again.
reallife_biz_stafftheft_warn: A formal warning. {name} stays, chastened; sometimes the money comes back.
reallife_biz_stafftheft_forgive: Say nothing. {name} stays, and nothing changes.
reallife_biz_stafftheft_repaid: {name} took the warning to heart and paid the money back.
reallife_biz_stafftheft_warned: {name} has had a final warning. The money is gone.
reallife_biz_stafftheft_forgiven: You let it go. {name} is still at {business}.
reallife_biz_argument_start: {name} and {other} at {business} have fallen out badly, and the customers have noticed. Each wants you on their side.
reallife_biz_argument_first: Take {name}'s side. {name} will be pleased; {other} will not forget it.
reallife_biz_argument_second: Take {other}'s side. {other} will be pleased; {name} will not forget it.
reallife_biz_argument_lunch: Sit them both down over lunch, on you: {amount}. Both come back in a better mood.
reallife_biz_argument_sided: You took {name}'s side. {other} is sour about it.
reallife_biz_argument_lunch_done: Lunch did it. {name} and {other} are talking again.
reallife_biz_argument_festered: Nobody dealt with the row at {business}. Both of them are unhappier for it.
reallife_biz_supplierlate_start: The wholesaler for {business} says the next delivery will be a day late (a lorry off the road) unless you pay {amount} for an express run. Answer today.
reallife_biz_supplierlate_express: {amount} for a courier run: the delivery comes on its day.
reallife_biz_supplierlate_wait: The delivery comes one day later. Watch the shelves.
reallife_biz_supplierlate_express_done: Express paid. The delivery to {business} comes on its day.
reallife_biz_supplierlate_waited: The delivery to {business} will come a day late.
reallife_biz_supplierprice_start: The wholesaler for {business} is adding a fuel surcharge to the next delivery: {amount}. Days left to answer: {days}.
reallife_biz_supplierprice_pay: Pay the {amount} and keep the delivery as it is.
reallife_biz_supplierprice_haggle: Call the rep and argue it. Your negotiation skill decides the odds: win and the surcharge is dropped; lose and you pay the {amount} anyway.
reallife_biz_supplierprice_switch: Move the order to another haulier: {amount} in paperwork, and this delivery comes a day late.
reallife_biz_supplierprice_paid: Surcharge paid. The delivery to {business} is unchanged.
reallife_biz_supplierprice_haggled: You talked the rep out of it. No surcharge for {business}.
reallife_biz_supplierprice_haggle_failed: The rep would not budge: the surcharge was paid.
reallife_biz_supplierprice_switched: The order for {business} has moved to another haulier. This delivery comes a day late.
reallife_biz_complaint_start: A customer's complaint about {business} is doing the rounds online. It is about your {figure}, which is your weakest point. Expect about {percent}% fewer customers for {length} days.
reallife_biz_complaint_voucher: A public apology and a voucher for the customer: {amount}. The story turns in your favour and the dip ends.
reallife_biz_complaint_ignore: Say nothing. It blows over in {length} days. (Raising your {figure} is what stops the next one.)
reallife_biz_complaint_voucher_done: The customer posted a thank-you. The complaint about {business} is forgotten.
reallife_biz_complaint_ignored: You did not answer the complaint about {business}. It will blow over.
reallife_biz_praise_start: A customer's glowing review of {business} is being passed around. About {percent}% more customers for {length} days.
reallife_biz_praise_share: Put it in the window and pass it on. It keeps bringing people in for five days instead of three.
reallife_biz_praise_shared: You shared the review. {business} stays busier for a couple of days longer.
reallife_biz_audit_start: The tax office has picked {business} for a spot audit of its books. You can go in with an accountant ({amount}) or on your own. Days left to answer: {days}.
reallife_biz_audit_accountant: {amount} for an accountant to sit beside you. Most audits then find nothing; if they do find something, it is a third of what it would have been.
reallife_biz_audit_alone: No fee. It may go cleanly; you may be handed an adjustment of up to {amount}; now and then they find they owe you.
reallife_biz_audit_clean: The audit of {business} found nothing. Your books are in order.
reallife_biz_audit_clean_accountant: With the accountant beside you, the audit of {business} found nothing.
reallife_biz_audit_adjusted: The audit of {business} found an error in the tax office's favour. Adjustment paid: {amount}.
reallife_biz_audit_refund: The audit of {business} found that you had overpaid. Refund: {amount}.
reallife_biz_bulkorder_start: An office nearby wants a bulk order from {business}: {amount}, collected tomorrow at {time}. The shop has to be open when they come.
reallife_biz_bulkorder_accepted: Bulk order accepted at {business}: {amount}, collected on day {day} at {time}. Be open.
reallife_biz_bulkorder_accept: Take it. {amount} when they collect, as long as the shop is open at that hour.
reallife_biz_bulkorder_decline: Turn it down. Nothing gained, nothing lost.
reallife_biz_bulkorder_taken: Order taken. They collect from {business} on day {day} at {time}: be open.
reallife_biz_bulkorder_declined: You turned the bulk order down.
reallife_biz_bulkorder_done: The bulk order was collected from {business}: {amount}.
reallife_biz_bulkorder_missed: They came for the bulk order and found {business} shut. The order went elsewhere.
reallife_biz_bulkorder_lapsed: The bulk order for {business} went to somebody who answered.
reallife_biz_feature_start: The local paper wants to run a feature on {business} and would like to talk to the owner. Free publicity, if you give them the time.
reallife_biz_feature_accept: Give them half an hour. The feature brings in about 8% more customers for three days.
reallife_biz_feature_done: The feature on {business} is in today's paper. About {percent}% more customers for {length} days.
reallife_biz_feature_lapsed: The paper ran its feature on somebody else.
reallife_biz_award_start: {business} has been named Local Business of the Month: the neighbourhood association has noticed how well it is run. There is a prize of {amount}.
reallife_biz_award_accept: Collect the plaque and the {amount} prize. A plaque in the window brings a few more customers for four days.
reallife_biz_award_done: The plaque is in the window of {business}, and the prize is in the bank.
reallife_biz_visit_collector_1: 'Nice place. Be a shame if the neighbourhood got rough. Let's talk about keeping it nice.'
reallife_biz_visit_collector_2: 'You the owner? Good. I look after the shops round here. Yours isn't on my list yet.'
reallife_biz_visit_collector_3: 'Lot of glass in this shopfront. Glass is expensive. I can make sure nothing happens to it.'
reallife_biz_visit_inspector_1: 'I've seen what I need to. You'll have my findings on your Business desk within the hour.'
reallife_biz_visit_inspector_2: 'That's the walk-round done. My report follows shortly. Good day.'
reallife_biz_visit_inspector_3: 'All noted. You will hear from the office within the hour.'
reallife_biz_visit_sting_1: 'It's that day of the week. You have something for me.'
reallife_biz_visit_sting_2: 'Collection day. Let's not make this take long.'
reallife_biz_visit_police: 'Police! Hands where I can see them!' An officer has come in behind him.
reallife_biz_visit_police_outside: He never makes it out of the door: the police were waiting outside.
reallife_character_skin: Finer skin on your character up close: a fine grain and a calmer shine, most on dark skin (subtle)

reallife_looks_legs_m_colour: Trousers colour (men; a print the garment cannot carry shows as a plain colour)
reallife_looks_dress_f_colour: Dress colour (women; a print the garment cannot carry shows as a plain colour)
reallife_looks_top_f_colour: Top colour (women; a print the garment cannot carry shows as a plain colour)
reallife_looks_legs_f_colour: Trousers or skirt colour (women; a print the garment cannot carry shows as a plain colour)

reallife_garage_police: A straight-through exhaust or riding without a helmet can be fined
reallife_garage_two_wheelers: Bicycles and motorbikes (bike-share docks, racks outside supermarkets, stands at car dealerships)
