reallife_garage_test_random: Test: put a random full build on my current or nearest car (free)
reallife_garage_test_restore: Test: restore my current or nearest car to stock
reallife_garage_test_vehicles: My vehicles: every build, and where each two-wheeler stands
reallife_garage_test_built: A random build is on the car. The restore test takes it off again.
reallife_garage_test_stock: The car is as it left the dealer.
reallife_keys_garage: Garage: the custom shop in a repair bay; hire, return and buy two-wheelers
reallife_test_refused_in_vehicle: Test not started: get out of the vehicle first.
reallife_test_refused_no_room: Test not started: the ground two metres in front of you is not clear.
reallife_test_refused_no_car_near: Test not started: you are not in a car, and no car of yours is within {metres} metres.
reallife_test_refused_not_a_car: Test not started: the custom shop only works on cars, vans and trucks.
reallife_test_refused_not_yours: Test not started: that vehicle belongs to a job or a hire company, not to you.
reallife_garage_refused_not_a_car: The custom shop only works on cars, vans and trucks.
reallife_garage_refused_not_yours: The custom shop only works on vehicles you own.
reallife_garage_work_note: Work is done while you wait. Leaving without paying puts the car back as it came in.
reallife_garage_cannot_afford: You cannot afford that: it comes to {amount}.
reallife_garage_paid: Custom shop: {amount} paid. The car is ready.
reallife_garage_no_paint: This vehicle's bodywork cannot be repainted.
reallife_garage_paint_factory: The colour it was bought in
reallife_garage_paint_mix_note: Move the three sliders to mix a colour of your own.
reallife_garage_finish_note: A finish changes how the whole body catches the light: a matte car has matte glass and trim too.
reallife_garage_glow_header: Underglow kit ({price}; another colour later costs a quarter)
reallife_garage_glow_note: Lit here so you can see it. On the road it comes on after dark.
reallife_garage_wheels_none: The shop has no other wheels in stock for this car.
reallife_garage_parts_off: Performance parts are switched off on the options page.
reallife_garage_fig_to100: 0-100 km/h: {from} s, with this build {to} s
reallife_garage_fig_top: Top speed: {from} km/h, with this build {to} km/h
reallife_garage_fig_stop: Stops from 100 km/h in {from} m, with this build {to} m
reallife_garage_fig_illegal: The exhaust is not street legal.
reallife_garage_fig_none: Sit in the car with "Realistic car performance" switched on to see acceleration and top speed here.
reallife_garage_fine_exhaust: The police stopped you over the noise of your exhaust: {amount} fine.
reallife_garage_summary_hired: {name}: on hire from a bike-share dock
reallife_garage_summary_none: None of your cars has been to the custom shop, and you have no bicycle or motorbike.
reallife_bike_facts_bicycle: Pedal power: about {speed} km/h on the flat. Pedalling uses energy. No licence.
reallife_bike_facts_motor: 0-100 km/h in {seconds} s, top speed {top} km/h. Helmet and motorcycle licence required.
reallife_bike_helmet_note: Worn whenever you ride a motorbike. Riding without one can be fined.
reallife_bike_collected: The bike-share company collected the bicycle you did not bring back: {amount} late fee.
reallife_bike_no_room: There is no clear ground beside this stand right now.
reallife_bike_no_licence: You hold no motorcycle licence. Take the ride assessment at a driving school desk before you ride: police fine riders without one and tow the bike.
reallife_bike_tired: You are worn out: you cannot push the pedals as hard until you have rested or eaten.
reallife_bike_fine_helmet: The police stopped you for riding without a helmet: {amount} fine.
reallife_justice_enabled: Courts: an arrest or a serious charge opens a case (bail, a court date, a verdict, a sentence)
reallife_justice_lawyers: The city's law firms can be retained (off: the public defender or yourself)
reallife_justice_courthouse: Hearings are attended in person at the courthouse (off: by video link from the Legal file)
reallife_justice_no_prison: No prison: fines and custody only
reallife_justice_community: Community service is a played shift (off: it becomes a fine)
reallife_justice_civil: People you crash into may sue (one claim at a time)
reallife_justice_aftermath: Appeals, record sealing and compensation for a wrongful arrest
reallife_justice_phone: Legal contact on the phone (opens the Legal file)
reallife_justice_test_case_minor: Test: open a case against me (evading the police)
reallife_justice_test_case_serious: Test: open a case against me (hit-and-run with an injury)
reallife_justice_test_case_grave: Test: open a case against me (fatal hit-and-run)
reallife_justice_test_case_weak: Test: open a case against me with no evidence (wrongful arrest)
reallife_justice_test_court_date: Test: advance my next case to its court date
reallife_justice_test_hearing: Test: hearing of my next case (by video link)
reallife_justice_test_prison_short: Test: send me to prison for 3 days (the days really pass)
reallife_justice_test_prison_cap: Test: send me to prison for the longest term
reallife_justice_test_parole: Test: parole hearing (the last morning of a 3-day term)
reallife_justice_test_civil: Test: somebody sues me over a crash
reallife_justice_test_clear: Test: clear everything (cases, debts, record, sentences)
reallife_justice_test_soon: Justice test: it starts when this menu is closed and nothing else is going on.
reallife_justice_test_cleared: Justice test: every case, debt, sentence and record entry has been cleared.
reallife_justice_test_date_set: Justice test: your case is now due on day {day}, between 9:00 and 17:00, {place}.
reallife_justice_test_date_warrant: Justice test: that case already has a bench warrant out. Hand yourself in at the courthouse between 9:00 and 17:00, or use the hearing test.
reallife_justice_refused_part_off: Justice test not started: the part it tests is switched off on the options page (or 'No prison' is on).
reallife_justice_refused_broken: Justice test not started: the justice system switched itself off after errors this session (see Player.log).
reallife_justice_refused_busy: Justice test not started: a hearing, custody, a civil claim or three open cases are in the way.
reallife_justice_refused_no_case: Justice test not started: open a case with a test button first.
reallife_justice_refused_in_prison: Justice test not started: you are serving a prison term.
reallife_justice_refused_indoors: Community service not started: go out into the street on foot first.
reallife_justice_refused_no_pavement: Community service not started: there is no clear pavement within 36 m, so try another street.
reallife_contact_legal_desc: Your cases, your lawyer, what you owe
reallife_text_legal_welcome: This is the courts' information line. If you are ever charged with something serious, your court dates and judgments arrive here. Call to open your Legal file or to find a lawyer.
reallife_justice_charge_hit_run: Leaving the scene of a crash
reallife_justice_charge_hit_run_injury: Leaving the scene of a crash with injury
reallife_justice_charge_hit_run_death: Leaving the scene of a fatal crash
reallife_justice_call_off: The courts' information line is closed. (The justice system is switched off.)
reallife_justice_call_file: Your file is ready. Put the phone away and it opens.
reallife_justice_desk_no_case: You have no open case. If you are ever charged, come back and we will talk.
reallife_justice_offer_pd: The public defender's office: free, and stretched thin. They will stand beside you and ask for a deal, but they take only a point or two off the case against you.
reallife_justice_offer_self: You could represent yourself. It costs nothing and it is exactly as good as your own training in law (skill {skill} of 100): worth {effect} points to you in court (a good firm is worth up to 19; below zero it does you harm). Study raises it.
reallife_justice_offer_own: {name} is your own firm, rated {stars}. Your people will take the case at no fee: about {effect} points off the case against you.
reallife_justice_offer_terms: Their fee for what you are facing is {fee}: {down} now if you can spare it, the rest over six days. Honestly: counsel of this standing takes about {effect} points off the case against you, more if you come to the office to prepare.
reallife_justice_hired_pd: The public defender has your file. Call this number to hear what they make of it.
reallife_justice_hired_self: You will speak for yourself. Call this number to go through your own file.
reallife_justice_hired_firm: {name} now acts for you. Call any time to hear where your case stands, or come to the office: a case prepared across a desk goes better.
reallife_justice_counsel_strong: I will be straight with you. On {charge} they have you: as things stand a court convicts about {percent} times in 100. A plea is worth thinking about.
reallife_justice_counsel_even: On {charge} it could go either way: as things stand, about {percent} in 100 that you are convicted. How you answer in court will matter.
reallife_justice_counsel_thin: On {charge} their case is thin: about {percent} in 100 that it sticks. I would fight it, and I would try a motion to dismiss first.
reallife_justice_counsel_date: You are due in court on day {day}, between 9:00 and 17:00. Do not miss it.
reallife_justice_counsel_warrant: There is a warrant out for you. Hand yourself in at the courthouse between 9:00 and 17:00 before they come for you.
reallife_justice_counsel_come_in: Come by the office before the hearing if you can.
reallife_justice_deal_reduced: You plead guilty to {to} instead of {from}.
reallife_justice_deal_tail: Sentence cut by 40%, and no prison.
reallife_justice_deal_tail_prison: Sentence cut by 40%. Prison stays on the table.
reallife_justice_deal_offer: The prosecutor will agree to this. {terms} It will be on the table at your hearing: take it there, or go to trial. Your choice.
reallife_justice_motion_none: I made the motion. The judge found enough evidence on every charge: nothing is dismissed. We have had our one try.
reallife_justice_motion_some: The motion worked in part. Thrown out for want of evidence: {charges}. The rest goes to the hearing.
reallife_justice_motion_all: It is over. The judge threw the whole case out for want of evidence.
reallife_justice_court_call_1: All rise. Case number {number}. Be seated. The accused is present. Let us begin.
reallife_justice_court_call_2: Case number {number} is called. I have read the file. I will hear both sides, and I will not be hurried.
reallife_justice_court_call_3: Number {number} on today's list. The accused will stand while the charges are read.
reallife_justice_court_call_warrant: I note that the accused did not come when this case was first listed, and had to be brought. That is before me too.
reallife_justice_court_appointed: You have come without counsel. The court appoints the public defender to act for you.
reallife_justice_court_charges: The accused is charged as follows:
reallife_justice_court_withdrawn: Having looked at the evidence again, the prosecution withdraws: {charges}.
reallife_justice_court_on_probation: The accused was on probation at the time. If convicted, the court will take that into account.
reallife_justice_court_plea: You have heard the charges. How do you plead?
reallife_justice_court_aside: Your side of the table, quietly: on {charge}, the case against you stands at about {percent} in 100 right now.
reallife_justice_plea_guilty_hint: No trial. Convicted on every charge that stands, with a quarter off the sentence.
reallife_justice_plea_not_guilty_hint: A trial of {rounds} rounds. The case against you starts at {percent} in 100; your answers move it.
reallife_justice_verdict_guilty_plea: The plea of guilty is entered. The court gives credit for it.
reallife_justice_verdict_deal: The court accepts the agreement between the parties. {terms}
reallife_justice_beat_officer_1: The arresting officer takes the stand and goes through the notebook: where, when, what was seen, what was said. It is delivered flat and careful.
reallife_justice_beat_officer_2: The prosecution calls the officer in the case, who tells it in order and without colour: the time, the place, and you.
reallife_justice_beat_witness_1: A witness is called: someone who was on the street that day. They look at you once, then tell the court what they saw.
reallife_justice_beat_witness_2: The prosecution's witness is sworn in. The account is short, and it puts you there.
reallife_justice_beat_camera_1: The screens are turned on. Camera footage: grainy, time-stamped, played twice. The room watches it in silence.
reallife_justice_beat_camera_2: The prosecution plays its recording. The picture is not sharp, but the court can see what it can see.
reallife_justice_beat_flight_1: The prosecutor turns to what you did next. 'An innocent person stops. This one did not. Ask yourselves why.'
reallife_justice_beat_flight_2: 'And then,' says the prosecutor, 'the accused ran. People who have nothing to answer for do not make the police chase them.'
reallife_justice_beat_character_1: With little else to show, the prosecutor talks about you: your habits, your record, the kind of person who ends up here.
reallife_justice_beat_character_2: The prosecution has no more witnesses, so it argues from what it has: that it all points one way, and that way is you.
reallife_justice_beat_closing_1: The evidence is closed. The judge looks over to your table. 'Before I send this for a verdict: does the defence wish to be heard?'
reallife_justice_beat_closing_2: 'That is the case,' says the judge. 'The defence may close.'
reallife_justice_answer_testify_hint_str: Once only. The evidence is strong: cross-examination will likely hurt you (+6). Counsel advises against it.
reallife_justice_answer_testify_hint_wea: Once only. The evidence is thin: your own account can carry weight (-8).
reallife_justice_answer_object_hint: Sustained about {percent} times in 100 (as good as your counsel): -4 if it is, +1 if the judge is annoyed.
reallife_justice_answer_silent_hint: Safe. Counsel picks at it: about -{points}.
reallife_justice_answer_friend_hint: Once only. Someone who knows you speaks for you: -8.
reallife_justice_answer_footage: Put in your own shop's camera footage and receipts
reallife_justice_answer_footage_hint: Once only. Your business has cameras: its record of your day can cast real doubt (-10).
reallife_justice_answer_footage_hint_act: Once only. You were caught at it: your own footage is unlikely to change anything (0).
reallife_justice_result_testify_good: You take the stand and tell it plainly. The prosecutor comes at you twice and gets nowhere. The court listens.
reallife_justice_result_testify_bad: You take the stand. It goes well for a minute; then the cross-examination begins, and your account does not survive it.
reallife_justice_result_object_sustained: 'Objection.' The judge thinks about it. 'Sustained. The court will disregard that.'
reallife_justice_result_object_overruled: 'Objection.' 'Overruled,' says the judge, without looking up. 'Do not waste the court's time.'
reallife_justice_result_friend: {name} takes the stand and says what you are like when nobody is charging you with anything. It is simple, and it lands.
reallife_justice_result_footage_good: Your footage and your till receipts go in. They do not prove everything, but they leave a hole in the prosecution's day.
reallife_justice_result_footage_nothing: Your footage goes in. It shows your shop on an ordinary day, and nothing that touches what the officer saw.
reallife_justice_result_silent_good: You say nothing. Your counsel stands, asks five quiet questions, and the certainty goes out of the answers.
reallife_justice_result_silent_plain: You say nothing. A few questions are asked on your behalf. The evidence stands much as it was.
reallife_justice_result_close_remorse: You stand and say you are sorry, and mean it. It does not undo the evidence, but the judge writes something down.
reallife_justice_result_close_admission: You stand and try to explain. Halfway through you hear how it sounds: like someone admitting it.
reallife_justice_result_close_counsel: Your counsel closes: where the evidence is firm, where it is not, and what doubt is for.
reallife_justice_result_close_nothing: The defence rests without a word. The judge nods and gathers the papers.
reallife_justice_result_down: The case against you: down {points}, now {percent} in 100.
reallife_justice_result_up: The case against you: up {points}, now {percent} in 100.
reallife_justice_result_same: The case against you is unchanged: {percent} in 100.
reallife_justice_close_speak_hint_strong: The evidence is strong: remorse helps a little (-2) and takes a tenth off any sentence.
reallife_justice_close_speak_hint_weak: The evidence is thin: explaining yourself can sound like admitting it (+3).
reallife_justice_close_counsel_hint: As good as your counsel: about -{points}.
reallife_justice_verdict_sum: THE VERDICT. On top of the evidence on each charge: your record +{record}, your counsel {counsel}, your own answers in court {choices}.
reallife_justice_verdict_line_guilty: {charge}: evidence {evidence}, case against you {against}; the court's doubt stood at {doubt}. GUILTY.
reallife_justice_verdict_line_not_guilty: {charge}: evidence {evidence}, case against you {against}; the court's doubt stood at {doubt}. NOT GUILTY.
reallife_justice_verdict_rule: (A charge is proved when the case against you is stronger than the court's doubt. The doubt was fixed when the case was opened.)
reallife_justice_verdict_acquitted: You are acquitted on every charge and free to go. Your bail, and anything you were fined at the roadside for this, is returned.
reallife_justice_sentence_fine_bounded: (The law says {amount}; the court holds it to what you can bear.)
reallife_justice_sentence_fine_credit: Less {amount} already paid at the roadside: {due} to pay.
reallife_justice_sentence_fine_plan: Paid at {amount} a day over {days} days.
reallife_justice_sentence_prison: Prison: {days} days (the longest term there is: {cap}). You are taken down from here.
reallife_justice_sentence_commuted: This offence calls for prison. In its place: the longest custody the station can hold you for, and a heavier fine.
reallife_justice_sentence_community: Community service: {hours} hours, within {days} days. Report at the courthouse sign, or from your Legal file.
reallife_justice_sentence_first: (A first conviction: the cell has been turned into hours of work.)
reallife_justice_sentence_probation: Probation: {days} days. Any new conviction in that time carries half as much again, and a charge of its own.
reallife_justice_reason_trial: Why: convicted after a trial, so the sentence is in full.
reallife_justice_reason_guilty: Why: a quarter off for pleading guilty.
reallife_justice_reason_record: Your record (earlier convictions: {count}) weighed against you.
reallife_justice_reason_probation: You were on probation: the fine is half as much again.
reallife_justice_reason_complied: You stopped and gave the police no trouble: 15% off.
reallife_justice_reason_remorse: The court believed your remorse: 10% off.
reallife_justice_reason_appeal: You may appeal once, within {days} days, from your Legal file.
reallife_justice_court_dismissed: The prosecution offers no evidence. On what is in front of me there is nothing for the accused to answer, and there never was. The case is dismissed. The court apologises for the arrest.
reallife_justice_court_dismissed_comp: You are paid {amount}: compensation for the hours you were held, and anything you were fined at the roadside.
reallife_justice_bail_recognisance: A first matter, and nothing to suggest you will not come back. You are released on your own promise to appear. Your hearing will be in {days} days: the date is sent to your phone.
reallife_justice_bail_refused: Given what you are charged with and how you have behaved, bail is refused. You will be held until the court next sits, and your case will be heard then.
reallife_justice_bail_set: Bail is set at {amount}. Your hearing will be in {days} days. Come to it and the money is returned; miss it and it is forfeit, and a warrant goes out.
reallife_justice_bail_pay_hint: Returned in full when you appear.
reallife_justice_bail_pay_hint_short: You cannot cover it today: the bondsman will stand it instead.
reallife_justice_bail_bond_hint: A tenth of the bail, not returned. Owed over three days if you cannot pay it now.
reallife_justice_bail_stay_hint: Costs nothing. You are held until the court next sits (a day at most) and heard straight away.
reallife_justice_custody_fade: You are taken down to the cells.
reallife_justice_prison_fade: The van is waiting. You are taken to prison.
reallife_justice_prison_released_early: Something went wrong with your prison term and the rest of it was let go. You are free.
reallife_justice_prison_intake: Intake. Your things go into a bag with your name on it. A bunk, a blanket, a list of rules. 'Keep your head down and the days come off,' says the officer.
reallife_justice_prison_morning_1: Unlock at seven. Porridge, weak tea, the count. Another one.
reallife_justice_prison_morning_2: Rain on the high window. The wing wakes slowly, one cough at a time.
reallife_justice_prison_morning_3: The count comes up one short, then right. Breakfast is late and nobody is surprised.
reallife_justice_prison_morning_4: Somebody down the landing is singing. It is not good, but it is morning.
reallife_justice_prison_visit: A visit this morning: {name}, across a table, pretending the room is normal. It helps more than you would have said.
reallife_justice_prison_call: Your phone slot comes up and {name} answers on the second ring. Ten minutes of the outside.
reallife_justice_prison_how: How do you spend the day?
reallife_justice_prison_work_hint: {amount} into your account, and it is noticed: behaviour +1.
reallife_justice_prison_exercise_hint: You come out fit and rested: full energy and a better mood on release.
reallife_justice_prison_study_hint: The law shelf: +1 to your Lawyer skill.
reallife_justice_prison_work_done: Eight hours in the laundry. {amount} goes on your account.
reallife_justice_prison_exercise_done: Circuits round the yard until your legs shake. You sleep better for it.
reallife_justice_prison_study_done: A day with the criminal code and a pencil. More of it makes sense than you expected.
reallife_justice_prison_yard: Association, an hour before lock-up. The wing is out on the landings.
reallife_justice_prison_mix_hint: Usually it goes well (behaviour +1, a favour worth a little). One time in five it is trouble (behaviour -2).
reallife_justice_prison_alone_done: You read the same page of an old magazine for an hour. Nobody bothers you.
reallife_justice_prison_mix_good_1: You fall in with a table of card players who mostly want someone new to explain things to. One of them squares a favour for you at the canteen.
reallife_justice_prison_mix_good_2: You help a man write a letter to his daughter. Word gets round that you are all right, and something turns up on your canteen sheet.
reallife_justice_prison_mix_plain: Talk about food, mostly, and what people will do first when they are out. An hour passes.
reallife_justice_prison_mix_bad_1: A joke lands wrong with the wrong man. There is shoving; an officer writes four names down, and yours is one.
reallife_justice_prison_mix_bad_2: You are standing next to an argument when it stops being an argument. Everyone near it goes on report.
reallife_justice_prison_lights_out: Lock-up. The landing goes quiet door by door.
reallife_justice_prison_remitted: A slip under the door. Days off your sentence for good behaviour: {days}.
reallife_justice_pe_contraband: Your cellmate holds out a phone wrapped in a sock. 'Keep it in your mattress till Friday. There is something in it for you.'
reallife_justice_pe_contraband_out_a: 'Suit yourself.' He finds someone else. The cell search on Thursday finds nothing of yours.
reallife_justice_pe_contraband_out_b: Thursday's cell search finds it in under a minute. He pays you what he promised; the officer writes you up.
reallife_justice_pe_search: Cell search. Two officers tip out everything you own and one of them treads on your letters.
reallife_justice_pe_search_out_a: You look at the wall until they are finished. One of them straightens the letters before he goes.
reallife_justice_pe_search_out_b: It feels good for three seconds. Then it is on your sheet as 'abusive to staff'.
reallife_justice_pe_fight: Two men go for each other by the hot plate. Trays fly. You are an arm's length away.
reallife_justice_pe_fight_out_a: You put your back to the wall and your hands where they can be seen. The officers go past you.
reallife_justice_pe_fight_out_b: You stop it, more or less. When the officers arrive they see three people in a fight, and report three.
reallife_justice_pe_letter: A letter from home. Short, careful, with news of ordinary things.
reallife_justice_pe_letter_out_a: Two pages, most of it about the food. Writing it settles something. The officer who collects the post notices.
reallife_justice_pe_letter_out_b: You put it under the mattress and read it again at three in the morning.
reallife_justice_pe_kitchen: The kitchen is two hands short. The officer asks along the landing for volunteers.
reallife_justice_pe_kitchen_out_a: Four hours of potatoes. A little extra on your account, and your name remembered kindly.
reallife_justice_pe_kitchen_out_b: Somebody else goes. Dinner is late.
reallife_justice_pe_book: The library trolley comes round with one law textbook on it, three years out of date. The man next door offers you phone credit for your turn with it.
reallife_justice_pe_book_out_a: You read the chapter on evidence twice. It is the most interesting thing that has happened all week.
reallife_justice_pe_book_out_b: He gets the book. You get a few minutes more on the phone, which goes on your account.
reallife_justice_pe_informer: An officer stops at your door. 'Somebody on this landing has a phone. You hear things. It would be remembered.'
reallife_justice_pe_informer_out_a: He looks at you for a while, then moves on. Nothing changes.
reallife_justice_pe_informer_out_b: It is remembered, as promised. You sleep badly for a night or two all the same.
reallife_justice_pe_cards: A card game on the landing, canteen credit on the table. There is an empty chair.
reallife_justice_pe_cards_out_a: The cards like you for once. You get up while you are ahead, which surprises everyone.
reallife_justice_pe_cards_out_b: You watch a man lose a week's canteen on two pairs. Cheaper to watch.
reallife_justice_pe_cards_out_lost: The cards do not like you. Your canteen credit crosses the table.
reallife_justice_pe_cellmate: A new man is put in with you: first time inside, and he has nothing but what he stands in.
reallife_justice_pe_cellmate_out_a: Tea, biscuits and the rules explained properly. It costs you a little. The wing officer sees it.
reallife_justice_pe_cellmate_out_b: Top bunk is yours, the window is yours, quiet after ten. He nods at all of it.
reallife_justice_pe_noise: Two in the morning and somebody is kicking a door. On and on.
reallife_justice_pe_noise_out_a: It stops about four. You have slept worse.
reallife_justice_pe_noise_out_b: Now two doors are being kicked, and the night officer writes down both cell numbers.
reallife_justice_pe_counsellor: The prison counsellor has a free half hour and your name is on her list.
reallife_justice_pe_counsellor_out_a: You talk about what happens after. She writes 'engaging' on your sheet.
reallife_justice_pe_counsellor_out_b: You stay on your bunk. The half hour goes to someone else.
reallife_justice_pe_queue: Forty minutes in the phone queue, and a big man walks to the front as if you were not there.
reallife_justice_pe_queue_out_a: You wait six more minutes. The officer at the desk saw all of it, and nods at you.
reallife_justice_pe_queue_out_b: You get your place back, and a report for fighting to go with it.
reallife_justice_parole_open: The parole board. Three people, your file, a jug of water. 'You have served {served} days of {days}. We are here to decide whether you serve the rest outside.'
reallife_justice_parole_score: Your sheet: behaviour {behaviour}, earlier convictions {priors} (each counts against you). The board looks for {need} or better.

reallife_justice_parole_flatter: Tell them what they want to hear
reallife_justice_parole_flatter_hint: A gamble: +3 if they believe it, -2 if they do not.
reallife_justice_parole_honest_done: You say it straight. Nobody at the table interrupts.
reallife_justice_parole_flatter_good: You say all the right words in the right order, and they go down well.
reallife_justice_parole_flatter_bad: You say all the right words. The chair has heard them, in that order, many times.
reallife_justice_parole_quiet_done: You answer what you are asked and nothing more.
reallife_justice_parole_granted: 'Parole is granted.' (You scored {score}; they needed {need}.) You leave today. The days you do not serve are added twice over to your probation.
reallife_justice_parole_refused: 'Parole is refused.' (You scored {score}; they needed {need}.) You serve the rest.

reallife_meta_preset_about_relaxed: Relaxed: the city is alive, but little is done to you. No crime against you, no police stops for your driving, no pursuit after a crash and no prison; crashing into a car costs nothing and does not hurt (hitting a person still costs the fine for it); traffic cannot knock you down. No illness, no driving licence needed, no fuel use or breakdowns, no effects of weather, relationships do not fade, and your businesses get only the opportunities. Accidents, crime, fires and police on the street are rarer, and jobs pay a quarter more.
reallife_meta_preset_about_standard: Standard: every option the presets cover goes back to the value the mod ships with.
reallife_meta_preset_about_realistic: Realistic: everything that can happen to you is on, and there is more of it: more accidents, crime and fires, more police about, a few more life events and more trouble for your businesses. Job pay is unchanged.
reallife_meta_preset_about_hardcore: Hardcore: everything on at the strict end. Accidents, crime and fires are frequent, police are about most of the time, life events and business trouble come often, the longest prison term is 10 days, and jobs pay a fifth less. Fines are the same in every preset. There is no permanent death in any preset.
reallife_meta_preset_confirm: A preset only changes the options listed under 'Presets' in the Guide. Camera, visuals, clothes, keys and performance stay as you have them. Your settings as they are now are written to a file first, so this can be undone with Import.

reallife_meta_remove_explain:
This takes Real Life Overhaul out of the save '{save}', so that you can go on playing it without the mod.

To remove the mod:
1. Press "Prepare this save for removing the mod" in each save you want to keep.
2. Quit to the main menu and unsubscribe from the mod, or switch it off under Mods.
3. Restart the game.

What pressing it does to this save:
- Two backup copies of the save's files are made first: one in a new folder RealLifeOverhaul_backup_(date and time) beside them, one in the mod's own folder. If either copy fails, nothing is changed.
- Everything the mod has going is ended (a hired job van is handed in), and its features stay stopped until you load a save again.
- Its moods, its phone contacts with their messages, its entries in the notification list and its own stored data are taken out of the save. Money you earned or paid stays as it is, and so do the bank entries for it.
- The game is saved under the same name, and you are shown a list of what was removed.

If you load this save again with the mod still on, the mod starts afresh in it.
reallife_meta_report_no_backup: No backup was made: this game has no save file yet. Nothing on disk is changed by this tool.
reallife_meta_report_player_moved: You were put on the nearest walkable ground.
reallife_meta_report_stopped: The mod's features were shut down (parts stopped: {count}); what they had changed on the game's cameras, cars, lights and phone was put back.
reallife_meta_report_data: Entries of the mod's own data ({count})
reallife_meta_report_transactions: Kept: bank entries the mod made (fines, fees, job pay), {count} in all. The money really moved, so they stay; without the mod they are listed by a code, not a name.
reallife_meta_report_van: Kept: the van hired for a job is still in the save. It is one of the game's own job vans, and the game removes a job van that has no job by itself (hourly, when it is not driven and not in view) once the save has been loaded again.
reallife_meta_report_saved: Saved as '{save}'. Things of the mod's left in the save at the moment it was written: {left}.
reallife_meta_report_save_slow: The game is still writing the save. Wait a moment before you quit.
reallife_meta_report_not_saved: The game refused to save, so the save file on disk is unchanged. The mod's features are stopped for now. The backups are in {folder}
reallife_meta_report_next: What to do now: press the same button in every other save you want to keep, then quit to the main menu, unsubscribe from the mod or switch it off under Mods, and restart the game. Every save you make before you load again is kept clean as well. The mod's options and key choices are kept by the game outside the save and do no harm.
reallife_meta_report_next_failed: What to do now: leave whatever stops the game from saving and save by hand (the save will be clean), or load your save again to get the mod back as it was.
reallife_meta_resetdata_title: Reset the mod's data in this save
reallife_meta_resetdata_next: The mod reads the save afresh within a second. Save the game to keep it this way; load without saving to go back.
reallife_meta_repair_modifiers_ok: The mod's moods are known to the game: nothing to do.
reallife_meta_repair_modifiers_fixed: The mod's moods had gone from the game's list and were put back.
reallife_meta_repair_modifiers_bad: The mod's moods could not be put into the game's list; mood effects stay off. See Player.log.
reallife_meta_repair_contact_off: {contact}: not on the phone (its feature, or 'Extra phone contacts', is switched off).
reallife_meta_check_summary: Checked: {features} features, {options} options and {rules} preset rules. Problems found: {problems}. Each is also in Player.log.
reallife_guide_start: Real Life Overhaul {version} adds everyday life to the city of Big Ambitions: a camera behind your character, cars that drive like their kind, accidents, crime and police, jobs, illness, people to know and a city government. Each part can be switched off by itself on the options page. # First steps - Out of doors the camera sits behind you and the mouse looks around. {key_free_cursor} gives you the mouse cursor back for clicking and takes it again; {key_camera_toggle} switches to the game's own camera. - Your phone has new contacts. Each can be called. # The options page - Open the game's Options and choose the Mods tab. The mod's page starts with a search box, the button for this Guide, the presets, and reset, export and import. Below them is one section per feature: click a name to open or close it. - Type two letters or more in the search box to find options by a word in their name or their feature's. # Presets - A preset sets how much happens to you. The mod starts on Standard. Relaxed leaves you nearly alone; Realistic and Hardcore bring more incidents and more police. The preset now is {preset}, and the page 'Presets' lists what each one sets. # This Guide - It opens from the button 'Open the Guide' on the options page, and from the contact 'Real Life Overhaul Guide' on your phone (there while 'Extra phone contacts' is on): call it. - The topics are on the left, one per feature. Type to search titles and text; Backspace deletes a letter, Esc clears the search, and Esc again closes the Guide. - Scroll with the mouse wheel, the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End. - Prices, fines and keys on these pages are read from the mod when a page is opened, so they are the ones in force. # The mod's keys, as you have them now - Change them on the options page under 'Controls'. The performance and development keys do nothing while 'Developer diagnostics' is off. {controls}
reallife_guide_presets: A preset sets a group of options in one go. The four buttons are at the top of the options page and on the welcome panel. The preset in use now is {preset}; it reads 'Custom' as soon as one of the options below differs from all four. - Relaxed: little is done to you. No crime against you, no police stops or pursuits, no cost or injury from your own crashes, traffic cannot knock you down, no illness, no prison, no driving licence needed, no fuel use or breakdowns, weather without effects, relationships that do not fade, and only the opportunities for your businesses. Fewer incidents; jobs pay a quarter more. (Hitting a person with your car still costs the fine for it.) - Standard: the values the mod ships with. - Realistic: everything on, with more accidents, crime and fires, more police about and more trouble for your businesses. - Hardcore: everything on at the strict end: incidents frequent, police about most of the time, the longest prison term 10 days, jobs pay a fifth less. There is no permanent death in any preset, and the fines are the same in all of them. A preset touches only the options in the table below. Camera, visuals, clothes, keys and performance stay yours. Before a preset is applied, your settings are written to settings_before_preset.txt in {folder}. To undo a preset, rename that file to settings.txt and press Import. Changes take effect at once; something already going on plays out under the old values. # What each preset sets
reallife_guide_camera_about: A camera behind your character on foot, and behind the car when you drive.
reallife_guide_camera: # On foot - The camera follows behind you. With mouse look on, the mouse turns the camera and the cursor is hidden; a small dot marks the middle of the screen. - {key_camera_toggle} switches between this camera and the game's own. {key_free_cursor} frees the cursor and locks it again. - The mouse wheel still zooms. Indoors (if you switch that on) the camera is pulled in front of walls. - Mouse look switches itself off while a menu, the map, a shop window or a dialogue is open, and while the game is not the active window. - {key_interact} (or {key_interact_alt} while the game shows no prompt of its own) near a door or your own car takes you in the way a click would: opening hours and entrance fees apply. The door must be within about 5 m, the car within about 4.5 m. During one of the mod's jobs the key opens no door: click the building instead. # In the car - A chase camera sits behind the car; the mouse looks around and the view swings back behind the car after about a second without mouse movement once you are moving. - Hold {key_look_behind} to look behind. - In garages and car parks, and when you use the game's own look-back, the game's cameras take over. # Map markers - The game's place markers are put at the correct edge of the screen when what they mark is behind the camera. # Known limits - Another camera mod fights with this one over the camera: see Troubleshooting. - The chase camera's mouse look is off while the game's own 'vehicle mouse input' setting is on.
reallife_guide_character_about: Your character drawn in the game's detailed version in the city, and clothes and shoes made for the mod.
reallife_guide_character:
# What it does
- In the city the game draws a simplified player. The mod hides it and draws the detailed character the game uses in character creation and the shop mirror instead, moving exactly as you do. If you wear something the detailed set does not have, your normal body is shown while you wear it.
- Hair and beards get a finish with depth, hair gets a hair-coloured scalp underneath, skin gets a finer grain up close, and textures are sharpened.
- Character creation and the previews at the hairdresser, the clothing store and the plastic surgeon get a fill light and a rim light.
- New looks: five styles of shoe in four colours each; T-shirts, a bomber jacket, jeans, chinos, suit trousers, a pencil skirt, a summer dress and an evening dress in up to 32 colours and prints.

# How to wear the new clothes
- In character creation the everyday pieces are in the game's own lists, tagged RLO.
- In a save, pick them in the wardrobe section of the options page: a garment, then its colour. The first entry of each list is 'Game's own', which shows whatever the game has you wearing.
- With 'Clothes must be bought' on (it is on in a new game), a piece has to be bought first at the Real Life Overhaul rack in a clothing store, for $35 to $260. What you chose in character creation is yours.
- Your picks are kept with the save. They are drawn over the game's clothes; choosing another piece of that kind in one of the game's own screens takes the mod's piece off.

# Known limits
- The clothes need the mod's files. If they are missing, the new looks are left out and the game's look stays.
- If the detailed character cannot be matched to your character, the mod says so once in Player.log and shows the game's own character until the next load.
reallife_guide_citylife_about: People at work and going about their day on the pavements near you.
reallife_guide_citylife: # What you see - Street sweepers, window cleaners, a road crew, people handing out leaflets, a painter on a ladder, a gardener, a postman on his round, a courier with a sack truck. - Friends talking, smokers, people on the phone, tourists with a map, joggers, a chess table, tai chi in the morning, a queue outside a door at night, umbrellas in the rain. - A coffee cart and a hot-dog cart with customers who walk up, queue, are served and walk off. - {city_count} different activities in all, each with its own hours. At most {city_sites} of them are out at once with {city_people} people in all, 45 to 95 m from you, and they are set up and taken away only where you are not looking. # What you can do - Buy a coffee: stand at the counter of the coffee cart and press {key_interact}. It costs {coffee_price} and gives a little energy (5 of 100). - Otherwise they are there to be seen. Drive into them and they fall like anyone else. # When it is quiet - Nothing is out between 02:00 and 05:00, little before 07:00 and after 22:00. - While an accident or a crime is going on, nothing new starts. - In the rain everybody is taken in except the people with umbrellas. # Known limits - It needs the mod's animation and model files. An activity whose animation or model is missing does not start.
reallife_guide_crime_about: Crime that happens near you, crime against you, and the police stopping you for your own driving.
reallife_guide_crime: # Crime near you - Now and then something happens within 35 to 80 m: a foot chase, a snatch, a mugging, graffiti, a car break-in, a traffic stop, a shoplifter, a hold-up. There are {crime_count} kinds. An orange marker shows where. - One thing at a time: no crime starts during an accident or while the police have business with you. - You can watch, walk away, or call 911 (the first choice names what is going on): an officer is sent, and if it ends in an arrest you get the 'Did the right thing' mood. - Somebody running for it can be stopped: stay within arm's reach of them. An officer comes, sometimes they try to break free once, and you are thanked, sometimes with cash. - In your own shop you can confront a thief with {key_interact}. - A 911 call about nothing is a warning twice a day; the third and every one after it cost {fine_wasted_call}, and with arrests for serious offences on the fifth puts you in a holding cell. # Crime against you (option: crimes against you) - Pickpocket: takes 6% of your cash, from $10 to $250. Catch them and you get it back. - Mugging, on foot between 21:00 and 05:00: hand over 15% ($20 to $400), or refuse: half the time they run, half the time you lose 7.5% ($20 to $200) and are hurt. Walking away before they reach you also works. - Neither happens while you carry less than $60. - Hold-up in your own shop: 4% of your cash ($40 to $500). - Out of your sight: a break-in at one of your shops overnight (stock, and a repair bill of $60 to $350; good security prevents most), your parked car broken into (repair up to $250), a scam call (hang up and it costs nothing; give the details and you may lose up to $400). - A pickpocket or mugger leaves you alone for at least two days after the last one; break-ins, car break-ins and scam calls rest five to seven days each. # Being pulled over (option: police stop you) - What counts: running a red light, speeding, driving on the pavement, driving against the traffic. Speeding means more than {speed_margin} km/h over the limit ({speed_limit} km/h where the road does not say) for {speed_seconds} seconds. - It only matters if somebody sees it. A patrol car happens to be near {seen_redlight} of the time for a red light, {seen_speeding} for speeding (twice that from {speed_gross} km/h) and {seen_reckless} for reckless driving, scaled by the crime frequency option; an officer on foot with a clear view sees much more. With the option 'Police attend accidents and chase hit-and-run drivers' off, nothing you do at the wheel is seen. - A patrol car then comes up behind you with its lights on. Stop within 15 seconds and stay stopped: an officer walks up and writes the ticket. - Fines: red light {fine_redlight}, speeding {fine_speeding}, reckless or wrong side {fine_reckless}. Each kind is charged once per stop. After two drinks or more, any stop adds $900 for driving after drinking. - If you drive on, it is a pursuit. Lose them (out of sight for ten seconds, or 240 m ahead) and you pay no fine, but your car is known for the rest of the day: it is noticed far more easily and pays half as much again. - If they catch you: the fines, plus {fine_fleeing} for fleeing and {fine_fleeing_step} for every quarter minute it lasted, at most {fine_fleeing_most}, and you are arrested and held at the nearest police station (see the Guide page on custody). With the custody option off, {custody_min} to {custody_max} hours pass and you are let go where you stood. - On foot, crossing on red or walking in the road in front of an officer earns a shout and, one time in five, a fine of {fine_jaywalk}. - Fines are charged in full, even if that takes you below zero. # Known limits - A pickpocket or a mugger cannot be reported to 911. - The crimes on this page never kill you; refusing a mugger can injure you.
reallife_guide_driving_about: Each car gets the acceleration and top speed of its kind, an eased throttle and a speedometer.
reallife_guide_driving: # What changes - In the game every car has the same engine and gearbox and is stopped by a limiter at 50 to 100 km/h. With car tuning on, the car you drive (never traffic) is given a 0-100 time and a top speed for its kind, and air drag instead of a limiter: it pulls hard to 50, steadily to 100 and builds slowly to its top speed. - Examples (0-100 km/h, top speed): Honza Mimic 12.5 s, 170; Vord Tiara Vic 10 s, 190; BIMA 320 8.5 s, 210; Mersaidi S500 6.5 s, 240; Vord Pony 5.8 s, 240; Ferdinand 112 5.0 s, 265; Anselmo AF90 4.5 s, 290; UMC Nunavut 9 s, 190; UMC Desert van 16 s, 140; Freight Truck T1 20 s, 130. Scooters and hand trucks are left alone. - The two sliders scale top speed and acceleration from 70% to 150% of those figures. - Smooth throttle: the throttle key eases the pedal down over {throttle_rise} s and lifts in {throttle_fall} s, so a tap pulls away gently. An analogue trigger keeps its own feel. - Hold {key_gentle_throttle} to keep the pedal at {gentle_throttle} at most. - Brakes are the game's own. From the new top speeds a car needs 66 to 122 m to stop: look ahead. - The speedometer shows km/h or mph, following the game's units setting. - Everything changed on a car is put back when you get out, change car or switch the option off. # Measure this car - The button on the options page times a real run: press it, come to a stop, then hold full throttle for 20 seconds. A message gives 0-50, 0-100 and the speed reached. # After a hospital trip - Your car is brought to a kerb space near where you come out, or towed to a repair shop, for {tow_fee}. # Known limits - A car from another mod is placed by its own data (weight, cargo room, the game's top speed) into one of the kinds above. - A car the sums cannot be done for (no combustion engine or no automatic gearbox) is left as the game made it, with a line in Player.log. - Faster cars mean the police notice speed only when it is well over the limit for a while: see Crime and police stops.
reallife_guide_jobs_about: Seven jobs you do yourself on the street, paid when the work is done.
reallife_guide_jobs: # How to get one - Call the Gig Line on your phone, or walk up to a help-wanted board (outside a few service buildings) and press {key_interact}. You are told each job's pay, your level and how much of it is left today; take one or ask what else there is. - To stop, call the Gig Line again and say you are done. Work done so far is paid. Giving up with most of the work undone can count as a failed shift. - A job cannot start indoors, during one of the game's own missions, or with energy below {job_min_energy}. # The jobs - A unit is one piece of the work: a flyer taken, a spill mopped, a box shelved, a customer served, a song, a parcel delivered, a fare. {job_table} - Flyers: offer a flyer to passers-by with {key_interact}. More pay on a busy street and for the whole bundle. - Cleaner: mop the spills inside a client's premises. - Shelf stocker: carry boxes from the kerb to a shop's shelves. - Drinks cart: serve each customer the drink they ask for with keys 1, 2, 3. Quick service earns tips; three customers who walk off end the shift. - Busker: pick a song with 1, 2 or 3, then press {key_interact} each time a strum is called for. Tips only, more where and when people are about. The police may move you on. - Courier: collect the parcels at the pick-up address, load the car, deliver to the doors on the round. A bonus for beating the clock. - Ride-hail: pick up fares and drive them smoothly: the tip follows the passenger's comfort. # The rules - Levels: {job_levels} per job. Each level above the first pays {job_level_bonus} more. The 'Job pay' option scales everything. - If you run businesses of your own, every job pays 15% less for each one, down to 55% of the usual pay at the lowest. The pay the Gig Line and the employers quote already includes this. - Ride-hail wants a reference (level {job_reference_level} in any job), no police stop on a job in the last {job_clean_days} days and, while driving licences are switched on, a taxi endorsement from a driving school. - A driving job needs a car within 60 m. With none of your own you are given a hired van for {job_van_fee} a day; it is taken back when the shift is over and you are out of it. - On a driving job a crash costs {job_crash_cut} of that unit's pay and a police stop {job_stop_cut} (twice that on the courier's round). A pay slip never goes below zero. - {job_strikes} failed shifts in a job and it lets you go for {job_sacked_days} days. A good shift takes a strike off. - Work uses energy and trains a skill through the game's own systems. It never takes your energy below 12. - A shift ends by itself, paid, if you sleep, are taken to hospital or into custody, take one of the game's missions, or walk into a building that is not the client's. - A job in progress is not saved: loading a game starts with no job on.
reallife_guide_job_row: {name}: {pay} a unit{metre}, at most {daily} units a day, a level every {level} units
reallife_guide_life_about: Small things that happen to you, a cold now and then, and people to call.
reallife_guide_life:
# Random events
- Every so often something happens (the frequency option is roughly the number of events per game week): a message on screen, a text from Alex or Mom, or a question with two answers. There are {life_count} of them, and none repeats in a save until all that fit your situation have been seen.
- They move small amounts of money, energy, hunger or mood, and a few give you a cold or a minor injury. A loss never puts you in debt, and questions are never asked while you drive.
- Nothing happens while you sleep, sit in a menu or a dialogue, or are otherwise busy.

# Being sick
- A cold lowers your mood and drains a little extra energy for a day or two.
- Call Dr. Patel while you are sick: a consultation costs {doctor_fee} and cures it. So does a hospital stay.

# The phone
- 911: report what is happening near you, or ask for an ambulance for yourself ({ambulance_fee}, plus the game's own hospital bill). If you were driving, your car is brought near the hospital afterwards for {tow_fee}.
- Alex and Mom can each be called once a day for a better mood. They also text you as part of events.

# Moods
- The mod adds its own entries to the game's happiness list (Feeling sick, Injured, Lucky day, Got robbed and so on). They wear off after a few hours to three days.

# Known limits
- The contacts appear only while 'Extra phone contacts' is on, and that option is read when a save is loaded.
reallife_guide_people_about: Officers on the beat, a patrol car at the kerb, and the crews at accident and crime scenes.
reallife_guide_people:
# What you see
- One or two officers walking a beat near you, a patrol car parked at the kerb with its crew beside it, an officer at a junction. The 'Police presence' and 'Officers on the beat: how often' options say how often.
- At scenes: drivers who get out, paramedics with a stretcher, officers who put up tape, direct traffic and take statements. Officers and paramedics wear one uniform each with their equipment.

# Why it matters
- An officer on foot who has a clear view of you is a witness to what you do at the wheel, and to crossing on red: see Crime and police stops.
- At an accident you can walk up to help (within about 9 m, on foot) for the 'Did the right thing' mood.

# Limits the mod keeps to
- Officers, crews and the people at scenes are at most {pool_people} at once, and at most {pool_presence} of them are there only to be seen. An accident or crime scene takes those first, so a parked patrol car may stand empty for a while.
- They appear and leave where you are not looking, and they walk wherever they go.
reallife_guide_phone_about: Contacts you can call, and a modern look for the phone.
reallife_guide_phone:
# Contacts
- Emergency Services (911): report an accident, a crime or a fire near you, or call an ambulance for yourself ({ambulance_fee}).
- Dr. Patel: a phone consultation when you are sick ({doctor_fee}).
- Alex and Mom: a chat once a day each, for your mood.
- Gig Line: the jobs (it needs 'Jobs' on as well).
- Real Life Overhaul Guide: opens this guide.
- Most other features add a contact of their own, described on that feature's page.
- The contacts and their messages are kept in your save by the game, like its own contacts.

# The phone's look
- With 'Modern phone look' on the phone has a modern body, a wallpaper, a clock and a status bar. Phone cases bought in the game keep working. Switching it off puts the game's phone back at once.

# Known limits
- 'Extra phone contacts' is read when a save is loaded: switching it on or off takes effect on the next load. It covers every contact the mod adds. Switching it off does not delete contacts already in a save; 'Prepare this save for removing the mod' does.
reallife_guide_ragdoll_about: People hit by a car fall as bodies with weight, and may be hurt or killed.
reallife_guide_ragdoll:
# When you hit someone
- Below about 15 km/h they are knocked over, get up after a few seconds and walk off angry. From 15 to 35 they stay down, hurt. Above that they may die: one in ten at 35 km/h, almost certainly from 90.
- Someone who stays down becomes an accident scene: an ambulance and a patrol car come, and the casualty is taken away.
- You have the same choice as after hitting a car: stop within about 12 seconds and stay near, or drive off. With 'police pursuit' off it is always settled as if you had stopped.
- Stopped: {fine_injury} for an injury, {fine_death} for a death. Fled and caught: {fine_injury_run} and {fine_death_run}. Got away: {fine_injury_escaped} and {fine_death_escaped}, billed some hours later. A death weighs on your mood for three days.
- At the roadside the police take at most 35% of your cash, or $250 if that is more. The rest of the fine goes to court with the case, or is not collected. A fine billed later is charged in full.

# When traffic hits you (option: player knockdown)
- On foot in the road you can be knocked down: shaken at low speed, injured from about 15 km/h, and taken to hospital from about 35. You lie for a few seconds and get up where you landed. You are never killed, and cannot be hit again for a few seconds.

# Pedestrians hit by traffic (option: pedestrians struck by traffic)
- Now and then a traffic car hits a pedestrian near you, and an ambulance and the police come. How often follows the accident frequency option.

# Limits the mod keeps to
- At most {ragdoll_max} people are falling with full physics at once; up to {ragdoll_still} more lie still. When more go down, the one who has lain longest makes room.
reallife_guide_traffic_about: Accidents among the game's own traffic, the emergency response to them, and what your own crashes cost.
reallife_guide_traffic:
# Accidents near you
- Now and then there is an accident 45 to 140 m away: one car or two, three in a severe one; minor, moderate or severe (a severe one may roll a car). An orange marker shows where and how far.
- A patrol car always comes (with 'police' on); an ambulance for moderate and severe ones, and for those the road is closed with tape, barriers and cones. Crews work, the casualty leaves on a stretcher, and the scene clears inside about three minutes (five at the very most).
- Some drivers run for it and are chased.
- You can walk up to help, or call 911 and report it, which sends the units at once. Both earn the 'Did the right thing' mood.
- A road the mod closed is opened again whichever way the scene ends.

# Your own crashes (option: crash consequences)
- Hitting a traffic car at about 25 km/h or more costs damages from $150 to $3,000 by the speed of the impact. Harder hits injure you; the hardest end in hospital.
- With 'police pursuit' on you have about 12 seconds to stop near the crash. Stop, and you pay the damages only.
- Drive off and a patrol car comes after you, at up to {pursuit_least} to {pursuit_most} km/h depending on your car (about 83 km/h while car tuning is off), with a second one after {pursuit_backup} seconds. Caught: damages plus {fine_caught}, and you are arrested: with custody on, 8 to 16 hours in a holding cell. Got away: damages plus {fine_escaped}, billed some hours later (the bill is kept in your save).
- If a person was hurt, the larger fines under 'Ragdolls and people hit by cars' apply instead.

# Options
- 'Traffic accident frequency' also sets how often traffic hits a pedestrian.
- 'Siren' and 'People at scenes and on the street' are read when a unit or a scene starts; one already out keeps what it had.

# Known limits
- One incident of any kind at a time. A scene that is running when you switch its option off plays to its end.
reallife_guide_visuals_about: Colour grading and detail distance for the whole picture.
reallife_guide_visuals:
# What it does
- Saturation and contrast are added on top of the game's picture and cost nothing.
- Bloom at 0 leaves the game's own bloom alone; raising it costs frames.
- Detail distance above 100% keeps detailed models for longer and costs frames.
- Switching 'Visual upgrades' off puts the game's picture back at once.
reallife_guide_keys_about: Every key the mod listens to, and how to change it.
reallife_guide_keys:
# The mod's keys, as you have them now
{controls}
# Changing a key
- Options page, 'Controls': click a line, then press the new key. Hold Shift, Ctrl or Alt with it for a combination. Esc cancels, and so does waiting 8 seconds. The left mouse button and gamepad buttons are not offered.
- A key the game itself uses is allowed; the line then says which of the game's actions shares it.
- 'Reset the mod's keys to their defaults' puts all of them back.

# Keys for developer diagnostics
- The four lines that end '(developer diagnostics)' only work while 'Developer diagnostics' is switched on, on the options page. While it is off those keys do nothing.

# Fixed keys
- In jobs, choices are 1, 2, 3 (top row or number pad).
- In this guide: Esc, the arrows, Page Up and Page Down, Home, End, and typing to search.
- While this guide or another panel of the mod's is open, none of the mod's keys does anything.

# The game's own keys
- The mod changes none of them. Its interact key ({key_interact}) is the game's own interact key unless you change one of them; the second one ({key_interact_alt}) only acts while the game shows no prompt of its own.
reallife_guide_performance_about: Small changes to how the base game draws the city, and the tools to measure them on your computer.
reallife_guide_performance: # The switches (options page, 'Performance') - On by default, with nothing to see: the refraction effect is off outdoors, where nothing uses it; the sky's reflection and its light on things are refreshed every 2 seconds instead of every frame; street lamps that are off no longer keep their lights switched on. - Off by default: scenery more than 1.3 km away is not drawn; people, cars and small things are drawn only within 300 m in every direction; street furniture and parked cars are not drawn beyond 200 m. The last one can be seen: they appear at 200 m instead of 300 m. - Each switch puts back exactly what it changed when it is turned off. One that meets something unexpected says so once in Player.log and stays off until the city is loaded again. - No gain is promised: what a switch saves depends on your computer. The tools below measure it. # Measuring on your computer - Two buttons at the end of the 'Performance' section. 'Measure performance for 10 seconds' writes RealLifeOverhaul_perf_(time).txt: where the time of a frame goes and what is in the city around you, with a screenshot in the folder RealLifeOverhaul_shots. - 'Run performance test, about 3 minutes' switches each item off and on in turn, several times, and writes the table RealLifeOverhaul_bench_(time).txt. It needs you on foot in the street; stand still and leave the mouse alone. Parts of the picture and of the interface go and come back while it runs. - After pressing a button, close the menu: the measurement starts two seconds later. - The keys {key_perf_probe} and {key_perf_bench} start the same two measurements, but only while 'Developer diagnostics' is switched on. While it is off they do nothing. - The files are in {data}, next to Player.log. # What the mod itself costs - Apart from the camera, the mod's features work on timers, not every frame, and wait while nothing is going on. Options that cost frames (bloom, detail distance) are off or neutral by default and say so in their label.
reallife_guide_savetools_about: What the mod leaves in a save, and how to take it out again.
reallife_guide_savetools:
# What the mod puts into a save
- Its own data: what it remembers about this save (life events seen, illness, fines owed, job and career progress, your licence and record, the people you know, the city government and so on) and the mod version.
- Its moods in the happiness list. The game cannot load a mood it does not know, so the mod takes its moods out every time the game saves and puts them back a moment later: an ordinary save already loads without the mod.
- Its phone contacts with their messages, and its lines in the notification list.
- Bank entries for fines, fees and job pay.
- During a job with a hired van: that van, which is one of the game's own job vans.

# Removing the mod
1. Press "Prepare this save for removing the mod" in each save you want to keep.
2. Quit to the main menu and unsubscribe from the mod, or switch it off under Mods.
3. Restart the game.

# What "Prepare this save for removing the mod" does
- It makes two backup copies of the save's files first, and stops if either fails: one in a folder RealLifeOverhaul_backup_(date and time) inside the save's own folder, one under backups in {folder}. The game deletes a save's folder whole when you delete the character or its last save; the second copy is out of its reach.
- It then ends everything the mod has going, stops the mod's features until a save is loaded again, removes the moods, contacts, notification lines and data listed above, saves under the same name and lists what it removed. The list is also written to {folder}.
- Bank entries stay, because the money really moved; without the mod they are listed by a code, not a name.
- You must be on foot, and not in the middle of a hospital trip, police custody, sleep, an activity, a subway ride or a trip on the casino boat.
- It works on the save that is loaded, one at a time. There is no button for all saves at once.

# Reset the mod's data in this save
- Ends what is going on, takes the mod's moods off and removes its stored data, and keeps the mod running: as if the mod had just been added to this save. Contacts stay. A backup copy is made first; the save file itself is not changed until you save.

# Repair
- Puts back the mod's phone contacts and its moods if they are missing from a save.

# After every load
- The mod checks the save for things another version of it left behind. Moods this version does not have are removed, with a line in Player.log for each; anything else it does not recognise is kept.

# The mod's own files
- Settings files, save-tool reports and the second backup copies: {folder}. Performance reports and diagnostic files: {data}. None of them is needed to play.
- Options and key choices are kept by the game with its own settings, not in a save.
reallife_guide_diagnostics_about: Detailed lines in Player.log, the diagnostic keys, and the test buttons.
reallife_guide_diagnostics: # Developer diagnostics - Off unless you switch it on. While it is off the mod writes only warnings and errors to Player.log, and the four diagnostic keys do nothing. - Switch it on to report a problem: the mod's features then also write what they are doing to Player.log (a line per step, never a line per frame). - While it is on, {key_perf_probe} measures performance for ten seconds, {key_perf_bench} runs the performance test, {key_phone_dump} writes the layout of the phone's interface and of the characters to text files with a screenshot, and {key_character_report} writes a report of the characters on screen. The files are in {data}. None of this changes anything in the game. # Test tools - 'Show test tools' is off unless you switch it on. It puts a section at the bottom of the options page with every feature's test buttons: an accident, a crime, a job, a life event and so on, started where you stand. A test that cannot start says why. - Some tests have real effects (a fine if you stop for the test patrol car, stock lost in the test break-in). # Check the mod's set-up - Looks through the options, the presets and the pages of this Guide for anything that does not fit together, and lists it. It changes nothing.
reallife_guide_trouble: # The camera jumps or fights itself - The Workshop mod 'Immersion - RPG Camera' also moves the camera. Two camera mods cannot both have it: switch one of them off under Mods, or switch off 'Third-person follow camera' and 'Chase camera when driving' here. The mod writes a warning to Player.log when it sees the other one. # The mouse cursor is gone - Mouse look hides it. Press {key_free_cursor} to get it back (and again to return to mouse look), or {key_camera_toggle} for the game's own camera. # A key does nothing, or does two things - Look at 'Controls' in this Guide for the keys as you have them, and at the Controls section of the options page: a line says when the game uses the same key. - {key_perf_probe}, {key_perf_bench}, {key_phone_dump} and {key_character_report} are diagnostic keys. They do nothing unless 'Developer diagnostics' is on. # Something of the mod's is stuck on the street - Switch its feature off and on again, or, with 'Show test tools' on, use the feature's clear or stop test button if it has one. 'Reset the mod's data in this save' ends everything at once. Loading the save also clears it: nothing the mod puts on the street is saved. # Frame rate - See 'Performance'. If in doubt, set bloom to 0 and detail distance to 100% under Visuals, and switch off the high-detail player character under 'Character and wardrobe'. # Where the files are - The game's log is Player.log in {data}. The mod's lines begin [Mod:Real Life Overhaul] (or [Mod:RealLifeOverhaul] for a copy in the ModsLocal folder). - Performance reports, diagnostic files and the folder RealLifeOverhaul_shots with their screenshots are in the same place. - Settings files and save-tool reports are in {folder}. - Backups of a save are inside that save's own folder under SaveGames, and again under backups in {folder}. # Reporting a problem - Switch on 'Developer diagnostics' (options page, Diagnostics) and make the problem happen again, so that Player.log has the detail. - Say what you were doing and what you expected, and attach Player.log from that session (it is overwritten when the game starts again). - For a frame-rate problem, press {key_perf_probe} while it is happening and attach the report it writes. - Export your settings (options page) and attach settings.txt. - Mention the mod version, {version}, and which other mods are on. # Going back - 'Reset every option and key of the mod to its default' puts the mod as it came. To remove the mod, see 'Save tools'.
reallife_guide_credits:
# The mod
- Real Life Overhaul {version}.
- Big Ambitions is made by Hovgaard Games. This mod is not made or endorsed by them.

# What is in the mod's files
- The mod's own code and texts.
- Clothes and shoes, 77 street models and 77 animations, all made for this mod with Blender by its own scripts.
- No model, texture, animation or sound of Big Ambitions is in the files, and no third-party model, motion capture or animation library.
- The clothes were shaped around measurements of the game's character. The animations were made to the joint positions and bone names of the game's street character, so that they fit its people. These are measurements: nothing of the game's was copied.
- The lettering on signs and tape is drawn with the font Aileron Regular by Sora Sagano (CC0 1.0).
- 'THE DAILY POST' and 'QUICK BITE' on models are names made up for the mod.
- No sound files: the sirens and the city sounds are generated by the mod's code.

# Tools used (none of them is in the mod's files)
- Blender, Unity 2022.3, UnityPy, Pillow, NumPy and the .NET SDK.

# Licence
- The mod is open source under the MIT licence. Ask the author before you reuse its code, texts, models or animations.

reallife_lic_q_d41: An officer is directing traffic at a junction. Whose signals do you follow?|Those of the officer|Those of the car in front|Your own judgement only
reallife_lic_q_d42: You see blue lights ahead at the roadside dealing with a stopped car. What do you do?|Slow down and pass with plenty of room|Stop beside them to look|Use the pavement to get past
reallife_lic_q_d43: Where on a two-way street do you drive?|In your own lane, with the traffic: never against it|On whichever side is emptier|Down the middle
reallife_lic_q_d44: How many points does driving against the traffic carry?|Four|One|None
reallife_lic_q_d45: On the practical test, what is staying in lane about?|Keeping within your lane and off the pavement for the whole route|Driving on the centre line|Changing lane as often as possible
reallife_lic_q_d46: You hit another car and it was your fault. What should you do?|Stop near the scene and settle the damage|Drive off quickly|Reverse into it again
reallife_lic_q_d47: What is smooth braking?|Slowing early and progressively, so nobody is thrown forward|Stamping on the pedal at the last moment|Never using the brake at all
reallife_lic_q_d48: On the practical test, a harsh stop from speed counts as:|A minor fault|A pass with distinction|Nothing
reallife_lic_q_d49: How many minor faults may you collect and still pass the practical test?|Six, with no serious fault|None at all|Twenty
reallife_lic_q_d50: Which of these is a serious fault that fails the practical test on its own?|Running a red light|Braking a little late|Driving at 45 in a 50
reallife_lic_q_d51: On the practical test you bump another vehicle hard while parking. What is that?|A collision: a serious fault|A minor fault|Normal parking
reallife_lic_q_d52: At the end of the test the examiner asks you to park in a marked bay. What counts?|Stopping inside the box, straight, without touching anything|Stopping anywhere near it|Stopping the fastest
reallife_lic_q_d53: For the commercial test, how must you enter the marked bay?|In reverse|Forwards at speed|Sideways
reallife_lic_q_d54: Which licence do you need for a delivery van or a truck?|Commercial|Car|None
reallife_lic_q_d55: Which of these may you ride or push without any licence?|An electric scooter or a hand truck|A pickup|A panel van
reallife_lic_q_d56: What extra do you need to carry passengers for hire?|A taxi endorsement on a car licence|Nothing extra|Only a commercial licence
reallife_lic_q_d57: You hold a car licence. May you drive an SUV or a pickup?|Yes: cars, SUVs and pickups are all on the car licence|No: they need a commercial licence|Only at weekends
reallife_lic_q_d58: What must you hold before you can sit the commercial test?|A valid car licence|A taxi endorsement|Nothing
reallife_lic_q_d59: How many penalty points get your licence suspended?|Twelve|Six|Thirty
reallife_lic_q_d60: For how long is a licence suspended at twelve points?|Seven days|One hour|For ever
reallife_lic_q_d61: After how long does a penalty-point entry stop counting?|Three weeks|One day|Never
reallife_lic_q_d62: You are stopped by police and have no licence for the vehicle. What happens?|A heavy fine, and the vehicle is impounded|A warning|They issue you a licence on the spot
reallife_lic_q_d63: You are caught driving while suspended. What happens?|A heavier fine, the vehicle impounded, and repeat offenders are arrested|Nothing new|The suspension ends early
reallife_lic_q_d64: For how long is a licence valid before it must be renewed?|120 days|7 days|For life
reallife_lic_q_d65: Your licence ran out last week. What do you do?|Renew it for a fee: no test is needed unless it lapsed more than 30 days ago|Sit both tests again at once|Nothing: it renews itself
reallife_lic_q_d66: How is driving without a licence discovered?|Only when police actually stop you, for an offence or at a roadside check|By satellite|The moment you start the engine
