reallife_civic_slogan_safety_3: An officer you know by name.
reallife_civic_slogan_roads_1: Fix the street before the ribbon.
reallife_civic_slogan_roads_2: Green means go. Red means red.
reallife_civic_slogan_roads_3: Potholes don't vote. I fill them anyway.
reallife_civic_slogan_business_1: Open the shutters, lower the bill.
reallife_civic_slogan_business_2: A city that says yes to the corner shop.
reallife_civic_slogan_living_1: A city you can afford to stay in.
reallife_civic_slogan_living_3: Your pay should outlast the month.
reallife_civic_slogan_services_2: You pay for a city. Get one.
reallife_civic_slogan_services_3: The bins, the buses, the basics.
reallife_civic_slogan_growth_1: Build it. Open it. Fill it.
reallife_civic_slogan_growth_2: The city that stays up late.
reallife_civic_policy_policing_up_fx: about 40% more officers and patrol cars about, street crime down about 20%; the city levy rises by $70 a week
reallife_civic_policy_policing_up_say: I will put four officers where there are three today, and you will see them on foot. It costs every household and business seventy dollars a week on the levy, and I think a street you can walk down is worth it.
reallife_civic_policy_policing_down_fx: about 40% fewer officers and patrol cars about, street crime up about 25%; $50 a week comes back on the city levy
reallife_civic_policy_policing_down_say: We pay for patrols that drive past. I will trim the force and hand fifty dollars a week back to you. Yes, there will be fewer officers about. I would rather say so than pretend.
reallife_civic_policy_traffic_up_fx: police fines 50% higher, traffic accidents down about 30%
reallife_civic_policy_traffic_up_say: Run a red light in my city and it will cost you half as much again. Fewer crashes is the whole point; if you drive properly it costs you nothing.
reallife_civic_policy_traffic_down_fx: police fines 30% lower, traffic accidents up about 30%
reallife_civic_policy_traffic_down_say: People who drive for a living are fined like a cash machine. I will cut fines by nearly a third. The roads will be a little rougher for it, and I trust adults to cope.
reallife_civic_policy_tax_up_fx: a surcharge of 20% of the income tax your sales run up, billed weekly
reallife_civic_policy_tax_up_say: The services everyone wants have to be paid for. One fifth more on business income tax, billed weekly so nobody gets a shock in the spring.
reallife_civic_policy_tax_down_fx: 20% of the income tax your sales run up is paid back to you, weekly
reallife_civic_policy_tax_down_say: One fifth of what a business owes on its income comes straight back, every week. Shops that keep their money hire people. That is the plan.
reallife_civic_policy_levy_up_fx: 0.5% of your sales is charged weekly; $40 a week comes off the city levy
reallife_civic_policy_levy_up_say: Half a cent on the dollar at the till, and forty dollars a week off the levy for everybody. Those who trade most carry a little more. I think that is fair.
reallife_civic_policy_levy_down_fx: 0.3% of your sales is paid back to you weekly
reallife_civic_policy_levy_down_say: Sell in this city and the city sends a little of it back: thirty cents on every hundred dollars. It is not much. It is every week.
reallife_civic_policy_grants_up_fx: $150 a week for each business you run, up to three businesses
reallife_civic_policy_grants_up_say: A hundred and fifty dollars a week to every small business, for up to three premises. The big chains do not need it and will not get more than anyone else.
reallife_civic_policy_grants_down_fx: a licence fee of $60 a week for each business you run, up to three businesses
reallife_civic_policy_grants_down_say: Sixty dollars a week for a licence to trade, for each business up to three. Nobody likes a fee. Everybody likes a city that works.
reallife_civic_policy_rent_up_fx: 6% on top of every rent you pay, billed weekly; if you let property, 4% more rent comes in
reallife_civic_policy_rent_up_say: Buildings get built when building pays. I will lift the rent rules. Rents will rise by around six per cent.
reallife_civic_policy_rent_down_fx: 6% of every rent you pay comes back to you weekly; if you let property, 4% less rent comes in
reallife_civic_policy_rent_down_say: Six per cent off every rent in the city, by rule. Landlords will tell you the sky is falling. They said that last time.
reallife_civic_policy_parking_up_fx: street parking costs 50% more; each parking ticket costs $60 more
reallife_civic_policy_parking_up_say: The kerb is the most valuable land we own and we give it away. Meters up by half, tickets up by sixty dollars.
reallife_civic_policy_parking_down_fx: street parking costs 40% less; each parking ticket costs $40 less
reallife_civic_policy_parking_down_say: Customers arrive by car whether we approve or not. Meters down by forty per cent, forty dollars off a ticket. Shops need the kerb more than the treasury does.
reallife_civic_policy_transit_up_fx: each subway ride costs $1 more; buses run about 30% more often (where the mod runs buses)
reallife_civic_policy_transit_up_say: A bus every few minutes instead of whenever. To pay for it the subway fare goes up a dollar a ride. I would rather pay for a service than save on a timetable nobody believes.
reallife_civic_policy_transit_down_fx: each subway ride costs $1 less; buses run about 25% less often (where the mod runs buses)
reallife_civic_policy_transit_down_say: A dollar off every subway ride. To pay for it some buses come off the quietest routes. Most people will wait two minutes longer and keep the dollar.
reallife_civic_policy_cleaning_up_fx: street sweepers two and a half times as common, a small lift to your mood; the city levy rises by $30 a week
reallife_civic_policy_cleaning_up_say: Street sweepers two and a half times as common, and a city that feels cared for. Thirty dollars a week on the levy. Ask anyone who has visited a clean city whether it was worth it.
reallife_civic_policy_cleaning_down_fx: street sweepers rare, litter weighs on your mood; $25 a week comes back on the city levy
reallife_civic_policy_cleaning_down_say: We sweep streets that are already clean. I will cut the rounds and give you twenty-five dollars a week. It will be grubbier. You will have the money.
reallife_civic_policy_night_up_fx: street crime up about 10%; opening hours do not change
reallife_civic_policy_night_up_say: A proper city does not go to bed at ten. I will have the police ease off the late streets. There will be a little more trouble after dark and a great deal more life.
reallife_civic_policy_night_down_fx: street crime down about 8%; opening hours do not change
reallife_civic_policy_night_down_say: Nothing good happens in a doorway at three in the morning. I will put the police on the late streets and keep them there. People who live above the bars have waited a long time to hear that.
reallife_civic_policy_permits_up_fx: construction sites work 35% faster and until 19:00; noise complaints are noted and nothing more
reallife_civic_policy_permits_up_say: A permit in days, not seasons, and sites allowed to work until seven. Roadworks that take a month will take three weeks. It will be louder while it lasts, and it will last less long.
reallife_civic_policy_permits_down_fx: construction sites work 25% slower and only 08:00 to 16:00; a noise complaint always brings quiet hours
reallife_civic_policy_permits_down_say: Nobody should be woken by a jackhammer at seven. Sites work eight to four, and one complaint brings an inspector. Yes, the works take longer. You will sleep through more of them.
reallife_civic_policy_events_up_fx: street events about 50% more often, a small lift to your mood; the city levy rises by $40 a week
reallife_civic_policy_events_up_say: Markets, parades, music in the squares: half as many again. Forty dollars a week on the levy buys a city people cross the river to visit.
reallife_civic_policy_events_down_fx: street events about half as often; $30 a week comes back on the city levy
reallife_civic_policy_events_down_say: A parade is a fine thing and a closed street is a closed street. Half the events, thirty dollars a week back. Celebrate at home; it is cheaper.
reallife_civic_policy_wages_up_fx: a floor of $16 an hour: for anyone you pay less you are billed the difference for their rota hours, weekly
reallife_civic_policy_wages_up_say: Sixteen dollars an hour, at least, for anyone you employ. If your business only works by paying less than that, we should talk about your business.
reallife_civic_policy_wages_down_fx: the city pays 5% of your weekly wage bill back to you
reallife_civic_policy_wages_down_say: Hire somebody and the city pays a twentieth of their wage. It is the cheapest job programme there is, and it leaves the hiring to people who know how.

reallife_civic_site_rain: Hours lost to rain so far: {hours}.
reallife_civic_site_halted: Work is stopped by order of the inspector.
reallife_civic_site_quiet: Under quiet hours after a complaint: working 09:00 to 15:00 only.

reallife_civic_site_gone: That site has been handed over; there is nothing there any more.
reallife_civic_notice_bye: You leave the notice board to the pigeons.
reallife_civic_site_starts_near: Building works are starting next door to you: {project} at {address}. Days expected: about {days}. Expect noise and dust in working hours. Details and complaints through City Hall's line.
reallife_civic_site_done_near: The works next door to you are finished: {project} at {address} has been handed over and the street cleared.
reallife_civic_complain_offer: File a noise complaint about this site? The first complaint is put on file; a second brings an inspector, who puts the site on quiet hours (09:00 to 15:00) for three days. The works take longer for it.
reallife_civic_complain_offer_fast: File a noise complaint about this site? Under the fast-track permits policy in force, complaints are noted and nothing more is done.
reallife_civic_complain_offer_strict: File a noise complaint about this site? Under the strict permits policy in force, one complaint puts the site on quiet hours (09:00 to 15:00) for three days.
reallife_civic_complaint_logged: Your complaint is on file. One more about this site and an inspector comes out.
reallife_civic_complaint_upheld: Complaint upheld: the site is on quiet hours, 09:00 to 15:00, for the next three days.
reallife_civic_complaint_already: This site is already on quiet hours after a complaint. Yours has been added to the file.
reallife_civic_complaint_noted: Your complaint is noted. Under the current permits policy no action follows.
reallife_civic_unsafe_offer: Report this site as unsafe? An inspector will look at it: missing cones or netting, a barrier left flat, an open cover with nothing round it. If you are right the site is stopped for a working day and put right.
reallife_civic_unsafe_right: The inspector agreed with you: the site is stopped until it is made safe, and the contractor has been written to. Thank you for saying something.
reallife_civic_unsafe_wrong: The inspector looked the site over and found it in order. Thank you for the call all the same.
reallife_civic_unsafe_already: You have already reported this site; the inspector has been.
reallife_civic_favour_offer: Call in a fast-track permit for this site? It will then work half as fast again until it is done. You are owed {favours}. The risk, as you were told when you donated: {odds} times in a hundred this becomes a "pay to play" story in the paper.
reallife_civic_favour_done: Done, quietly. The permit office has moved this site to the top of the pile.
reallife_civic_favour_story: The permit went through, and so did a reporter's question about why. It is in the paper. The mayor's approval has taken a knock and so has your day.
reallife_civic_labour_offer: The foreman could use a pair of hands today. Take a day's labouring on this site?
reallife_civic_labour_go: Your hard hat is on the hook by the gate. Get yourself over there.
reallife_civic_labour_no: The foreman has nothing for you right now.

reallife_civic_refit_ordered: Agreed: {amount} paid. The hoarding goes up at {address}; follow the work on City Hall's line or on the notice outside.
reallife_civic_refit_done: The hoarding is down at {address}: your shopfront has been refitted.
reallife_civic_refit_none: You have no shop with a door on the street to refit. Once you run a business, its frontage can be done up from here.
reallife_civic_refit_busy: A refit of yours is already under way. One frontage at a time.
reallife_civic_refit_recent: Your frontage was refitted within the last four weeks. The paint is barely dry.
reallife_civic_refit_broke: You do not have the money for that bid.

reallife_text_family_welcome: Call to see your household, what is coming up, your memories and the family budget, and to make the family's decisions.
reallife_text_partner_welcome: Nobody here yet. Call when you would like a friend to introduce you to someone.
reallife_text_inlaws_welcome: Hello dear! It's us. We are so happy about the two of you. Call any time, we mean it.
reallife_happinessmodifier_broken_night: Up in the night with the baby
reallife_transaction_family_contribution: Partner's share of rent and bills

reallife_family_no_fault: Something went wrong (see Player.log). Nothing was lost: try again.
reallife_family_no_partner_social: This needs a partner, and your relationships are kept in People: start seeing someone there first.
reallife_family_no_not_engaged: You are not engaged. A ring and the right moment come first.
reallife_family_no_home: You need a home of your own first: rent a flat.
reallife_family_no_room: Your home is too small for the household: it needs 30 square metres for two and 15 more for each child.
reallife_family_no_not_yet: {name}: I love that you asked. Let's give it a little longer first. Soon.
reallife_family_no_children: There are no children in the family yet.
reallife_family_no_children_off: Children are switched off on the options page.
reallife_family_no_three: Three children is a full house.
reallife_family_no_baby: A pushchair walk needs a child under three. (For a test: press the pregnancy test button until the baby is born.)
reallife_family_no_away: The children are at their other parent's this weekend.
reallife_family_no_pushchair: You have no pushchair yet. A gift shop or a clothing shop sells one.
reallife_family_no_walk_indoors: A walk starts out of doors, on foot. Step outside first.
reallife_family_no_prop: The pushchair could not be brought out just now. Try again in a moment.
reallife_family_no_ring: You have no ring. A jeweller sells them.
reallife_family_no_propose_again: {name} asked for a little time. Give it a week before you ask again.
reallife_family_no_propose_indoors: Not in here. Ask at home while {name} is in, or out of doors where {name} can walk up to you.
reallife_family_no_room_here: There is no clear pavement right here for {name} to stand on. Try a few steps further on.
reallife_family_no_way_in: {name} cannot get to you here. Try another spot.
reallife_family_no_room_wedding: There is not enough clear pavement here to set out a wedding. Move to a wider, emptier stretch nearby and try again.
reallife_family_no_room_wedding_small: Still no room here to set anything out. Press again and it will be a small standing ceremony, told rather than shown.
reallife_family_menu_nothing: There is nothing to decide just now.
reallife_family_menu_off: Family life is switched off on the options page.
reallife_family_greet_morning_1: {name}: Morning! There is coffee in the pot if you are quick.
reallife_family_greet_morning_2: {name}: You are up. I was about to send a search party.
reallife_family_greet_day_1: {name}: Hey! I didn't expect you home in the middle of the day.
reallife_family_greet_day_2: {name}: There you are. How is it going out there?
reallife_family_greet_day_3: {name}: Oh good, it's you. I thought it was the landlord.
reallife_family_greet_day_4: {name}: Hi! Stay for five minutes, at least.
reallife_family_greet_evening_1: {name}: You are home! Come and tell me about your day.
reallife_family_greet_evening_2: {name}: Hey you. Shoes off, it is the evening now.
reallife_family_greet_evening_3: {name}: There you are. I saved you some.
reallife_family_greet_evening_4: {name}: Perfect timing. I was just thinking about you.
reallife_family_greet_late_1: {name}: Look at the time. I waited up.
reallife_family_greet_late_2: {name}: There you are. Long one today?
reallife_family_greet_late_3: {name}: Shh, come in. I was getting worried.
reallife_family_greet_low_1: {name}: Oh, come here. You look done in.
reallife_family_greet_low_2: {name}: Hey. Sit down. Whatever it is, it can wait until you have eaten.
reallife_family_greet_low_3: {name}: That face. Rough day? I am right here.
reallife_family_home_asleep: {name} is asleep in bed. Keep it down.
reallife_family_home_leaving_work: {name}: Right, off to work. See you tonight!
reallife_family_home_leaving_out: {name}: I am heading out for a bit. Back later!
reallife_family_moved_in: {name} has moved in. The place feels different already.
reallife_family_move_in_yes: {name}: Yes! Yes. I will start packing tonight.
reallife_family_new_home_done: {name}: So this is home now. I like it. Which side of the bed is mine?
reallife_family_watch_home: {name}: I will get the blanket. You pick.
reallife_family_cook_1: You chop, {name} stirs, and somehow it turns into dinner. It is good, too.
reallife_family_cook_2: {name} insists on the family recipe and will not say what is in it. You eat two helpings.
reallife_family_cook_3: The sauce catches, the smoke alarm sings, and you eat it anyway, laughing.
reallife_family_cook_4: A proper meal, cooked side by side, with the radio on. The best part of the day.
reallife_family_watch_1: Two episodes turn into four. {name} falls asleep on your shoulder before the end.
reallife_family_watch_2: {name} guesses the ending in the first ten minutes and is unbearable about it.
reallife_family_watch_3: A film neither of you chose and both of you loved. A quiet, good evening.
reallife_family_watch_4: You talk through most of it. Neither of you could say what it was about.
reallife_family_date_leisure: {name}: It's a date. See you there.
reallife_family_date_no_place: {name}: I can't think of anywhere to eat near here. Let's cook at home instead.
reallife_family_date_set: {name}: Dinner at {place}, {day}. I will meet you at the door. ({amount} for two.)
reallife_family_dinner_1: A long dinner with {name}. You were the last table to leave.
reallife_family_dinner_2: {name} ordered for both of you and got it exactly right.
reallife_family_dinner_3: You and {name} talked about everything and nothing. The bill was worth it.
reallife_family_dinner_4: {name} stole half your dessert and you let it happen. A good night.
reallife_family_dinner_5: Candles, a corner table, {name} laughing at your worst joke. More of this.
reallife_family_stoodup_1: I waited an hour at the door. I felt a bit of a fool, to be honest. Call me.
reallife_family_stoodup_2: So that was dinner for one. I know you are busy. I just wish you had said.
reallife_family_stoodup_3: You didn't come. I am not angry, I am sad, which is worse. Talk to me.
reallife_family_neglect_1: Hey stranger. I feel like I only see you in passing these days. Dinner soon?
reallife_family_neglect_2: I miss you. That's all. That's the message.
reallife_family_neglect_3: Is everything all right with us? We have not really talked in days.
reallife_family_chore_1: {name}: The bins are overflowing. Could you take them down before they walk out by themselves?
reallife_family_chore_2: {name}: I cooked, so by ancient law the dishes are yours. Deal?
reallife_family_chore_3: {name}: The bathroom light has gone again. Could you change the bulb? I can't reach.
reallife_family_chore_4: {name}: There is a mountain of laundry and I am already late. Could you put a wash on?
reallife_family_chore_5: {name}: We are out of milk, bread and patience. Could you run to the shop?
reallife_family_chore_6: {name}: The shelf I asked about last week is still leaning against the wall. Today?
reallife_family_chore_thanks_1: {name}: Thank you. Really. It is the little things.
reallife_family_chore_thanks_2: {name}: My hero. I will remember this at dessert.
reallife_family_chore_thanks_3: {name}: Done already? I could get used to this.
reallife_family_chore_sigh_1: {name}: Fine. I will do it myself.
reallife_family_chore_sigh_2: {name}: All right. Later, then. (It will not be later.)
reallife_family_sickcare_1: {name} made soup, found the good blanket and took your phone away. You feel a little better already.
reallife_family_sickcare_2: {name} sat up with you, tea and all. Being ill is easier with somebody there.
reallife_family_sickcare_3: {name}: Bed. Now. I have called in for you. No arguing.
reallife_family_encourage_1: {name}: Bad day? Come here. Tomorrow is a different one, I promise.
reallife_family_encourage_2: {name}: You built all this from nothing. One rotten day does not undo that.
reallife_family_encourage_3: {name} listens to the whole story, start to finish, and somehow it weighs less afterwards.
reallife_family_encourage_4: {name}: I am proud of you. I don't say it enough. Now eat something.
reallife_family_encourage_5: {name} runs you a bath and takes your phone hostage. You needed that.
reallife_family_baby_sound_1: {child} is gurgling away in the cot.
reallife_family_baby_sound_2: A small, determined cry from the cot: {child} is awake.
reallife_family_baby_sound_3: A squeal from the cot: {child} has found their own feet again.
reallife_family_baby_sound_4: Hiccups from the cot, each one followed by a surprised squeak from {child}.
reallife_family_baby_sound_5: {child} is babbling a long and serious story to the ceiling.
reallife_family_objective_aisle: Walk up the aisle and stand beside {name}
reallife_family_objective_walk: Pushchair walk with {child}: about {n} m to go
reallife_family_errand_birth: It's time! Get to the hospital: {place}
reallife_family_errand_adopt_meet: Meet your child at the agency: {place}
reallife_family_errand_school_play: The school play, with {child} in it: {place}
reallife_family_prompt_birth: {key}: go in, the baby is coming
reallife_family_prompt_adopt_meet: {key}: go in and meet your child
reallife_family_prompt_school_play: {key}: go in to the school play
reallife_family_prompt_planner: {key}: plan your wedding with the agency
reallife_family_prompt_walk_end: {key}: end the walk and fold the pushchair away
reallife_family_todo_cot: To buy: a cot (a furniture store)
reallife_family_todo_pushchair: To buy: a pushchair (a gift shop or a clothing shop)
reallife_family_todo_flowers: To order: the wedding flowers (a florist)
reallife_family_ring_2: a gold ring with a single stone
reallife_family_ring_4: a designer ring with a stone that catches every light in the room
reallife_family_rings_offer: Jeweller: For a proposal? Then have a look at this: {text}, {amount}.
reallife_family_rings_offer_again: Jeweller: You have a ring already, but if you would rather have this one: {text}, {amount}.
reallife_family_rings_have: Jeweller: That is the very one you bought: {text}. A fine choice. Shall I show you another?
reallife_family_rings_already: Jeweller: You own that one already. It suits the occasion, if I may say so.
reallife_family_rings_bought: Jeweller: Wonderful. Boxed and ready: {text}. Choose your moment well: an evening, a dry sky, the end of a good night out. Ask {name} to come to you from the Family contact, wherever you choose, or ask at home.
reallife_family_propose_coming: {name} is on the way to you. Wait here.
reallife_family_propose_called: {name}: You sound strange. Good strange. Stay where you are, I am coming to you.
reallife_family_propose_another_time: The moment has passed. Another time.
reallife_family_propose_waited: {name}: You wanted to tell me something? ...Another time, then. I have to run.
reallife_family_propose_ask_2: You: I had a speech. I have forgotten all of it. {name}, marry me?
reallife_family_propose_ask_3: You: {name}. Every good day I have had lately has you in it. Will you marry me?
reallife_family_propose_yes_1: {name}: Yes. Yes! Of course yes. Get up, come here.
reallife_family_propose_yes_2: {name}: I was starting to think I would have to ask you myself. Yes!
reallife_family_propose_yes_3: {name} cannot speak, nods a great many times, and then manages: Yes.
reallife_family_propose_yes_4: {name}: Yes. A thousand times. Put it on me before I wake up.
reallife_family_propose_no_too_soon: {name} takes your hands and pulls you up. It is too soon, love. Not no. Just not yet. Ask me again when we know each other's bad days.
reallife_family_propose_no_rough: {name}: Not like this. Not right after we have been at each other's throats. Let's be all right first, and then ask me again.
reallife_family_propose_no_moment: {name} smiles, a little sadly. I want to say yes on a day I will want to remember. Not here, not like this. Ask me again, somewhere that is ours, on a good evening.
reallife_family_propose_no_not_yet: {name}: I love you. I am not ready. Keep the ring, and ask me again soon. I think the answer is changing.
reallife_family_memory_engagement_off: The engagement to {name} was called off
reallife_family_venue_here: right here, where you are standing
reallife_family_plan_already: Your wedding is booked: {place}, {day}. To move it or call it off, ring Family.
reallife_family_plan_intro_agency: Planner: Congratulations to you and {name}! We see to everything: the venue, the invitations, the flowers, for 15% on top. Shall we begin?
reallife_family_plan_intro_self: Planning it yourselves: you and {name} choose the venue and the day now. The invitations will be yours to send, and flowers are ordered at a florist. Ready?
reallife_family_plan_outdoors_moved: You are no longer standing where an open-air wedding could be held. Stand on the spot you want, out of doors, and start again.
reallife_family_plan_no_venue: No venue could be found. Stand out of doors where you would like to hold it and start again.
reallife_family_plan_tier_simple: How big? Simple: the two of you, the family, a short ceremony. Costs as quoted.
reallife_family_plan_tier_classic: How big? Classic: an arch at the front, more guests, a proper party. 1.8 times the cost.
reallife_family_plan_tier_grand: How big? Grand: the arch, a runner down the aisle, a crowd, the works. 3.2 times the cost.
reallife_family_plan_flowers_agency: Flowers along the aisle? {amount}, before the size of the wedding is counted in. We order them for you.
reallife_family_plan_flowers_self: Flowers along the aisle? {amount}, before the size of the wedding is counted in. You will need to order them at a florist before the day.
reallife_family_plan_music: Music at the reception? {amount}, before the size of the wedding is counted in.
reallife_family_plan_catering: A caterer? {amount} a guest, before the size of the wedding is counted in.
reallife_family_plan_summary: So: {place}, {day}, about {n} guests. All together {amount}: {text} now as a deposit, the rest on the day.
reallife_family_plan_booked_agency: Planner: Done! {place}, {day}. The invitations go out today. Be at the venue between 11:00 and 20:00 and we will do the rest.
reallife_family_plan_booked_self: Booked: {place}, {day}. Send the invitations from the Family contact, and be at the venue between 11:00 and 20:00.
reallife_family_plan_booked_self_flowers: Booked: {place}, {day}. Send the invitations from the Family contact, order the flowers at a florist, and be at the venue between 11:00 and 20:00.
reallife_family_plan_invited: The invitations are sent: about {n} people, for {place}, {day}.
reallife_family_plan_flowers_ordered: Florist: Ordered for your wedding day. {amount}, on the day's bill.
reallife_family_plan_postpone_ask: Put the wedding back a week? The venue charges {amount} to move it.
reallife_family_plan_cancel_ask: Call the wedding off? The {amount} already paid is not returned. You would still be engaged.
reallife_family_plan_cancelled: The wedding is off. You and {name} are still engaged; plan again when you are both ready.
reallife_family_memory_wedding_off: The wedding with {name} was called off
reallife_family_coldfeet_mine: Tomorrow you marry {name}. Tonight your stomach is in knots. Is this right?
reallife_family_coldfeet_talked: You talked until late. {name} has the very same knots. You both feel better for saying so.
reallife_family_coldfeet_slept: You slept badly, and woke up sure.
reallife_family_coldfeet_theirs: Can we talk before the ceremony tomorrow? Nothing is wrong. I just need a minute with you first.
reallife_family_eve_message: Tomorrow! I can't sleep. See you at the front.
reallife_family_coldfeet_theirs_talk: {name} takes you aside, pale. I love you. I am just scared. What if we are rushing?
reallife_family_coldfeet_reassured: {name} breathes out, and laughs. All right. All right. Let's get married. (Begin the ceremony when you are ready.)
reallife_family_coldfeet_given_time: You hold their hands. There is no hurry. The wedding moves to {day}, at no charge, and {name} loves you the more for it.
reallife_family_wedding_missed_once: Where were you? I told everyone it was nerves. The venue can do {day}. Please be there.
reallife_family_wedding_missed_twice: Twice. I stood there twice. The venue has let the booking go. I need you to show me that you want this.
reallife_family_wedding_interrupted: The ceremony was interrupted. Everyone will wait: begin again when you are ready.
reallife_family_wedding_walked_off: You left your own ceremony. Everyone is waiting: come back and begin again while the day lasts.
reallife_family_officiant_welcome: Officiant: We are here today for {name} and for you. Who has the first words?
reallife_family_officiant_pronounce: Officiant: Then by the power this city gives me: you are married!
reallife_family_vow_body: {name} is looking at you. Everybody is. What do you say?
reallife_family_vow_heart_1: You: {name}, I came to this city for money. I am staying for you.
reallife_family_vow_heart_2: You: I promise you my good days and my bad ones, {name}, and to come home at the end of both.
reallife_family_vow_heart_3: You: Whatever I build, {name}, I build it with you, or it is not worth building.
reallife_family_vow_funny_1: You: {name}, I promise to love you, honour you, and let you believe you are right about the dishwasher.
reallife_family_vow_funny_2: You: I vow never to check my phone at dinner, {name}. Starting next week.
reallife_family_vow_funny_3: You: {name}, you are the best decision I ever made, and I have made some terrible ones.
reallife_family_vow_theirs_1: {name}: You make an enormous city feel like a small one. I am yours.
reallife_family_vow_theirs_2: {name}: I promise to believe in the next idea, and the one after that, and to tell you when to sleep.
reallife_family_vow_theirs_3: {name}: I was fine by myself. I am so much better with you. Yes, to all of it.
reallife_family_vow_theirs_4: {name}: I promise to laugh at your jokes. Most of them. Yes: all of it, always.
reallife_family_rings_exchanged: The rings: {text} for {name}, and a plain band for you.
reallife_family_reception_simple: A small party, and a happy one: a few toasts, a short speech from your mother, and {name} beside you the whole evening.
reallife_family_reception_classic: A proper wedding party: speeches that ran long, a first dance that almost went right, and {name} glowing through all of it.
reallife_family_reception_grand: The kind of wedding people talk about for years: a full room, a late night, and {name} lifted on to somebody's shoulders at one point.
reallife_family_reception_music: The band played until they were made to stop.
reallife_family_reception_no_music: There was no band, so somebody's phone and a borrowed speaker did the honours.
reallife_family_reception_catering: The food was so good that people asked for the caterer's card.
reallife_family_reception_no_catering: Everybody brought a dish, and somehow there were four potato salads.
reallife_family_reception_flowers: The flowers went home with the guests, an armful each.
reallife_family_reception_money: The day came to {amount} in all. Your {n} guests left gifts worth {text}.
reallife_family_honeymoon_body: {n} days away with {name}, somewhere warm, for {amount}. Your businesses run without you while you are gone.
reallife_family_honeymoon_later: The honeymoon can wait. You can ask again from the Family contact.
reallife_family_honeymoon_asking: {name}: A honeymoon? Let me think about it. Yes.
reallife_family_honeymoon_back: Back from the honeymoon with {name}: sunburnt, rested and very married.
reallife_family_mom_moved_in: Moved in together! Sweetheart, that is wonderful. Does {name} eat properly? Do you? I am sending recipes.
reallife_family_mom_engaged: ENGAGED! I had to sit down. Tell {name} they are family now, and that I will need measurements for the knitting.
reallife_family_mom_date_set: A date! I have told everyone. I have told the neighbours. I have told the man at the bakery. I am so happy for you both.
reallife_family_mom_invited_1: The invitation came: {place}, {day}. I have already chosen my hat. Nothing will keep me away.
reallife_family_mom_invited_2: {place}, {day}. I will be there early, sweetheart, in the front row, with tissues.
reallife_family_friend_invited: {place}, {day}? Try and stop me. Is there a free bar? Asking for me.
reallife_family_mom_married: My baby is MARRIED. It was a beautiful day and I cried through all of it. Look after each other. Love, Mom
reallife_family_mom_expecting: A GRANDCHILD! I am knitting already. Is {name} resting? Are you? Call me, call me, call me.
reallife_family_mom_adopting: Adopting! Oh, sweetheart. Some lucky child is going to have the best home in the city. I am so proud of you both.
reallife_family_mom_born: {child}! What a perfect name. I have put {amount} in your account for all the small things. Kiss that baby for me. Love, Grandma
reallife_family_mom_adopted: {child} is home! I can't wait to meet them. Here is {amount} for all the small things. Love, Grandma
reallife_family_mom_birthday: Happy birthday to my {child}! {n} already! Here is {amount} for a present. From Grandma, with love.
reallife_family_mom_arrest: ARRESTED? I am not angry. I am worried sick. Call your mother and tell me you are all right.
reallife_family_mom_separated: Oh, sweetheart. I am so sorry. Come home for a few days if you need to. No questions, just soup.
reallife_family_mom_reconciled: You two worked it out! I never said a word, but I was hoping. Give {name} a hug from me.
reallife_family_mom_divorced: It is done, then. You were brave to try, and brave to stop. I love you. Come for dinner.
reallife_family_mom_visit_1: Dropped by while you were out! Left a casserole in the fridge and tidied a little. Don't be cross. Love, Mom
reallife_family_mom_visit_2: Lovely to see you all on Sunday. I left something small on the kitchen table. Love, Mom
reallife_family_mom_visit_3: I was in the neighbourhood (I was not) and popped in. Your plants needed water. Love, Mom
reallife_family_inlaws_welcome: We always hoped it would be you. Welcome to the family, dear. Come for Sunday lunch, both of you.
reallife_family_inlaws_invited: We would not miss it for the world. Tell us what to bring. We are bringing something anyway.
reallife_family_inlaws_married: What a day. We could not have wished for a better match. Thank you for making our child so happy.
reallife_family_inlaws_expecting: A grandchild! We have been not-saying-anything for months. We are over the moon.
reallife_family_inlaws_grandchild: We are grandparents! Send pictures. Send more pictures. We can babysit any time, we mean any time.
reallife_family_inlaws_repaid: We have put the money back in your account, with our thanks. You are a good one.
reallife_family_child_no_room: {name}: I would love to. But where would we put a cot? We need a bigger place first.
reallife_family_child_not_now: {name}: Let's get ourselves right first. A child deserves a happy home, and we have been snappy with each other lately.
reallife_family_child_unsure: {name}: I don't know yet. Honestly. I am not saying never. Give me some time to think, and ask me again in a while.
reallife_family_child_yes_first: {name}: I have been thinking about it too. A family. Ours. Yes. How shall we do it?
reallife_family_child_yes_another: {name}: Another one? ...Yes. The house is not loud enough yet. How shall we do it?
reallife_family_child_who_carries: {name}: Then the next question is which of us carries. I am happy either way.
reallife_family_child_started_me: It took no time at all: you are expecting, due {day}. There are scans to go to, and a nursery to get ready: a cot, a pushchair, supplies. {name} has already started a list.
reallife_family_child_started_them: It took no time at all: {name} is expecting, due {day}. There are scans to go to together, and a nursery to get ready: a cot, a pushchair, supplies.
reallife_family_adopt_age_baby: The agency asks who you hope to welcome. A baby, a few months old? (The filing fee is {amount}.)
reallife_family_adopt_age_toddler: The agency asks who you hope to welcome. A toddler of about two? (The filing fee is {amount}.)
reallife_family_adopt_age_child: The agency asks who you hope to welcome. A child of about six, already at school? (The filing fee is {amount}.)
reallife_family_adopt_started: {name}: Then let's do it. The papers are filed in person: {place} is the nearest office, and the fee is {amount}. After that they visit our home, and then we wait for the call.
reallife_family_adopt_filed: The adoption papers are filed. A worker will visit your home {day}, between 10:00 and 19:00: be there.
reallife_family_adopt_visit_done: The adoption worker looked in every cupboard, asked a hundred questions and smiled at the end. You and {name} are approved. Now you wait for the call.
reallife_family_adopt_visit_moved: Adoption agency: We missed you at home. No harm done: our worker will come {day} instead, between 10:00 and 19:00.
reallife_family_adopt_matched: Adoption agency: We have a match. Come to our office {day}, between 09:00 and 18:00, to meet your child and take them home.
reallife_family_adopt_meet_moved: Adoption agency: We waited for you today. Come {day} instead, between 09:00 and 18:00. Somebody small is looking forward to it.
reallife_family_adopt_home: {child} is home: {text} old, wide-eyed, and holding your hand rather tightly. Welcome to the family.
reallife_family_adopt_wait_1: Adoption agency: Your file is with the panel. These things take the time they take; we will call.
reallife_family_adopt_wait_2: Adoption agency: No news yet, which is the usual news. You are near the top of the list.
reallife_family_adopt_wait_3: Adoption agency: Thank you for your patience. We have not forgotten you.
reallife_family_bought_cot: A cot for the nursery: {amount}. It stands at home while a child is under two.
reallife_family_bought_pushchair: A pushchair: {amount}. Walks are on, once there is somebody to push.
reallife_family_bought_supplies: Nappies, bottles, blankets and a great many small socks: {amount}.
reallife_family_nursery_ready: The nursery is ready. {name} stands in the doorway for a long minute, just looking at it.
reallife_family_expecting_1: It kicked. In the middle of a meeting. I nearly shouted.
reallife_family_expecting_2: Craving of the day: pickles and ice cream. Together. Do not judge me. Bring both.
reallife_family_expecting_3: I can't see my own feet any more. Are they still there? Please confirm.
reallife_family_expecting_4: I read that the baby can hear us now. So be nice about my singing.
reallife_family_expecting_5: Sorted the tiny clothes by size today and cried over a pair of socks. Hormones. Or the socks.
reallife_family_expecting_6: Name idea number forty-one. No, don't make that face. Just think about it.
reallife_family_birth_time: It's time! {name} is on the way to the hospital. Get there!
reallife_family_birth_time_me: It's time! The baby is coming. Get to the hospital!
reallife_family_birth_time_text: It's time. It's really time. I am going in now. COME.
reallife_family_passage_birth: A long night at the hospital
reallife_family_born: {child} is here: healthy, loud and perfect. You have three days at home together before the world wants you back.
reallife_family_birth_missed: You weren't there. {child} is here, and healthy, and beautiful, and I did it without you. Come home and meet your child.
reallife_family_name_body_girl: A girl. {name} looks at her, and then at you: {child}?
reallife_family_name_body_boy: A boy. {name} looks at him, and then at you: {child}?
reallife_family_scan_done_1: The first scan: a heartbeat, quick and steady, and a grainy picture for the fridge. {name} has not let go of your hand.
reallife_family_scan_done_2: The second scan: everything where it should be. You could see fingers. {name} counted them twice.
reallife_family_class_done: Birth class with {name}: breathing, bags to pack, and a doll that you held upside down. You both feel nearly ready.
reallife_family_appointment_missed: You missed the appointment. I went by myself. It was fine. I just wanted you there.
reallife_family_appointment_missed_me: You missed your appointment. The clinic has rebooked you without fuss.
reallife_family_checkup_due: The clinic wants to see {child} for a check-up tomorrow, between 09:00 and 18:00.
reallife_family_checkup_done: The check-up: {child}, {text}, is growing exactly as a child should. A sticker was awarded.
reallife_family_checkup_missed: You missed the check-up, so I took {child} myself. All fine. Next time, together?
reallife_family_night_1: 02:40. {child} is awake, and so, now, are you.
reallife_family_night_2: {child} wanted feeding at three, changing at four and company at five.
reallife_family_night_3: A night walked up and down the hall with {child} on your shoulder. Asleep at last, both of you, in the chair.
reallife_family_night_4: {child} slept for four whole hours in a row. You woke up twice to check.
reallife_family_memory_expecting: You and {name} found out you were expecting
reallife_family_memory_first_scan: The first scan, and a heartbeat
reallife_family_memory_first_sentence: {child} said a whole sentence, and it was a demand
reallife_family_memory_first_school_day: {child} had a first day at school
reallife_family_memory_first_walk: The first walk with {child} in the pushchair
reallife_family_school_body: {child} starts school. The public school is free and perfectly good. A private school costs {amount} a month and tends to mean better reports.
reallife_family_school_private_chosen: {child} is enrolled at the private school: {amount} a month, a quarter of it each week.
reallife_family_school_run_done_1: {child} ran in through the gates without looking back. You stood there a moment anyway.
reallife_family_school_run_done_2: Dropped at the gate with a lunch box and a wave. {child} told you three secrets on the way.
reallife_family_school_run_done_3: On time, bag packed, shoes on the right feet. {child} gave you a hug in front of everyone.
reallife_family_report_great: School report for {child}: 'A pleasure to teach. Bright, kind and curious.' Top marks nearly everywhere.
reallife_family_report_good: School report for {child}: 'Works well and is well liked.' Good marks, and a note about talking in class.
reallife_family_report_fair: School report for {child}: 'Capable, when the mind is on the work.' Middling marks. A little more time at home might help.
reallife_family_report_struggling: School report for {child}: 'Seems distracted and a little sad this term.' {child} could do with more of you.
reallife_family_drawing_1: A new drawing on the fridge from {child}: the whole family, with you much the tallest and holding a briefcase the size of a car.
reallife_family_drawing_2: {child} has drawn the flat. Every window has a face in it. One of them is a cat you do not own.
reallife_family_drawing_3: A drawing from {child}: a purple dog, labelled, in careful letters, NOT A DOG.
reallife_family_drawing_4: On the fridge: {child}'s picture of your shop, with a queue of customers reaching the sun.
reallife_family_drawing_5: {child} drew you at work. You are on the phone, and smiling, which {child} says is how you look when you think nobody sees.
reallife_family_drawing_6: A masterpiece from {child}: the city at night, mostly black crayon, with one yellow window. 'That one is us.'
reallife_family_drawing_7: {child} has drawn a rocket. You are flying it. Grandma is waving from the moon.
reallife_family_drawing_8: New on the fridge: a family portrait by {child}, everybody holding hands, everybody with the same enormous smile.
reallife_family_school_play_invite: The school play is {day}, 17:00 to 21:00, at the theatre. {child} has a part and has asked four times whether you are coming.
reallife_family_school_play_done_1: {child} was a tree. A very still, very serious tree, who waved at you once and then remembered not to.
reallife_family_school_play_done_2: {child} had one line, said it twice as loudly as anyone else, and bowed longest of all. You clapped until your hands hurt.
reallife_family_school_play_done_3: {child} forgot the words, made up better ones, and brought the house down.
reallife_family_school_play_missed: {child} looked for you in the audience all through the play. Next time, please be there.
reallife_family_parents_evening_invite: Parents' evening for {child} is {day}, 16:00 to 20:00, at the school.
reallife_family_parents_evening_great: The teacher had only good things to say about {child}, and seemed a little sorry to send them home each afternoon.
reallife_family_parents_evening_good: {child} is doing well: a few things to work on, and a teacher who clearly likes them.
reallife_family_parents_evening_fair: A careful talk with the teacher. {child} is finding it hard just now, and time with you would help more than anything.
reallife_family_parents_evening_missed: You missed parents' evening for {child}. The teacher has sent a note home instead.
reallife_family_birthday_body: {child} turns {n}! How do you mark the day?
reallife_family_birthday_where: A party for {child}, then. At home ({amount}) or out at a venue ({text})?
reallife_family_birthday_home_done: Balloons, a houseful of small guests and a cake that lasted ninety seconds. {child} says it was the best birthday ever.
reallife_family_birthday_venue_booked: The party for {child} is booked at a restaurant, {day}, between 11:00 and 20:00.
reallife_family_birthday_venue_done: A long table, paper hats and a waiter who sang. {child} fell asleep in the car home, still holding a balloon.
reallife_family_birthday_venue_missed: The party went ahead without you. {child} kept a slice of cake for you, and watched the door a good deal.
reallife_family_birthday_quiet: {child} is {n}! A cake, candles and a wish that is not to be told.
reallife_family_grown_fund_full: {child} is grown up, and off to college with every bill paid: the fund reached {amount}.
reallife_family_grown_fund_part: {child} is grown up and off to college. The fund of {amount} covers part of it; a weekend job covers the rest.
reallife_family_grown_fund_none: {child} is grown up and out in the world, paying their own way, the way you once did.
reallife_family_grown_call_1: {child} rang: all is well, the flat is tiny, and could you send the recipe for the thing you used to make?
reallife_family_grown_call_2: A message from {child}: 'Saw one of your shops today. Told everyone it was my family's. Love you.'
reallife_family_grown_call_3: {child} is coming home for the weekend, with washing.
reallife_family_custody_body: The children live with you. How often will they stay with {name}?
reallife_family_custody_away: The children are with {name} this weekend. The home is very quiet.
reallife_family_custody_home: The children are with you this weekend.
reallife_family_care_partner: your partner works short days to look after them
reallife_family_care_offer_you: Look after the little ones yourself? It costs no money, takes a good slice of your energy every day, and brings you closest to them.
reallife_family_care_offer_partner: Ask {name} to work short days and look after them? No fees, but {name} brings in half as much towards the rent.
reallife_family_care_offer_nursery: A nursery? {amount} a month for each child under five, a quarter of it each week. Your days are your own.
reallife_family_care_offer_nanny: A nanny? {amount} a month, a quarter of it each week, however many children. The nights are covered too.
reallife_family_pocket_set: Pocket money for {child}: {amount} a week from now on.
reallife_family_fund_added: Added. The college fund for {child} now stands at {amount}.
reallife_family_walk_start: Out for a walk with {child} in the pushchair. Wherever you like: a couple of hundred metres will do you both good.
reallife_family_walk_start_both: Out for a walk with {child} in the pushchair, and {name} is coming too.
reallife_family_walk_called: Shoes on, blanket, hat, the small rabbit that must come everywhere. Off you go.
reallife_family_walk_done: A good walk. {child} is fast asleep, one hand still holding the blanket.
reallife_family_walk_done_both: A good walk, the three of you. {child} is asleep, and {name} heads home.
reallife_family_walk_cut_short: The walk is cut short. The pushchair is folded away, and {child} does not mind.
reallife_family_walk_sight_1: {child} points at a pigeon with enormous seriousness.
reallife_family_walk_sight_2: {child} babbles at everyone you pass, and expects an answer.
reallife_family_walk_sight_3: {child} has kicked a sock off again. On it goes.
reallife_family_walk_sight_4: {child} is watching the traffic lights change as if it were the cinema.
reallife_family_walk_sight_5: A dog barks somewhere. {child} would like it noted that this is the best thing that has ever happened.
reallife_family_walk_sight_6: {child} has gone quiet, which means asleep, or planning something.
reallife_family_holiday_invite_1: Sweetheart, tomorrow is the {text} dinner. You will be with family, yes? Don't work through it. Love, Mom
reallife_family_holiday_invite_2: The {text} dinner is tomorrow! I have been cooking since Tuesday. Tell me you are not at the shop all day.
reallife_family_holiday_invite_3: Tomorrow: the {text} dinner. Family at the table, phones in a drawer. I mean it this year. Love, Mom
reallife_family_holiday_at_moms: It is the {text} dinner today, sweetheart, and there is a place set for you from midday. Ring Family when you are ready to come over.
reallife_family_holiday_going: On your way to Mom's for the {text} dinner. She will say you look thin.
reallife_family_holiday_done_1: The {text} dinner: too much food, the good plates, and the same three stories, better every year.
reallife_family_holiday_done_2: Everybody round one table for the {text} dinner. Somebody sang. Nobody was at work. A good day.
reallife_family_holiday_done_3: The {text} dinner ran late: seconds, thirds, and a board game that nearly ended in tears.
reallife_family_holiday_done_4: A full table for the {text} dinner, and a toast to the year so far.
reallife_family_holiday_missed_1: We kept a plate for you at the {text} dinner. It is in the fridge. We missed you, sweetheart.
reallife_family_holiday_missed_2: The {text} dinner was lovely, and one chair was empty. Next time, yes? Love, Mom
reallife_family_inlaws_hello: The in-laws: Hello, dear! How lovely. Is {name} looking after you? Are you looking after {name}?
reallife_family_inlaws_hello_favour: The in-laws: Hello, dear! We are so glad you rang. Did you see our message? We hate to ask.
reallife_family_inlaws_again: The in-laws: Twice in one day! We are flattered. Go on, go and live your life, dear.
reallife_family_inlaws_chat_1: Twenty minutes on the garden, the neighbours and what {name} was like at seven. You come away smiling.
reallife_family_inlaws_chat_2: They want to know everything about the business, and they understand about half of it, and they are proud of all of it.
reallife_family_inlaws_chat_3: A long story about a holiday in 1987, with a twist you did not see coming. Family.
reallife_family_inlaws_chat_4: They pass the phone back and forth and both talk at once. It is oddly comforting.
reallife_family_inlaws_advice_fine: The in-laws: Honestly, dear? You two seem happy. Keep eating dinner together. That is all we ever did right.
reallife_family_inlaws_advice_tense: The in-laws: Every couple has a hard season. Do the small things: the dishes, the bins, an evening out. And there is no shame in seeing a counsellor.
reallife_family_inlaws_advice_apart: The in-laws: We are not taking sides, dear. But ring {name}. Every day if you can. Doors close when nobody knocks.
reallife_family_inlaws_advice_plan: The in-laws: A wedding does not have to be grand, you know. Pick a day and a place and tell us where to stand.
reallife_family_inlaws_advice_expecting: The in-laws: Sleep now, while you can. And get the cot before the baby, not after. We learned that one the hard way.
reallife_family_inlaws_advice_children: The in-laws: They are small for such a short time, dear. Walk them to school when you can. The shop will still be there.
reallife_family_inlaws_ask_lift: Dear, we hate to ask: the car is in the garage and we need a lift across town this week. Could you? Ring us.
reallife_family_inlaws_ask_loan: Dear, this is awkward. The boiler has gone and we are a little short this month. Could you lend us some money, for a week? Ring us.
reallife_family_inlaws_ask_move: Dear, we are finally clearing the old flat, and the wardrobe will not carry itself. Could you spare an afternoon? Ring us.
reallife_family_inlaws_thanks_lift: You drove them across town and back, and heard the whole history of the street on the way. They are very grateful.
reallife_family_inlaws_thanks_loan: You lent them {amount}. They insist on paying it back in a week, and on feeding you in the meantime.
reallife_family_inlaws_thanks_move: An afternoon of boxes, stairs and one enormous wardrobe. Your back aches, and you are the favourite now.
reallife_family_kin_set: Next of kin: {text}. It is only a line on a form; it changes nothing else.
reallife_family_argue_1: {name}: You said you would be home by seven. It is past ten. I ate by myself, again.
reallife_family_argue_1_a: You say sorry and mean it. {name} softens. Just ring me next time. That's all I ask.
reallife_family_argue_1_b: You point out who pays for all this. {name} goes very quiet, and goes to bed without a word.
reallife_family_argue_2: {name}: I have told you about my day three times this week and you have not heard a word of it. Where do you go?
reallife_family_argue_2_a: You put the phone face down and listen, properly. It takes an hour. It is the best hour of the week.
reallife_family_argue_2_b: You say you are tired. {name} says: so am I. The rest of the evening is very polite.
reallife_family_argue_3: {name}: You forgot. You actually forgot what today was.
reallife_family_argue_3_a: The joke lands like a dropped plate. {name} does not laugh. Not this time.
reallife_family_argue_3_b: You tell the truth: the week ran away with you, and you hate that it did. {name} sighs, and lets you make it up.
reallife_family_argue_4: {name}: We agreed to talk about big purchases first. And then I see the bank statement.
reallife_family_argue_4_a: You say sorry. {name} nods. All right. Next time, we decide together.
reallife_family_argue_4_b: You walk {name} through the numbers, calmly. It was a fair call, and {name} comes round to it.
reallife_family_argue_5: {name}: Your mother rang me to ask if I was feeding you. I am not your housekeeper.
reallife_family_argue_5_a: You listen, and promise a word with Mom. {name} almost smiles. She means well. I know. Still.
reallife_family_argue_5_b: You defend your mother. It was the wrong moment for it, and you know so at once.
reallife_family_argue_6: {name}: There is a wet towel on the bed. There is always a wet towel on the bed.
reallife_family_argue_6_a: You wear the towel as a cape and beg forgiveness. {name} laughs in spite of everything.
reallife_family_argue_6_b: You shrug. It is a towel. {name} looks at you for a long moment. It is never about the towel.
reallife_family_argue_7: {name}: You always say sorry. You say it so quickly. I don't think you even hear what I am upset about.
