reallife_guide_home_about: Hygiene, stress and a tidy flat; cooking, sleep, fitness, illness and the doctor.
reallife_guide_home:
# What it adds
- Three light needs beside the game's own: hygiene, stress and how tidy your home is. A small strip on screen shows them at home, or when one runs low. A need left low costs you mood and, in time, your health.
- At home, click a cooker to open the cooking panel (the game says "Click to cook" when you point at one). In a home without a cooker, {key_interact} at a fridge opens it. It lists the dishes you can make right now from what is in this home's fridges: for each one the portions, the time, how much a portion fills and exactly which items it uses. Dishes that are one ingredient short are listed in grey with what is missing. Three sizes (normal, double, family size) make more portions where the fridges hold enough.
- Choose a dish and you walk to the cooker and cook it. The food leaves the fridge when the cooking starts, so stopping early wastes it. You eat one portion and the rest are put by as leftovers, which the same panel reheats later. Cooked food fills more than its ingredients eaten as they are, and a meal can burn, more often when you are stressed or exhausted.
- A home without a cooker can still make what needs no cooking: a salad, a fruit bowl, cheese and fruit. Clicking a fridge works as it always did, and anything in it can be eaten as it is.
- At a coffee machine at home, {key_interact} makes a coffee.
- Sleep has a quality: your bed, the hour you went to it and how long you slept decide the morning's mood, and sleep you skip is owed.
- Exercise and what you eat move your fitness over days, and slowly your build. The Wellbeing contact on the phone says how you are doing, and starts tidying, floor exercises and a run of six checkpoints out of doors.

# Being ill
- A cold, flu, food poisoning, a bad back or burnout can follow from how you live (out in the rain, no sleep, junk food, work without a break). The Wellbeing contact says what you have and what helps.
- Inside a hospital or clinic, {key_interact} offers a consultation for $80: a diagnosis, a prescription ($45) that halves what is left, and a sick note ($20 more) that covers a missed job shift for two days.

# Options
- "Easy needs" halves what wears a need down and every chance of illness. Each part (needs, the strip, routines, sleep, illness, fitness, the changing body, the run, the morning summary) has its own switch.
reallife_meta_title_law: Police stations, custody and your record
reallife_guide_law_about: A police station in every district, a holding cell if you are arrested, and a record that follows you.
reallife_guide_law:
# Police stations
- One building in each district is a police station with a name of its own: a sign, patrol cars at the kerb, officers at the door, a marker on the map. The Police Records Desk on your phone points you to the nearest.
- Close to the door, {key_interact} takes you in. The front desk takes a report of a crime or an accident, takes payment of fines, reads out your record, has your car brought from the pound and issues a police report ($15). Where a station cannot be entered, the front desk answers at the door.

# Arrest and custody
- Caught after fleeing a traffic stop or a crash, after a death on the road, or on the fifth 911 call about nothing in one day, you are arrested and held in a holding cell at the nearest police station: never longer than {law_most_hours} hours.
- In the cell you can sit it out, pay bail to walk at once (no bail after a death), or call a lawyer once for {law_lawyer_fee} (less if the public thinks well of you), which takes a third off what is left.
- After release your car is at the police pound: any front desk has it brought to the kerb for {law_impound_fee}. Where the station cannot be entered, the car is brought round at release for the same fee.
- If you got away after hurting someone, you are wanted. For seven days a front desk lets you hand yourself in for half the time and half the bail.
- The fines are charged once, by whoever stopped you. With the courts on, the hours in the cell count as time served and bail paid here is the bail of your case.

# Record and reputation
- Every ticket, every stay in a cell and every escape goes on your record. The police watch someone with a fresh record more closely; a clean spell ends that.
- The public notices what you do for others: from a good name on, passers-by say thanks.
- The Police Records Desk reads out both.
reallife_meta_title_transport: Buses, the subway and car ownership
reallife_guide_transport_about: Bus stops with buses to board, subway journeys that take time, and a car that needs looking after.
reallife_guide_transport:
# Buses and the subway
- Bus stops stand along up to six routes between the subway stations. At a stop a panel shows the route, the next bus and the stops ahead. While the bus stands at the stop, {key_interact} boards it: pick where to get off with 1 to 3 and pay the $2.75 fare. The ride is a fade to black while the time passes.
- With no bus at the stop, {key_interact} sits you on the bench if there is one, or else buys a day pass: $7.50 for every bus and subway journey until midnight.
- At a subway entrance a panel shows how often trains run, delays and the night closure (one station, 23:00 to 05:00). {key_interact} lists the stations: pick one, pay the game's $3 fare, and the wait and the trip pass as a fade. The City Transit contact tells you the state of the subway and sells the day pass.

# Your car
- A car you own wears: tyres and brakes lose grip and bite with distance, and a service falls due every so often. Once the service is overdue the car can break down.
- Stop in a filling station's repair bay and a panel lists what is due; {key_interact} has it all done.
- The Garage contact lists every car with its fuel, condition, tyres, brakes, service, insurance and registration. Roadside Assistance sends a mechanic or ten litres of fuel to your car, or tows it to a repair bay.
- Insurance runs {car_policy_days} days, renews itself and pays 80% of a repair bill above the first $100; each claim makes the next premium dearer. A car modified at the custom shop wears faster and costs more to insure.

# Options
- "Easy car ownership" switches fuel use, wear and breakdowns off.
reallife_guide_leisure_about: Chess, fishing, a night out, sights to see, clothes to buy, city sounds and photo mode.
reallife_guide_leisure:
# Things to do
- A prompt appears where something can be done; press {key_interact}. One thing at a time, never during a job or in a vehicle.
- Street chess: from 09:00 to 20:00 in dry weather a chess player sits at a table on the pavement (the City life option must be on). The stake is $10. Five positions, three moves to choose from, 22 seconds each: 7 points of 10 wins $10, 5 or 6 gets the stake back.
- Fishing: stand still at the water's edge near a pier, harbour or bridge, facing open water. Bait is $6 for five casts; the catch is sold by weight.
- A night out: in a nightclub, dance on the dance floor (press on the beat) and order at the bar: beer $8, cocktail $14, soft drink $4. From {leisure_tipsy_from} drinks you are tipsy (a beer counts as 0.8, a cocktail as 1.2): your car wanders, and driving like that is an offence. A drink wears off in 90 minutes.
- Sightseeing: stop at a landmark you have not seen and take its picture.
- Cinemas and theatres name the day's show as you go in. Watch it for 45 minutes or more and you get a verdict on it.
- At night, two people stand talking outside an open club, cinema or theatre near you.

# Clothes
- The mod's clothes and shoes are sold at the Real Life Overhaul rack in any clothing store: {key_interact} tries one on, and again buys it. What you do not buy comes off when you walk away. At home, a wardrobe or dresser holds what you own and three saved outfits.
- "Clothes must be bought" is kept per save: on for a new game, off for a save that was already going.

# Sound and photos
- Out of doors: birds by day, crickets at night, distant traffic and a crowd murmur near people, each with its own volume.
- {key_photo_mode} opens and leaves photo mode: the game pauses and the camera flies free within 150 m of you. The keys are listed on screen; Enter saves a picture.
reallife_meta_title_events: City events: fires, weather, street events
reallife_guide_events_about: Fires and the fire service, weather that matters, and markets, parades and fireworks in the street.
reallife_guide_events:
# Fires
- Now and then a car, a bin or a shopfront catches fire near you. The lane beside it is closed, a fire engine comes and the crew puts the fire out. Report it through 911 and the engine is sent at once.
- At a burning shopfront, {key_interact} at the door warns the people inside.
- A fire at a business of your own closes it for 2 to 10 hours and leaves a repair bill of up to $1,800. Both are smaller the sooner water is on the fire, and if you rang 911, warned the people inside or the business has good security. A save's only business is spared in its first ten days.

# Weather
- Rain, mist, thunderstorms and, on some summer and winter days, a heat wave, a cold snap or ice change your car's grip, the speed of traffic, how far the police see, and how often accidents and street crime happen. On foot out of doors, heat in the middle of the day and cold at any hour cost a little energy.
- Only the rain is drawn: heat, cold and ice are announced, not shown. The City Bulletin contact has the morning forecast.

# Street events
- Street markets, a farmers' market every Saturday, parades, protests, fun runs, film shoots and, twice a year, fireworks close a stretch of road near you for a few hours. Each is announced at 18:00 the day before and at 07:00 on the day, on screen and by the City Bulletin.
- With {key_interact} you can buy a snack at a stall for $6, sign the petition, cheer the runners or marchers, or watch a take. A thunderstorm calls the event off.

# One thing at a time
- One fire or street event runs at a time, and none starts while an accident, a crime, a police stop or a rally is going on.
reallife_meta_title_social: Social life and the City Ledger
reallife_guide_social_about: People you get to know, things to do together, and a morning paper about your city.
reallife_guide_social:
# People
- {social_cast} people can be in your life: Mom and your old friend Alex from the start; the others walk up to you in the street, after the gym, a job shift, a coffee at the cart or a good turn, or outside your home or shop. Press {key_interact} to talk and swap numbers.
- Each relationship moves through stages, from acquaintance to close friend or partner, by what you do: calls, outings kept, favours. Neglect cools it; standing somebody up is remembered.
- The People contact lists everyone and how things stand.

# Outings
- Plans are made by calling somebody: coffee, a meal, drinks, the cinema, a workout, a walk, a drive, a look round your business. Friends also ask for a lift or help moving.
- From an hour before, the place and time are on screen with a marker. Meet them outside and press {key_interact} to say hello. Over 20 minutes late costs trust; after 75 you have stood them up.
- At a business they go in at the door and the time inside passes as a fade: you do not see the inside and nobody sits down. A walk, a drive (they ride in the back) and carrying boxes happen in the street.

# The City Ledger
- Every morning after 06:00 a paper comes to the City Ledger contact: accidents, crime, arrests, court verdicts, fires, election results, your own business news.

# With the rest of the mod
- A close friend speaks for you in court and visits you in prison. Friends know of a record, and of a good name.
reallife_guide_travel_about: Hotels to stay in when you have no bed, and holidays booked at the travel agencies.
reallife_guide_travel:
# Hotels
- Eight places to stay: seven city hotels, from a hostel to luxury, and cottages in the Hamptons. Press {key_interact} at a hotel's door for reception: choose a room and the nights, and pay now or leave a deposit.
- With a room booked, the same key takes you up. The room is a panel of choices, not a place you walk around: sleep, shower, food, laundry, rest, extend, check out. Checkout is at 11:00.
- A night costs from $45 for a dorm bed to $900 for a corner suite, before district, weekend and season. Seven nights or more are cheaper, and eight nights earn a free one.
- The Trips contact shows your booking and points you to the nearest hotel.

# Holidays
- Press {key_interact} at the door of an open travel agency. After the first visit Getaways Travel also takes bookings by phone.
- Trips run from a Hamptons weekend ($520) to a Europe tour ($5,600), dearer or cheaper by season. First class, insurance and a companion cost extra. A ticket is good for 7 days.
- The Hamptons weekend is a real stay at the cottages: you travel there yourself. Every other trip is told in texts, one a day with a choice, while the days pass at home and your businesses run without you.
- You come back rested, with souvenirs for friends.
- You cannot leave town with a warrant out, a bail decision pending or a court date inside the trip.
- Your partner or a close friend can come along, which does the relationship good.
- Weeks of work without a break end in burnout, which lowers your happiness until you take a holiday or rest in a hotel room over a few days.
reallife_guide_careers_about: A steady job with an employer: a rota, reviews, promotion and a CV.
reallife_guide_careers:
# How it works
- Six employers have their offices at the help-wanted boards. Walk up to a board and press {key_interact} to speak to the boss, or call the Work contact and choose Apply for a job: it asks the same questions and gives the same job. Where the city has no board for an employer, the phone is the only way. Three take anyone, Fairway Markets and Hudson Parcel Co. want one good reference, Five Borough Cabs wants two. A reference letter from gig work counts as one.
- You pick a rota of fixed days. On a rota day, clock on at the office or through the Work contact, from two hours before the shift. The shift is the employer's kind of gig work, paid as the gig plus a basic hourly wage for up to four hours.
- More than an hour late costs a mark and an hour's basic pay, and a missed shift costs a mark. Three marks and you are dismissed, your reference is marked down and that employer will not take you back for 7 days.
- A doctor's sick note, or being ill, excuses the day: say "I'm not well today" to the boss or the Work contact.
- After every three shifts a review is due at the office. A good score brings a raise or the next rank, a poor one a mark. The top ranks work the dispatch desk or a shift in charge, both clocked on at the office.
- To leave, give notice and work two more shifts. Walking out marks your reference down.
- The Work contact shows your rota and your CV: where you have worked, your references, gig levels and any criminal record.
reallife_guide_business_about: Things that happen to the businesses you run: rivals, inspections, staff, suppliers, an audit.
reallife_guide_business: # What happens - Each morning at 09:00 there is a chance that one of your businesses gets an issue: 8% a day at frequency 1, about 30% at 10. Nothing comes up in the first seven days, or at a business you have had for less than seven. - The kinds: a rival's move, a protection racket, a health or fire-safety inspection, a licence renewal, staff trouble, supplier trouble, a complaint or praise that spreads, a tax audit, an opportunity. - Each issue has a deadline and up to four answers, each read out with its cost. The Business desk contact lists what is open; an issue left alone is settled by its default at the deadline. - One issue per business and two in all at a time. Effects are limited: customers down by 12% or up by 10% at most for a few days, a closure of 12 hours at most, a one-off cost set by what the business takes in a day. - If you are in the shop, the collector, an inspector or the police may walk in. - Switching the option off closes every issue and puts customer numbers and closures back. # Options - Each kind of issue has its own switch. "Easy business" leaves only the opportunities and praise.
reallife_guide_garage_about: Paint, parts and tuning for your cars in any repair bay, and bicycles and motorbikes.
reallife_guide_garage:
# The custom shop
- Drive a car you own into a repair bay, stop and press {key_garage}. Each choice shows on the car at once with its price.
- Pay keeps the build. Leave puts the car back as it came in.
- Performance parts cost something in use: faster wear of tyres and brakes and dearer insurance (both need car ownership switched on), less grip in the wet with some tyres, and a straight-through exhaust that the police can fine ($120).
- "My vehicles" lists every build, valued at {garage_resale} of what was spent. The price the game pays for the car does not change.

# Bicycles and motorbikes
- Press {key_garage} at a bike-share dock, a bicycle rack outside a supermarket or a motorbike stand outside a car dealership. All three are on the map.
- Hiring a bicycle costs $15. Return it to any dock by the end of the next day, or it is collected with a $25 late fee.
- Bicycles cost $350 and $900, motorbikes $7,500 and $18,000, a helmet $120. A rack or stand buys yours back at {garage_resale} of its price.
- Pedalling uses energy. Riding a motorbike without a helmet can be fined ($60).
- A motorbike needs a motorcycle licence (see Licences). The dealer will sell you one without, and says so. Riding it unlicensed is for the police to find: a fine, and the bike is towed.
- "My vehicles" shows where each two-wheeler stands. "Bring it here" works on foot and out of doors.
reallife_guide_justice_about: An arrest for something serious opens a case: bail, a lawyer, a hearing, a sentence.
reallife_guide_justice:
# A case
- Tickets stay tickets. An arrest, or a charge for something serious, opens a case with a court date two to four days ahead. Texts remind you; the Legal contact has your file.
- Bail: released on your promise, an amount returned when you appear, a bondsman for a tenth, or custody until the court sits. Bail already paid at a police station is the bail of your case.
- A lawyer tells you the odds, can move to dismiss weak charges and can bring a plea deal. The public defender and yourself are free. A law firm's fee depends on its rating and how serious the charge is: a quarter at once, the rest over six days.
- On the day, between 9:00 and 17:00, go to the courthouse and press {key_interact} at its sign. Miss it and a warrant is issued. Without a courthouse (or with that option off) the hearing is by video link from the Legal file.

# The hearing and the sentence
- Plead guilty (a quarter off the sentence), take a deal (40% off), or fight it: each round of a trial has a choice, and every term of the verdict is shown.
- A sentence can be a fine (never more than a share of your cash, at most {justice_fine_cap}), community service (up to {justice_community_cap} hours of litter picking), custody (at most {justice_custody_cap} hours; hours already spent in a cell count), prison (days, capped by the option), probation and a driving ban.
- What you paid at the roadside is taken off the fine. A fine too large to pay at once is taken in daily instalments.
- Prison passes a day at a time, with choices each morning. Good behaviour takes days off.

# Afterwards
- One appeal within {justice_appeal_days} days. The record is sealed after {justice_seal_days} clean days.
- Someone you crash into may sue: settle or contest the claim from the Legal file.
- "No prison" turns prison into custody and a larger fine.
reallife_guide_licences_about: A licence to drive: the school, the theory and driven tests, points and what a stop finds.
reallife_guide_licences:
# Getting a licence
- At a driving school desk (the learner plate outside a school building), between 7:00 and 20:00, press {key_interact}: the theory test ({lic_theory_fee}), a lesson ({lic_lesson_fee}) and the driven test ({lic_test_fee}) in the school's car.
- A commercial licence (vans and trucks) and a taxi endorsement build on the car licence. A bicycle and an electric scooter need none.
- A motorcycle licence is for motorbikes and stands on its own. Pass the theory test, then pay {lic_motorcycle_fee} at the desk for the ride assessment. The school has no motorbike to lend, so there is no driven test: the assessment is recorded as passed at the desk.
- A licence runs {lic_valid_days} days. Renewals, the taxi endorsement and your licence card can also be had by phone from the Licensing Office contact. If you already own a car or a motorbike when the rules first run, you are given that licence.

# Points
- Offences booked at a stop put points on your licence: a red light, speeding, driving on the pavement or against the traffic, driving after drinking, fleeing, leaving a crash, hurting somebody.
- Points count for 21 days. {lic_points_limit} points suspend every licence for {lic_suspension_days} days. A court can suspend it too: it is the same suspension.

# Driving without one
- Nobody knows until police stop you: after an offence, after a pursuit, or at a routine roadside check.
- A motorbike is checked the same way as a car. A licence for another class, such as a car licence on a motorbike, is the wrong class: a fine of {lic_wrong_class_fine}, and the vehicle is towed.
- No licence: a fine of {lic_no_licence_fine}, and the car is towed to a repair shop for $350. Suspended: a larger fine, the car towed, and a court case. The third time in 30 days (the second while suspended): arrest.

# Options
- "Driving needs a licence" off: everyone may drive anything, as in the base game.
reallife_guide_civic_about: A mayor and a council whose policies change the city, elections you can vote in, and building sites that progress over days.
reallife_guide_civic: # The city government - The city has a mayor, a council of five and {civic_levers} policy matters, from policing and traffic enforcement to rent, parking, transit and wages. Each is as the city came, or one step either way. - A policy in force changes the game: how many police are about, street crime and accidents, police fines, parking prices and tickets, the subway fare, how often buses and street events come, and a weekly city account that charges or pays you by your sales, rents and wages. - An election is held every 8 weeks. In the week before it there are posters, a canvasser with leaflets and rallies, and you can donate, endorse a candidate or hand out leaflets yourself. An endorsement from somebody with a criminal record is a scandal. - On election day, 07:00 to 20:00, vote at your district's polling place: stand at the white sign by its door and press {key_interact}. The winner's policies come in one a day. - Call the City Hall contact for the policies in force and what they cost or pay you, the candidates, the count, building sites and petitions. # Building sites - Roadworks, scaffolding, shop refits and utility works are in progress around the city, six at a time, and move through five stages over days. Crews work on weekdays and stop for rain. - A site near you is set out in the street, with a lane closed where it must be and a notice board you can read with {key_interact}. There, or through City Hall, you can complain about noise or report the site as unsafe. # Known limits - Posters, boards, scaffolding and the things on a site are plain shapes without artwork. - The night-life policy changes street crime only: bars and clubs keep the game's hours. The transit policy does not change bus fares. - You cannot stand for office. - Refitting your own shopfront through City Hall ($1,800 to $3,600) puts up a hoarding for some days and lifts your mood when it comes down; the shop's trade does not change.
reallife_map_places_shown: The mod's places on the map: bus stops, hotels, the courthouse, driving schools, bike hire, custom shops, help-wanted boards, polling places, construction sites, sights and what's on, each with markers and its own map filter (off hides all of them, police stations too)
reallife_fine_rest_court: That was all the police took at the roadside. The rest of the fine, {rest}, goes to court with the case.
reallife_fine_rest_waived: The roadside fine was held to what you could pay. The remaining {rest} is not collected.
reallife_transit_stop_coming: The bus is {metres} m away, about {minutes} min. It calls at:
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_none: DELAYED: no bus has been able to set out yet. It calls at:
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_light: DELAYED: the bus is held at a red light, {metres} m away.
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_traffic: DELAYED: the bus is held up in traffic, {metres} m away.
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_closure: DELAYED: the road is closed ahead of the bus, {metres} m away.
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_late: DELAYED: the bus is running late, {metres} m away.
reallife_transit_bus_skipped: The {route} bus you were waiting for is stuck and is not coming. The next one has been sent.
reallife_changes_001: First public release. In it: a camera behind your character and behind the car; cars that drive like their kind; traffic accidents with police, an ambulance and a cordon; street crime, police stops, police stations, custody, courts and prison; driving licences and a driving school; life events; jobs and careers; home life, health and a doctor; people to know, outings and a morning paper; a partner, a wedding and children; buses, the subway as a journey and car ownership; a custom shop, bicycles and motorbikes; hotels and holidays; fires, weather and street events; a city government and building sites; pressure on your businesses; leisure, clothes and photo mode; presets, this Guide, and tools for taking the mod out of a save.
reallife_guide_family_about: A partner who moves in, an engagement and a wedding, children and relatives, lived mostly through your phone.
reallife_guide_family: # A partner - With the social life on, your partner is someone from People: get close to them until they will go out with you. With it off, the Someone special contact has a friend introduce you to someone. Plan evenings out: dinner for two is {family_dinner}. - After {family_move_in_days} days, once you are close enough, ask them to move in from the Family contact. You need a rented flat of {family_sqm} square metres, plus {family_sqm_child} for each child. - At home, face them and press {key_interact} to talk. Every evening they pay a share of the rent. # Engagement and wedding - A jeweller sells four rings, {family_ring_least} to {family_ring_most}. After {family_propose_days} days together, propose at home or out of doors. - Plan the wedding from the Family contact, or at an event planning agency for {family_planner_fee} more. A venue is {family_venue_least} to {family_venue_most}, of which {family_deposit} is paid as a deposit. Be there between {family_wedding_from}:00 and {family_wedding_to}:00 on the day. A honeymoon is offered afterwards for {family_honeymoon}. If you put it off, ask for it from the Family contact within {family_honeymoon_days} days of the wedding. # Children - Once you live together, talk about children from the Family contact: a pregnancy, or an adoption ({family_adoption_fee} to file). Up to {family_children_most} children. - A scan is {family_scan} and the birth {family_birth}. A month of nursery is {family_nursery} for each child, a nanny {family_nanny}, a private school {family_school}. - A child ages a year every {family_year_weeks} in-game weeks (an option). # Hard times - Chores, arguments, time apart and divorce can be switched off. Counselling is {family_counselling} a session. A divorce settlement is {family_settlement} of your cash, at most {family_settlement_most}. - Your partner hears of every arrest, and of a prison sentence. They take it hard, but it never ends things by itself. While you are locked up, family life waits. # Not shown - Children are never seen as characters: a baby is a cot at home and a pushchair on walks, an older child is messages and appointments. - Your partner stands and walks at home but never sits or lies down.
reallife_guide_limits:
What is rough, partial or absent in version {version}.

# Little played
- This is the first public release. Courts and prison, the family, buses and two-wheelers have had little or no play from start to finish. If something there goes wrong, see 'Troubleshooting' for how to report it.

# Told, not shown
- The bus ride and the subway journey are a fade to black while time passes. There is no bus or train interior.
- A hotel is a prompt at its door and a panel of choices. Holidays other than the Hamptons weekend are told as messages, one a day.
- On an outing your companion goes in at the door and the screen fades while the time passes. Nobody sits at a table.
- A court hearing, prison and most of custody are pages of text with choices. A police station can be walked into only where its district has an empty unit for it; elsewhere the front desk answers at the door.
- Life events are text. The people in them do not appear.
- A cooked dish is never an item: you eat one portion when it is done, and leftovers are a count on the cooking panel, not something you can take out of the fridge.

# Family
- Children are never seen as characters: a baby is a cot at home and a pushchair on walks, an older child is messages and appointments.
- Your partner stands and walks at home and never sits or lies down. In a home with no clear floor they are not shown.
- A wedding is held on the pavement outside the venue, with five guests at most.

# The city
- One incident at a time: no crime starts while an accident, a fire or a street event is on.
- The bus is a minibus. A bus can be late, and a district the roads do not connect may have no route.
- Heat, cold, ice and mist change grip, traffic and energy but have no look of their own.
- The transit policy changes the subway fare but not bus fares, and the night-life policy does not change opening hours.
- Chess is five positions with a choice of moves, not a board you play on.
- Some actions use an animation of the game's own where the mod has none, and can look approximate.

# Vehicles
- The game's own panel still calls a bicycle or a motorbike an electric scooter.
- Parts from the custom shop do not raise what the game pays when you sell the car.
- A car added by another mod gets the performance of the nearest kind of car.

# Work
- A job, a shift or an activity in progress is not saved: loading a save starts without it.

# The mod as a whole
- Its models and animations are built for Windows.
- English only.
- Another camera mod cannot run together with this mod's cameras: switch one of them off.

reallife_transaction_gunshop_sale_label: Firearm sold back to the gun shop
reallife_transaction_family_contribution: Partner's share of rent and bills

reallife_guide_trouble_stutter:
# It stutters after a while
- Switch on 'Developer diagnostics' (options page, Diagnostics) and play until it stutters, for ten minutes at least. Once a minute of play the mod then writes a line to Player.log that begins 'Session': how long the frames took, how many took longer than 33 ms and 50 ms, how much memory is in use, and how many things of the mod's are in the city. A frame longer than 80 ms gets a line of its own (12 a minute at most), which says what the mod was doing at the time and where you were (on foot, driving or indoors).
- Send Player.log from that session. Say how long you had played when it began, your processor, graphics card and memory, and which other mods were on.
- To see what the mod adds, play the same save for the same time with the mod switched off under Mods, and say whether it still stutters.
reallife_changes_001_1: Smoother over a long session. The mod's people are now made ready while the city loads, where 0.1.0 made each one in the middle of play, and a passer-by keeps the same look for three outings or ten minutes before it changes. A bus stop is only solid to people on foot while you are on foot within 60 m of it, so driving past stops no longer costs anything; until you walk up, pedestrians may pass through its pole and panels. The first time a kind of worker is wanted, their site can take a few seconds longer to appear. For reports of stutter: with 'Developer diagnostics' on, the mod writes a line a minute to Player.log, and the Guide's Troubleshooting page says what to send. With the Workshop item and a local copy both switched on, the second one now does nothing where it used to run everything twice.
reallife_changes_001_2: The buttons on the options page now say what they do, where they used to read YOUR TEXT HERE, and every slider shows its value.
reallife_career_other_3: A job with another employer, or leaving the one you have?
reallife_test_lic_motorcycle: Test: grant / revoke the motorcycle licence
reallife_school_pitch_motorcycle: Motorcycle licence: after the theory test, the ride assessment. The school has no motorbike to lend, so you give your account of your riding at the desk and it is recorded as passed. Fee {amount}. {status}
reallife_school_done_motorcycle: Your riding is recorded as assessed and your motorcycle licence is issued. Wear the helmet.
reallife_lic_grandfather_motorcycle: Riding now needs a motorcycle licence. You already own a motorbike, so a motorcycle licence has been issued to you, valid for {days} days. The Licensing Office is in your phone contacts.
reallife_bike_bring_indoors: Your bike cannot be brought indoors. Go out on to the street, on foot, first.
reallife_bike_bring_paused: Your bike cannot be brought while a menu is open or time is being skipped.
reallife_bike_bring_off: Bicycles and motorbikes are switched off on the options page.

reallife_bike_bring_no_room: There is no clear ground in front of you to stand your bike on. Move to an open stretch of pavement.

reallife_guide_planner_about: An app on the phone that lists what you have to do, with reminders and your own notes.
reallife_guide_planner: # What it is - Planner is an app on your phone, beside the game's own. On the phone at the edge of the screen it is on the second page of the home screen: turn the page with the mouse wheel or the dots under the apps. In the phone's full menu it is in the row of apps at the top. - It lists what you have to do: rota shifts, court dates, licence dates, family appointments, plans with friends, a hotel checkout, city events, election day, deadlines at your businesses, the game's tax bill and your own notes. - A feature that is switched off adds nothing to it. # Reading it - Today shows today in time order. Upcoming shows the next {planner_days} days, each under its day. - The last column says where an entry stands: Next, Now, Done, Missed, Over, or Clash when two things you have to attend overlap. - Click a row for its details: when, where, what it costs or pays and what happens if you miss it. Set destination points the game's guide at the place, where the Planner knows it. - A number on the app's button counts what begins within two hours. It goes when you open the app. # Reminders - In an entry's details, choose a reminder: at the time, 1 hour before, or the evening before ({planner_evening}). It arrives as a notification; click it to open the entry. - A reminder is not sent for something that is done, over or gone. One that fell due while time was skipped arrives once, marked late. # Your own notes - New note: pick a title or type one, a day, an hour or all day, and a reminder. Inside a building, This building keeps its address with the note. - A note can be marked as done, edited and deleted. The Planner holds {planner_notes} notes. # Settings - Settings in the app chooses which kinds of entry are shown and the reminder a new note starts with. Times follow the game's own 12 or 24 hour option. - Notes, reminders and these settings are kept with the save.

reallife_changes_001_3: Planner: a new app on the phone that lists what you have to do, with reminders and your own notes. Cooking works: click the cooker at home and choose from the dishes your fridge can make. Coffee, tidying and exercises at home now start when you press Start. Every employer can be applied to by phone. A motorbike needs its own licence. Your partner is someone you have met, and hears when you are arrested. A honeymoon you turned down stays on offer for a while.
reallife_changes_001_4: Buses: nobody waits more than about 20 minutes of the game clock for a bus. A bus now waits at the stop for you instead of leaving after a few seconds, and a notice says when yours has pulled in and how to board. Bus stops are there when you arrive: after loading a save, a taxi ride or the subway, a stop near you is put up at once, and when driving they are put up from further away. A stop where a line ends says that no bus picks up there and where the nearest stop to board at is. The driving school takes its car back: when a lesson or test ends you are asked to step out, and the car can no longer be kept and driven. An officer posted at a junction stands watch and no longer waves at traffic that is following the lights. Boarding is offered beside the bus, not from across the street. Bicycles are faster: about 38 km/h for the city bicycle and 50 for the road bicycle.
